Male bosses get bonuses twice as big as those given to female colleagues who do the same job. Over their careers, men earn an extra 141,500 pounds compared to women.

According to the Chartered Management Institute (CMI), in 2012, men in UK management roles got average bonuses of 6,442 pounds, while women got 3,029 pounds.

Female directors received bonuses of 36,270 pounds over the last year, compared to 63,700 pounds for male directors.

These numbers show that pay in British businesses is not equal. People who fight for workplace equality want action taken.

Ann Francke, the CMI's chief executive, said it's time to make this issue a main topic in management discussions. She thinks management needs to change, with more flexibility, less focus on office time, and better transparency about performance and rewards. This could help organizations perform better and improve workers' well-being.

Some reasons for these differences might include women working in jobs where bonuses are less common. However, the bonus gap does seem to worsen Britain’s pay gap. The government says the pay gap is getting smaller, but full-time male employees still earn 10% more than women.

Maria Miller, the Minister for Women and Equalities, said the CMI figures show that women still earn less than men. While changes are happening and the pay gap is closing, more needs to be done for full equality in the workplace.

The government is helping by signing up 120 companies to the Think, Act, Report scheme, which encourages companies to hire, promote, and pay women fairly. They've also introduced shared parental leave and the right to ask for flexible working hours.

The CMI data shows that the pay gap between male and female bosses seems to be getting smaller since 2012. For a group of 17,000 managers, men's earnings grew faster than women's for the first time in five years. Men's earnings went up by 3.2%, while women's went up by 2.8%. At the highest levels, male directors' earnings rose by 5.3%, compared to just 1.1% for female directors.

Male bosses get bonuses twice as big as female bosses in the same jobs. Men get £141,500 more in bonuses over their careers than women. In 2012, men in UK management got an average bonus of £6,442, while women got £3,029. Female directors got £36,270 in bonuses over the last year, compared to £63,700 for male directors. This shows that pay is not equal in British businesses.

Ann Francke, who leads the Chartered Management Institute (CMI), thinks workplaces need to be more flexible and focus on good work instead of long hours. She also wants more openness about how bonuses are given. If these changes happen, organizations will perform better and workers will be happier.

Sometimes, women work in jobs where bonuses are less common. But the big difference in bonus sizes makes the pay gap worse. The government says the pay gap is getting smaller, but full-time male workers still earn 10% more than women.

Maria Miller, a government minister, says the CMI numbers show women still earn less than men for the same work. Changes are happening, but more needs to be done. The government is helping by encouraging companies to treat women fairly when hiring, promoting, and paying them. Some big companies like Tesco and BT are part of this effort.

The CMI numbers also show that the pay gap is getting smaller. The difference in average salaries between male and female bosses is now less than it was in 2012.

Maria is sitting on a black chair at a community center on a cold Tuesday afternoon. She is waiting for her number to be called. She is number 34.

When it's her turn, Maria picks up a brown paper bag filled with food like pasta, eggs, and cornflakes. She can also choose between butternut squash or carrots for vegetables.

Maria is the 34th person to receive food today at the East Hampton Food Pantry. The pantry is close to some of the most expensive houses in the world.

Every day during this season, over 400 families get their weekly food bags from the pantry. The food helps them survive the cold winter in Long Island.

The Hamptons are seaside towns near New York City. In summer, they are visited by rich and famous people. But after Labor Day, when the rich leave, the local community faces tough times. Most of these people are immigrants who live there all year.

Maria works long hours in the summer cleaning big houses but has no work in the winter. She laughs when asked if she has enough money. "There is no work in the winter," she says. Many people live in small rooms because they cannot pay rent.

Some families with five children live in basements and pay over $1,000 a month in rent. Many people cannot afford heating or medicine without help from the food pantry.

Vicki Littman runs the East Hampton Food Pantry. In 2015, they gave out more than 31,000 food bags. More people are coming to the pantry each year.

Littman says that visitors to the Hamptons are surprised to learn about the food pantries. They only see the glamorous side with big parties and fancy houses. But there are many people who work in landscaping, childcare, and restaurants who depend on summer income to survive the winter.

Housing costs are very high in the Hamptons. Homes often sell for over $25 million. Over half the houses are empty most of the year, causing the population to drop from 80,000 in August to 10,000 in winter.

Larry Cantwell, who grew up in East Hampton, says the area used to be a farming and fishing community. Now, it is hard for working-class people to find affordable housing.

Eddie Vallone, 22, says the Hamptons have drug problems and other issues. He cleans pools and does odd jobs in the summer. His earnings can last until November if he saves well, but he has no work until May or June.

Robert Mysłajek finds what he is looking for between two paw prints on a muddy mountain path—wolf droppings. He is happy because wolves are rarely seen, so finding their droppings is a good sign. There are now about 1,500 wolves in Poland, double the number from 15 years ago. Wolves, along with brown bears, lynxes, and wolverines, are Europe's last large predator carnivores. Scientists from Britain, Germany, and the Netherlands visit Poland to learn how the country has protected wolves.

In the droppings, bits of bone and hair show that the wolf ate a red deer. Mysłajek, a biologist at the University of Warsaw, can determine the wolf’s diet, gender, sexual habits, age, health, and family connections through DNA tests. These tests show that Polish wolves travel widely; one wolf even reached the Netherlands before being hit by a car. A typical Polish wolf pack needs about 250 square kilometers of territory.

Alex Entwisle, a 23-year-old student from the UK, wonders if wolves could be reintroduced to Scotland. He and other students look for droppings and paw prints in the Beskidy mountains of the Polish Carpathians. They discuss whether to bring wolves back to the British Isles for the first time since the 18th century.

Mysłajek visited the Scottish Highlands in 2015 to answer questions about the Polish experience. He notes that Scotland eats pork and has many sheep, unlike Poland. Both countries have many deer, and Poland also has about 200,000 wild boars that damage farmers' crops. Wolves help control these populations.

Wolves can travel up to 30 kilometers during a hunt. The Beskidy pack has eight or nine animals, including five cubs, two young wolves, and two adults. They are tracked using motion cameras and by following their tracks in the mud and snow. Only one adult pair in each pack has cubs each year, and all pack members care for the young.

Mysłajek doesn’t understand why wolves have a bad reputation, like in the fairy tale "Little Red Riding Hood." He believes scientific arguments, such as the need to regenerate forests and control wild animal populations, can help protect wolves. Natural predators balance ecosystems by reducing herbivore numbers, allowing trees to grow taller for birds to nest in.

Wolf hunting was banned in the western Carpathians in 1995 and throughout Poland in 1998. Now, wolf packs live in most of Poland’s major forests alongside humans. The Polish government compensates farmers for livestock killed by wolves and advises them to use electric fences. Mysłajek promotes traditional deterrents like red flags and Tatra Mountain Sheepdogs.

Poland’s wolves benefited from late infrastructure development. Before 1989, Poland had only one motorway. After joining the EU in 2004, major road projects began and considered wildlife. Attitudes towards wolves have changed. In 1975, there were fewer than 100 wolves in Poland, and hunting was encouraged by the authorities. However, wolves are now much safer, though not completely protected, as hunting still occurs in neighboring countries.

Mysłajek says the new Polish government, led by Environment Minister Jan Szyszko, a hunter, may not support wolves. There are 120,000 licensed hunters in Poland with significant influence. Promoting wolves as a tourist attraction is difficult because they avoid humans.

The British students leave the Polish Carpathians without seeing a wolf. Entwisle doubts Scotland can match Poland’s success due to roads, sheep, and potential conflicts with farmers. In Britain, people prefer watching predators on TV rather than having them nearby.

Robert Mysłajek stops. He sees something between two paw prints on a mountain path. "Droppings!" he says happily. Wolves are hard to see, so finding droppings is great.

There are now about 1,500 wolves in Poland. This number has doubled in 15 years. Scientists from Britain, Germany, and the Netherlands come to learn how Poland saved wolves.

From the droppings, Mysłajek can tell the wolf ate a red deer. He can also tell if the wolf is male or female, its age, health, and family.

DNA tests show Polish wolves travel far. One wolf went to the Netherlands before being hit by a car. A Polish wolf pack needs about 250 square kilometers of land. They can walk up to 30 kilometers while hunting.

Mysłajek follows a pack of eight or nine wolves. This year, they had five cubs, two young wolves, and two adults. He uses cameras and tracks in mud and snow to follow them. Only one pair in each group has babies each year. All wolves help care for the young.

Mysłajek, whose father was a shepherd, does not understand why wolves have a bad name. He thinks wolves are fascinating.

Wolves help the environment by controlling the number of herbivores, allowing trees to grow taller for birds to nest in. Hunting wolves was banned in the western Carpathian mountains in 1995 and in all of Poland in 1998. Now, wolf packs live in most of Poland's big forests near people.

The Polish government pays farmers when wolves kill their animals. Mysłajek tells farmers to use electric fences, small red flags, and Tatra Mountain Sheepdogs to protect their sheep.

Until recently, Poland didn't have many big roads, which helped wolves. After joining the EU in 2004, Poland started building more roads but now considers wild animals.

People's views on wolves have changed. In 1975, there were fewer than 100 wolves in Poland. Now, wolves are safer, but not completely. Some wolves go to nearby countries where hunting still happens.

Mysłajek says Poland's new government does not like wolves. The Environment Minister, Jan Szyszko, is a hunter. Hunters have a lot of influence in Poland. It's hard to protect wolves because most tourists want to see them, but wolves avoid humans.

Anthony McDowell from Liverpool was happy walking on Rios Copacabana beach towards a World Cup match. He said the place is beautiful and the people are friendly. He and his friends joined thousands of other supporters making the beach a fun area with national colors and cheers. They walked, talked about football, and waited for the next game to start on a big screen nearby.

Before the World Cup, there were protests and problems with transportation and stadiums. Now, supporters are enjoying themselves despite the difficulties. Brian Hill from Sunderland traveled over 20 hours to Rio and said it was worth it. His son, Andrew, had his sunglasses stolen right after sitting on the beach. Many bars did not have big screens for the games, but the atmosphere was still great.

Robin van Persie scored an amazing goal for the Netherlands against Spain. So far, there have been 28 goals in the first eight games, which is almost three times as many as in the same stage of the 2010 World Cup in South Africa. Latin American teams have done well.

The World Cup has faced some issues, such as late stadium deliveries and traffic problems. In Natal, bus drivers went on strike, and in Salvador, travel times were five times longer than usual. Protests have decreased since the opening day, and the main security issues now are petty theft and excited fans.

The World Cup experience varies greatly across Brazil. In São Paulo, the event had little impact, while in Manaus, a distant Amazonian city, there was a lot of excitement with decorated streets and flags on cars.

There are nice things about walking on Rio's Copacabana beach and watching a World Cup match. Anthony McDowell from Liverpool was happy. He said, "The place is lovely. The people are great. There’s a party feeling." He wished the England team would play better.

Anthony and his six friends joined many other fans making the beach fun. They danced, took photos, and drank. Most just walked and talked about soccer, waiting for the next game on a big screen.

Before the World Cup, there were protests, transport problems, and issues with the stadiums. Now, fans just want to have fun. Brian Hill, another England fan, said, "It’s great to be here."

Hill traveled over 20 hours to Rio. His son lost his sunglasses right after sitting on the beach. Many bars did not have big screens for games. But, fans loved the tournament's exciting start.

Fans enjoyed Robin van Persie's amazing goal for the Netherlands against Spain. There were 28 goals in the first eight games, much more than in the 2010 World Cup. Latin American teams did well, adding to the festive mood.

The World Cup had some problems, but not as many as expected. Stadiums were late and not fully done, but there were no big issues. Ticket sales were poor, with many empty seats. At the game between the Netherlands and Spain, only 48,000 of 51,900 seats were filled.

In the 12 host cities, traffic was worse than usual. In Natal, bus drivers went on strike. In Salvador, trips took five times longer than normal. Protests were less common after the first day. The main security issues were small thefts and excited fans.

The World Cup felt different in various cities. In São Paulo, it was hard to notice. But in Manaus, a faraway Amazon city, there was lots of excitement with decorations and flags everywhere.

In the UK, a girl born today can expect to live to about 82 years old, while a boy can expect to live to about 78 years old. In Andorra, they would live longer (85 and 79), and in the US, slightly shorter (81 and 76). In the Central African Republic, they would only live to around 49 and 44. Most places in the world see people living longer, except in some countries hit hard by HIV and violence. The good news is that fewer young children are dying now compared to 40 years ago. Deaths of children under five dropped by almost 60%, from 16.4 million in 1970 to 6.8 million in 2010.

The Institute of Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) in Seattle worked on a big project for five years with almost 500 researchers to look at how diseases affect people worldwide. This helps the world know how to keep children alive. The project used new ways to find out why people die, like asking families about deaths when there were no official records. One surprising finding was that more people die from malaria than thought before—about 1.2 million each year, mostly adults. Doctors usually think malaria mainly kills young children, but this study shows it also affects adults.

Some experts welcome the study, but others want more proof. The study found that the main causes of death are changing quickly. People are living longer and having fewer children, which means the world's average age is rising. For example, in Brazil, life expectancy increased from below 30 in 1970 to almost 64 in 2010. This change is so fast that many places cannot handle it.

Another change is that people are getting more non-communicable diseases like heart disease, stroke, diabetes, and cancer instead of just infectious diseases. This shift is happening in Latin America, the Middle East, and parts of Asia. The study also found that many people are living longer but not healthier. Common disabilities include mental health issues, arthritis, back pain, and substance abuse. These conditions are not improving over time.

In the UK, a girl born today will live to be about 82 years old, and a boy will live to be about 78. In Andorra, they would live longer: a girl to 85 and a boy to 79. In the US, they would live a bit shorter: 81 for girls and 76 for boys. In the Central African Republic, they would only live to about 49 and 44. Life expectancy is getting longer almost everywhere, except in places like Lesotho where there are problems with HIV and violence. Fewer babies and young kids are dying now compared to 40 years ago. Deaths of children under five dropped by almost 60%, from 16.4 million in 1970 to 6.8 million in 2010.

The Institute of Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) in Seattle did a big study on diseases around the world. Knowing how many children die and why can help save their lives. The IHME study uses a method called "verbal autopsy" when there are no death records. This means they ask families what happened. The study found that more adults than expected die from malaria each year, about 1.2 million. Doctors usually think malaria mostly kills young children, but the study shows it also kills many adults.

Some people agree with the study, but others are unsure. They want to check if the numbers are right. The study also found that the main causes of death are changing quickly. People are living longer and having fewer kids, so the world's average age is going up. In 10 years, it went from 26 to almost 30. In Latin America, life expectancy increased by 35 years in 40 years.

There are also more "lifestyle" diseases like heart disease, stroke, diabetes, and cancer. These diseases are replacing communicable diseases in many places. Another finding is that many people have disabilities, even though they are living longer. Mental health issues, arthritis, back pain, and drug abuse are common problems that do not go away over time.

In Rjukan's market square, there is a statue of Sam Eyde, the town's founder. He looks north towards a mountainside. Behind him, to the south, is a 1,800-meter peak named Gaustatoppen. Along the narrow Vestfjord valley, lies the town Eyde built for factory workers at the start of the last century. Eyde used the 100-meter Rjukanfossen waterfall to create electricity in what was then the world’s largest power plant.

However, Rjukan is in shadow for half the year because of the surrounding mountains. From late September to mid-March, the town is not bright during the day. To solve this, three large, solar-powered, computer-controlled mirrors were placed 450 meters above the town. These mirrors reflect sunlight onto the square.

Ingrid Sparbo, a retired secretary who has lived in Rjukan all her life, says the mirrors make her feel warm both physically and mentally. Many people enjoy the sunlight, including young mothers with children and elderly couples.

Eivind Toreid, an electrical engineer, thinks the light is like a spotlight, not real sunlight. Heidi Fieldheim, who heard about the project on the radio, says it brings much happiness.

Martin Andersen, a 40-year-old artist who moved to Rjukan in 2001, came up with the idea for the mirrors. He noticed that each day in September, they had to go further down the valley to find sunlight. By September 28th, the sun disappears from Rjukan's market square and doesn't return until March 12th.

A German company specializing in concentrated solar power installed the three 17-square-meter mirrors by helicopter. Some people were initially against the project, worried about costs. However, most now agree it works well.

Rjukan's mayor, Steinar Bergsland, sees the mirrors as a symbol of hope. Visitor numbers are up, and businesses are reporting increased earnings. A hi-tech company is considering moving to Rjukan due to the advanced technology and publicity. The town needed to find only 1 million kroner of the 5 million kroner total cost, with the rest coming from government grants and donations.

In Rjukan, Norway, there is a statue of Sam Eyde, who built the town. The statue faces north toward a mountain. Behind the statue, to the south, is a big mountain called Gaustatoppen. Rjukan is in a valley between mountains. Eyde made electricity using a 100-meter waterfall called Rjukanfossen. This was the largest power plant in the world at that time.

Rjukan is in the shadow for half the year. From late September to mid-March, the town does not get much sunlight. To solve this problem, three big mirrors were put on a mountain. These mirrors reflect sunlight onto the town's square.

People in Rjukan like the mirrors. Ingrid Sparbo, who lives there, says it warms her both physically and mentally. Mothers bring their children to play in the sun. An elderly couple enjoys the warmth. Shop worker Silje Johansen thinks it is "awesome."

Martin Andersen, an artist, came up with the idea for the mirrors. He wanted to bring sunlight to the town during winter. At first, some people did not like the idea. They thought the money should be spent on other things like better schools and roads. However, most people now enjoy the mirrors.

The town paid only 1 million krone of the 5 million krone cost. The rest came from the government and a local business. Rjukan's mayor, Steinar Bergsland, says the mirrors bring more visitors and help shops make more money. People are happy with the mirrors.

Four minutes to fitness might sound too good to be true, but Dr. Izumi Tabata's program proves it works. His plan involves 20 seconds of intense effort, followed by 10 seconds of rest, repeated eight times. When he first tested it on university students in the early 1990s, they were so tired they thought they were dying. But after six weeks, everyone was surprised by the results.

Dr. Tabata started his research after noticing that short bursts of very hard exercise helped Japan’s speed skating team as much as hours of moderate training. He tested this idea by comparing two groups of students. One group did an hour of steady exercise on a bike five times a week. The other group did a ten-minute warm-up, followed by four minutes of Tabata training four times a week, plus one 30-minute session of steady exercise with two minutes of Tabata.

After six weeks, the group using Tabata’s plan, who exercised for just 88 minutes a week, increased their anaerobic capacity by 28% and their VO2 max, which measures cardiovascular health and aerobic power, by 15%. The control group, who trained for five hours each week, improved their VO2 max by 10%, but their training had no effect on anaerobic capacity. Tabata also found that the heart size increased after three weeks of these exercises.

To do Tabata correctly, you must work very hard. It requires intense bursts on a stationary bike or rowing machine, explosive bodyweight exercises, or sprints. The effort should be at 170% of your VO2 max. If you feel okay afterward, you didn’t push hard enough. Beginners should start with a trainer to ensure they work at the right intensity.

Tabata’s program burns an extra 150 calories in the 12 hours after exercise, even when resting. While it helps people get fit or stay fit, it also burns fat. Currently, mainly serious athletes use this plan, but Tabata plans to release a DVD and train instructors to help more people learn the correct way to do it.

Richard Scrivener, a former rugby fitness coach, suggests that while Tabata offers clear benefits, it should be an addition to, not a replacement for, regular sports or training methods. For example, runners can reduce long runs and overall mileage by adding Tabata training, giving their joints a chance to rest and recover. Gym-goers can benefit by doing three strength sessions and three Tabata sessions a week. For others, gradually increasing the number of sessions is recommended, knowing that every session needs maximum effort.

Dr. Izumi Tabata made a workout plan that says you can get fit in just 4 minutes a day. His plan is 20 seconds of hard work, then 10 seconds of rest, repeated 8 times. That's only 4 minutes! If you do this 4 times a week, plus one longer workout, you train for just 88 minutes each week.

In the 1990s, Dr. Tabata tested his plan on college students. At first, they were very tired after the 4 minutes. But after 6 weeks, they got much better. 

He found that short, hard workouts can be as good as long, normal workouts. One group of students exercised for 1 hour, 5 days a week. Another group did a 10-minute warm-up, then 4 minutes of Tabata training, 4 times a week, plus one longer workout with some Tabata.

After 6 weeks, the Tabata group improved more than the group that trained for 5 hours a week. The Tabata group got 28% better at anaerobic exercise and 15% better at aerobic exercise. The other group only got 10% better at aerobic exercise and didn't improve at anaerobic exercise.

To do Tabata right, you must work very hard. You can't just sit and read a magazine. You need to do intense activities like running or using a rowing machine. It feels like doing 8 sprints with only 10 seconds of rest between them.

Dr. Tabata says you should work at 170% of your VO2 max. If you feel okay afterward, you didn't work hard enough. Beginners should start with a trainer.

Tabata training can help you get fit and burn fat. Right now, mostly serious athletes use it, but soon there will be instructors and DVDs to teach it.

Richard Scrivener, a fitness coach, says you shouldn't stop your regular training. Runners can do fewer long runs and add Tabata to rest and recover. Gym users can do 3 strength workouts and 3 Tabata workouts a week. For others, slowly add more Tabata sessions, but remember, every session needs your best effort.

In 2005, BlackBerry introduced instant messaging to mobile phones, making it very popular in Canada. Six years later, during riots in London, BlackBerry Messenger (BBM) was used so effectively by rioters that politicians wanted to shut it down. Now, two years after that, users are leaving BBM.

BlackBerry phones are less popular now because there are many other free messaging apps like WhatsApp and Kik. To keep customers, BBM was released for Android and Apple phones. Over 20 million people downloaded it, but many think it's too late. A blogger named James Gooderson says WhatsApp has made BBM unnecessary for young people.

BBM has 80 million monthly users after an update, but WhatsApp has 300 million. BBM doesn't have features like video calls, location sharing, or stickers, which other apps have. Messaging is changing from text to images. Apps like Instagram and Snapchat are becoming more popular.

Jean-Pierre Moore, who runs a youth club in London, says BBM was once very useful during riots, but now he uses an iPad. He believes shutting down BBM wouldn't stop crime. Most young smartphone owners use multiple social apps. Instagram is popular among teenagers because it feels more private than Facebook.

BlackBerry's low cost is still an advantage, but people don't trust BBM's privacy anymore. In richer areas, students prefer using WhatsApp on Apple phones. One teenager feels isolated because he's the only one with a BlackBerry.

In 2005, BlackBerry made instant messaging popular on phones. It was very successful then because the iPhone did not exist yet. BlackBerry was a big export from Canada.

In 2011, there were riots in London. People used BlackBerry Messenger (BBM) to talk during the riots. Later, fewer people wanted BlackBerry phones. Many new apps like WhatsApp and Kik became popular. These apps are free and work on different phones.

BBM tried to stay popular by working on Android and Apple phones. Over 20 million people downloaded BBM, but some think it won't last. James Gooderson, a tech blogger, says BBM came to Apple phones too late. WhatsApp is more popular with young people.

BBM has 80 million users, but WhatsApp has 300 million. Other apps have features BBM doesn't, like video calls and stickers. BBM's contact and calendar sharing is not available on Apple and Android phones.

Now, messaging includes photos and videos. In 2011, BBM helped start a revolution in Egypt and was used during the London riots. Today, nearly 80% of young smartphone users use social apps, often more than one. Most 16- to 24-year-olds use Facebook daily, but many also use other apps.

Apps change quickly. Some last, like Instagram, while others disappear. Bennett, a 13-year-old, has three phones: a BlackBerry for messaging, an iPhone for games, and an Android for calls. He uses Instagram a lot. "Instagram is Facebook without parents," he says.

BlackBerry phones are cheap to buy and use. You can get a second-hand phone and a £7-a-month plan to use BBM. But people don't trust BBM's privacy anymore. After the riots, people were arrested, showing messages weren't secret.

In rich areas of London, teenagers use Apple phones and WhatsApp. BBM is not popular anymore. One teenager says he feels isolated because he is the only one with a BlackBerry.

The right of Bolivia's indigenous tribes to chew coca leaves, which are used to make cocaine, has caused big disagreements internationally. This could affect how drugs are controlled around the world. Bolivia got a special permission from the 1961 Convention on Narcotic Drugs, allowing its indigenous people to chew the leaves.

Bolivia argued that the convention went against its 2009 constitution, which protects coca as part of its culture. South American Indians have chewed coca leaves for centuries because they provide energy and have medicinal uses. Danny Kushlick from the Transform Drug Policy Foundation said Bolivia’s move is inspiring and shows countries can change their relationship with UN drug rules.

However, the UN’s International Narcotics Control Board (INCB) thinks Bolivia is threatening drug control. Countries like the UK, US, Italy, Sweden, the Netherlands, and Russia oppose Bolivia’s demands. The UK worries the exemption might increase coca production and cocaine trade, weakening the fight against drugs.

The right to chew coca leaves was taken away in 1964 when Bolivia was under a dictatorship. Bolivia was given 25 years to stop, but the ban ended in 1989, leading to disputes. In 2011, Bolivia’s President Evo Morales, a former coca grower, said Bolivia didn’t want to be part of the convention anymore. Now, Bolivia is back in the convention with an exemption for its indigenous people to chew coca leaves.

This is the first such exemption in UN drug treaties, raising concerns that other countries might ask for similar exemptions. Russia warns this could increase illegal cocaine and set a bad example. The British parliament suggested supporting Bolivia’s request, arguing it’s important for countries to stay in the convention. Bolivia’s return could be blocked if a third or more of the 184 countries that signed the convention oppose it.

Critics argue that objections to Bolivia’s demands are legally weak and ignore international norms on cultural and indigenous rights. The ban on coca chewing was based on a 1950 report that supporters say wasn’t based on evidence. Growing coca leaves is legal and regulated in Bolivia, which some think has helped reduce cocaine production, making Bolivia a model for others.

A big argument started about Bolivia's native people being allowed to chew coca leaves. Coca leaves are used to make cocaine. Bolivia got a special permission from a 1961 agreement that controls drugs worldwide. This permission lets Bolivia’s native people chew the leaves.

Bolivia says the agreement does not agree with its new rules. These rules say it must protect coca leaves as part of its culture and say that coca leaves are not dangerous.

For many years, South American natives have chewed coca leaves because they give energy and have healing powers. People who support Bolivia think it is right to defend the rights of native people. Danny Kushlick from the Transform Drug Policy Foundation says Bolivia’s action is important. It shows that any country can change how it deals with the UN drug rules.

However, the UN’s International Narcotics Control Board (INCB) thinks Bolivia might hurt the global drug rules. Countries like the UK, the US, Italy, Sweden, the Netherlands, and Russia do not want to give Bolivia what it wants.

The UK told the UN it respects the cultural value of coca leaves in Bolivia. But it is worried that letting Bolivia chew coca leaves could lead to more coca production and more cocaine. This would make it harder to stop illegal drugs.

In 1964, when Bolivia had a dictator, it signed the agreement and took away the right of South American Andean people to chew coca leaves. In 2011, Bolivia told the UN it did not want to be part of the agreement anymore. Now, Bolivia is back in the agreement but with a special permission for its native people to chew coca leaves.

This is the first time a country has gotten such a permission in UN drug rules. Other countries might ask for similar permissions too. Russia says this will lead to more illegal cocaine and sets a bad example.

The British parliament asked the UK government to support Bolivia’s request. It is important for countries to stay in the agreement. Bolivia’s return could be stopped if one-third or more of the 184 countries that signed the agreement oppose it. Some people think the US and UK are telling other countries to block Bolivia’s request.

Nancie Prud’homme from the International Centre on Human Rights and Drug Policy says people are wrong to oppose Bolivia’s request. She says these objections are not fully legal. Supporting cultural and native rights is becoming normal around the world, so we should support Bolivia.

The rule to ban coca chewing was based on a 1950 report that some say did not use any proof. It is okay to grow coca leaves in Bolivia. Because of this, cocaine making has gone down in the country, and some experts think Bolivia is a good example for others.

A Dutch company named Mars One wants to send four astronauts to Mars to start a new home there in 2023. However, there are some big issues.

First, the astronauts' bodies will need to adjust to Mars's gravity, which is much weaker than Earth's. This could change their bones, muscles, and blood flow so much that they wouldn't be able to live on Earth again. Second, because of this, the astronauts won't be able to come back to Earth.

According to Mars One’s website, coming back isn’t planned. To return, they would need a special rocket with enough fuel to leave Mars and travel back to Earth. They would also need to meet up with a space station or land safely back on Earth.

Despite these challenges, over 10,000 people have applied to join the mission. The Medical Director, Norbert Kraft, said the applicants range from 18 to 62 years old, and most are men.

One applicant, a 32-year-old American woman named Cynthia, said she always dreamed of going to Mars. She thinks being part of the first colony on Mars would be exciting and inspiring.

Mars One looks for qualities like resilience, adaptability, curiosity, trustworthiness, and resourcefulness in their astronauts. They must be at least 18 years old.

Mars One says that water can be found in the soil and that Mars has nitrogen, an important part of the air we breathe. Solar panels will provide power for the colony.

The project costs around $6 billion. Bas Lansdorp, the founder, hopes to raise some of this money by selling broadcasting rights, similar to how the London Olympics made money.

Paul Rmer, who helped create the reality TV show Big Brother, thinks this mission could be a huge media event.

The goal is to start a permanent home on Mars. The first group of four astronauts would arrive in 2023, followed by more teams every two years.

Some people doubt if the mission can succeed, especially with the challenges of getting to Mars and setting up a colony.

Mars One believes that starting a colony on Mars is important for learning more about the solar system, the origin of life, and our place in the universe.

To go, astronauts must be strong, flexible, curious, trust others, and be smart with resources. They must be older than 18. Mars One says the astronauts can find water by melting ice in the ground and use the nitrogen in the air. They will use solar panels for power.

Paul Römer, who made a famous TV show called Big Brother, thinks this mission could be the biggest TV event ever. It would be like a reality show that never ends.

Mars One wants to build a home for people on Mars forever. The first group would land in 2023, and then four more astronauts would come every two years.

Some people don't believe this can happen. They worry about how the astronauts will get there and build a home with everything they need.

Mars One hopes this mission will make people believe anything is possible, just like the moon landings did. They think it's important to build a home on Mars to learn more about space, life, and where we come from.

At Leicester University, a big meeting told everyone that they found King Richard III's body under a parking lot. The man had a curved spine. They also learned about his final moments and how his body was treated badly after he died. Richard Buckley, the leader of the archaeologists, announced that they were sure they found Richard III.

The proof was strong. Scientists did DNA tests, used special computer images to look at the bones, and found a living relative with matching DNA. Experts also studied old writings about the king’s death and burial.

People are planning a new tomb for Richard III in Leicester Cathedral, close to where they found him. There will be a ceremony to put him in his new grave, likely next year. The city is also making plans for a new visitor center in an old school building near the site.

Richard III died in battle at Bosworth on August 22, 1485. He was the last English king to die in battle. A photo showed a deep cut on the bottom of his skull, probably from a sharp axe. This blow likely killed him instantly. Another sword cut to his head was also deadly. Some injuries happened after he died, suggesting his body was mistreated as it was taken to Leicester.

One injury shows that his body was probably dragged on a horse and humiliated. Bob Savage, a weapons expert, thinks it was done with a common knife or dagger, not a weapon used in battle.

Michael Ibsen, a Canadian furniture maker and a descendant of Richard III’s sister, heard the news and was shocked. He said many people died that day, and Richard was just one of them.

Mathew Morris found the body on the first day of digging. At first, he didn’t think it was the king. The area was chosen based on years of research. The body was buried quickly in a church called Grey Friars. When they confirmed it was the king, they carefully dug up the bones.

Philippa Langley from the Richard III Society believes Richard was a good king who faced unfair stories. There is also the mystery of the two young princes who disappeared after Richard III took the throne. Their bones were found later, but it’s not certain if they belong to the princes. More DNA tests might be needed to solve this mystery.

A team at Leicester University found King Richard III's body under a car park. When Richard Buckley, the team leader, announced this, everyone cheered.

Scientists did DNA tests, used special computer pictures to look at the bones, and found a family member with matching DNA. They also read old stories about where the king was buried.

People are making a new tomb for the king in Leicester Cathedral, close to where they found him. There will be a ceremony to put him in his new grave next year. Leicester’s Museums are planning a new visitor center near the spot where he was found.

King Richard died in a battle on August 22, 1485. He was the last English king to die in battle. Scientists found out how he died. His skull had a big cut from an axe, which likely made him unconscious and dead quickly. Another sword hit also went into his brain. Other cuts happened after he died, showing his body was hurt as it was taken back to Leicester.

Bob Savage, who knows about old weapons, said the cuts were probably from a sharp knife, not a war weapon.

Michael Ibsen, a relative of the king, was surprised when he heard the news. He said many people died that day, and it was a violent time.

Mathew Morris found the body on the first day of digging in the car park. At first, he did not think it was the king. Later, when they saw the curved spine, they realized it might be him.

Philippa Langley from the Richard III Society thinks Richard was a good king. Some people still believe he killed two young princes who were kept in the Tower of London. Their bodies were never found, so scientists might need to do more tests to find out what happened.

Scientists put a fake memory into the brains of mice to understand why people sometimes remember things that never happened. False memories can cause problems in court because eyewitnesses might say something that isn't true, leading to wrong decisions.

Susumu Tonegawa, a scientist at MIT, and his team studied how false memories form in the brain. They made memories in mice by changing certain brain cells. Real and fake memories use the same parts of the brain.

In the experiment, mice were placed in a box and allowed to explore. Their brain cells made a memory protein. The next day, the mice were put in another box and got a small electric shock. At the same time, the researchers used light to turn on the memory of the first box. This made the mice connect the fear from the shock with the first box.

When the mice went back to the first box, they were scared even though they hadn’t been shocked there. This shows that the mice had a false memory.

Tonegawa thinks humans might do the same thing. People can mix up what they imagine with real events. He says it’s hard for someone with false memories to tell the difference between real and fake ones. He hopes this research will show legal experts how unreliable memories can be.

Chris French, a researcher from the University of London, says the study is important for understanding false memories. He warns that creating false memories in mice is much simpler than making complex false memories in humans, like remembering things that didn’t happen in childhood.

Mark Stokes, a scientist at Oxford University, says the experiments are impressive but should be seen in context. Changing memories in the brain is different from normal memory.

Steve Ramirez, a colleague of Tonegawa, says they can now ask more complex questions about memories. For example, can false memories be made for objects or other mice?

French adds that as the technology improves, scientists must consider the ethical issues. There is a big risk of misuse if false memories can be implanted.

Scientists did an experiment where they put fake memories in mice brains. They want to learn why people sometimes remember things that didn't really happen.

Fake memories can cause problems in court. People might say they saw something, but later, new proof shows they were wrong.

A scientist named Susumu Tonagawa from MIT and his team studied how fake memories form. They made mice remember things that didn’t happen by changing brain cells.

First, they let the mice explore a box. Then, the next day, they put the mice in a different box and gave them a little shock. At the same time, they used light to make the mice remember the first box. So, the mice thought the first box was scary even though nothing bad happened there.

This shows that mice can get scared of a place they shouldn’t be scared of. The same thing might happen to people.

Tonagawa said that our minds can mix up what we think with what really happens. He thinks this study helps show that memories can be tricky and not always true.

Chris French, a researcher from the University of London, said that while this study is helpful, human memories are much more complicated. He warns that we still don’t fully understand how complex fake memories, like remembering being abused as a child or seeing aliens, form in the brain.

Steve Ramirez, who works with Tonagawa, said that now they can change memories in mice, they can start answering questions about memories that used to only be thought about in science fiction stories.

Music services like Spotify and Deezer have made over $1 billion worldwide as more people pay to listen to music online. In 2013, money from streaming and subscriptions went up by more than 50% to $1.1 billion. For the first time in 12 years, recorded music sales in Europe increased.

Many people still listen for free, but more music fans are paying for better choices. The number of paying users went from 8 million to 28 million in three years, according to the 2014 digital music report from the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI).

Subscription services are popular because they are easy to use on smartphones and tablets. People like these services because they are cheaper, easier to use, and legal compared to illegal downloads. According to IFPI Chief Executive Frances Moore, music streaming and subscription services are now a main part of the music business.

One Direction sold the most music in 2013 with 4 million copies of their album "Midnight Memories." Katy Perry's "Prism" was the top album by a woman, coming in sixth place after Eminem, Justin Timberlake, Bruno Mars, and Daft Punk.

Big tech companies like Apple and Google are also getting into music streaming with services like iTunes Radio and Google Play Store. Small companies like Beats Music are also joining.

In the UK and US, streaming could soon make more money for the music industry than downloads from online stores like Apple's iTunes. Subscription services now make up a third of all digital sales globally, with downloads making up the rest. However, the growth rates of these two formats are different.

In the US, the percentage of people using subscription services and streaming rose from 19% in 2012 to 23%, while the percentage of people downloading dropped slightly from 28% to 27%. In the UK, the number of downloaders stayed the same at one-third, while the number of subscribers grew from 19% to 22%. In Sweden, France, and Italy, streaming is already more popular than downloading.

Digital formats now make up 39% of all music sales, which is almost 5.9 billion out of 15 billion. Even though sales of physical formats like CDs and vinyl have dropped sharply in 2013, they still bring in more than half of the industry’s income.

Vinyl sales are increasing again in some places. They went up by 32% in the US and 101% in the UK in 2013.

Music apps like Spotify and Deezer made over $1 billion worldwide. Fans are now paying for music online.

In 2013, money from music streaming and subscriptions went up by more than 50%, reaching $1.1 billion. For the first time in 12 years, sales of recorded music in Europe also increased.

Lots of people still listen to music for free, but many prefer to pay for a wider choice. The number of paying users went from 8 million to 28 million in three years, as reported by IFPI.

These services are easy to use on phones and tablets. They are popular because they offer a cheap, easy, and legal way to listen to new music instead of downloading illegally.

In Britain and America, streaming could soon earn more money than downloads from stores like Apple's iTunes. One-third of all digital music sales now come from subscription services, while the rest come from downloads.

In the U.S., the number of people using subscription services and streaming rose from 19% in 2012 to 23%. At the same time, the number of people downloading music dropped from 28% to 27%.

In Britain, the number of people downloading music stayed the same at one-third, but the number of subscribers grew from 19% to 22%. In Sweden, France, and Italy, streaming is already more popular than downloading.

Now, 39% of all music sales are digital. CD and vinyl sales dropped a lot in 2013, but they still make up over half of the music industry’s income.

Vinyl sales are coming back in some areas. They increased by 32% in America and by 101% in the UK in 2013.

Inside one of Britain's most expensive homes, called The Tower, you can see lots of bird droppings and broken things. It’s a big 30-meter palace in a rich area of north London. This palace and nine others nearby have been empty for about 25 years. People think they were bought for members of the Saudi Arabian royal family. The buildings are falling apart, with broken columns, and swimming pools filled with trash. Owls now live there.

This is happening on a street that Lloyds Bank says is the second most expensive in Britain. As house prices go up by 11.2% each year, making it hard for many people to buy homes, 16 mansions on this street are empty, often behind locked gates and guarded by dogs.

Across the street, another mansion worth £18 million has broken windows and paint to stop people climbing. Another mansion, sold for £20 million, has metal bars blocking its windows.

Seeing these empty, ruined homes is upsetting for people who struggle to find affordable places to live in London. A security guard working on the street finds it frustrating to see so many homes that could house many people falling apart.

Rich people from countries like Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, Iran, China, Russia, and Kazakhstan have bought homes on this street near Hampstead Heath because it is famous, like the Champs Elysees and Rodeo Drive. Two mansions recently for sale cost £65 million and £38 million, with fancy features like marble floors, leather elevators, and panic rooms.

In the empty mansions, gardens are overgrown, fountains are breaking, and inside, water drips from ceilings onto rotting carpets. Moss grows through broken bricks, and the swimming pools are full of dirty water with plants growing through the tiles.

The Tower is the most dramatic ruin, with pigeon-filled halls and green walls covered in algae. Boxes marked "bullet-proof glass" show the past owners' fear for safety.

Very few people live on the street all the time. Magdy Adib Ishak-Hannah, who lives there permanently and has a personal wealth of £45 million, says only about three houses are lived in 24/7, and half of the properties are occupied three to six months a year. The rest are rarely used.

These ruined homes show that rich people see British property as investments. Some want to change the street by building smaller, cheaper apartments instead of large mansions to bring more people back. However, no one plans to use the empty properties to help solve the housing crisis because the land is too expensive.

There are bird droppings in a very expensive house in London called The Tower. It costs £30 million. The house is empty and in bad shape. Pigeons are inside, and water is coming through the walls. 

Ten big houses on The Bishops Avenue are empty. The Saudi Arabian royal family owns some of these houses. The columns are breaking, and the swimming pools are full of broken pieces. Plants and owls have moved in.

The Bishops Avenue is the second most expensive street in Britain. Houses there cost a lot of money. Many people cannot afford to buy a house, but 16 big houses on this street are empty. The gates are locked, and there are guard dogs in the gardens.

Across the street, there is another empty house worth £18 million. Its windows are broken, and the walls have paint to stop people from climbing. Another house, sold for £20 million, has metal bars on the windows.

Seeing these empty houses is hard for people who cannot find a place to live. A security guard said it is annoying to see so many empty houses.

Rich people from Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, Iran, Russia, Kazakhstan, and China buy houses on this street. Two mansions are now for sale for £65 million and £38 million.

Inside the empty houses, things are falling apart. In one house, the ceiling fell down, and water is dripping from a big light fixture. Moss is growing on the walls, and plants are growing through the tiles of the swimming pool.

The Tower, a big house, is the worst. Pigeons are inside, and the walls are green with algae.

Very few people live on The Bishops Avenue all the time. Magdy Adib Ishak-Hannah, who has £45 million, is one of the few who live there all the time. He says only a few houses are used all the time, while others are used for just a few months each year.

Some of the world's richest people buy these houses as investments. Anil Varma wants to build smaller apartments to bring more people to live there. He plans to build 20 apartments with a pool, spa, and cinema.

For Tua Pittman, a traditional navigator from Raratonga in the Cook Islands, a canoe is more than just transportation. The canoe represents the island, the crew members represent the community, and the navigator is the leader. Pittman explains that navigating a canoe involves using the stars, moon, sun, and birds, and it's about leading the crew and showing them the way of life.

Pittman and his crew arrived in Sydney for the World Parks Congress after a long journey starting from the Cook Islands on September 25. They traveled through Samoa, Fiji, Vanuatu, and the Gold Coast before reaching Sydney. About 100 crew members were part of the voyage, aiming to use only traditional navigation methods. However, they sometimes had to use modern equipment to arrive on time.

The voyage is called the Mua Voyage. It's a project by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and five Pacific Island countries: Samoa, Tonga, New Zealand, the Cook Islands, and Fiji. The 6,000-nautical-mile (11,000 km) trip aimed to send a message about the state of the oceans to the World Parks Congress.

The message warns that fish and marine life are decreasing due to overfishing and that coral reefs are disappearing. The Pacific Islanders want to highlight that the ocean is vast but not unlimited, and growing populations and development are harming marine life.

At the Congress, there was discussion about setting new targets for marine protected areas. In 2013, only about three percent of the world’s oceans were protected, and less than one percent of that was completely off-limits to fishing. Scientists like Professor Callum Roberts say that the previous target of 20-30% protected areas is not enough and suggest raising it to 33%.

After discussions, the Congress agreed to set a new goal: each marine habitat should have at least 30% protected areas. Pittman was happy with this decision, saying it was a big reward for their efforts.

Pittman, aged 55, noticed that catching fish is becoming harder and pollution is worsening, especially near big cities. Climate change is also affecting Pacific Islanders more severely than larger, developed countries.

The Mua Voyage took years of planning and preparation. Pittman hopes that world leaders will listen to their message and find a new path forward, similar to how traditional navigators guide their canoes.

Tua Pittman from Raratonga in the Cook Islands is a traditional navigator. He says, "A canoe is like our island, the crew is like our community, and the navigator is the leader. On a canoe, we use stars, the moon, the sun, and birds to move from one place to another. Navigation shows the crew how to live."

Tua and about 100 others sailed four canoes from the Cook Islands to Sydney for the World Parks Congress. They started on September 25 and went through Samoa, Fiji, Vanuatu, and the Gold Coast before reaching Sydney. They tried to use only old ways to navigate but sometimes used modern tools to get to Australia on time.

This trip is called the Mua Voyage. It is a project by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and five Pacific Island countries: Samoa, Tonga, New Zealand, the Cook Islands, and Fiji. They traveled 11,000 kilometers to tell the Congress that there are fewer fish now, and the fish are smaller. Foreign fishermen take their fish, and their coral reefs and fishing places are disappearing. Their ocean is big but not endless.

At the Congress, they talked about protecting more of the ocean. In 2013, less than 3% of the world's oceans were protected, and less than 1% of that was 'no take' (no fishing). The goal now is to protect at least 30% of the ocean.

Tua is happy with the decision. He says it is a good step. He sees it is harder to catch fish now and that pollution is worse near big cities like Sydney. Climate change is also hurting Pacific Islanders a lot.

The Mua Voyage took years to plan. Tua wants world leaders to listen and act. He says rich country leaders should think like traditional navigators who know their boats are small in a big sea. Politicians need to change how they work. "The world needs a new way," Tua says.

The Chief Medical Officer for England says antibiotic resistance is as dangerous as terrorism. But each year, more people die from drug-resistant bacteria than from terrorist attacks.

The World Health Organization says that just for tuberculosis, multi-drug resistance causes more than 150,000 deaths per year. Antibiotic resistance is a serious threat. We need to fight it.

A hundred years ago, life expectancy in the UK was about 47 years for men and 50 for women. Many babies and young children died from diseases. Now, a child born in Britain has a one in four chance of living to 100. This improvement is thanks to public health systems, vaccines, and antibiotics.

In intensive care units, where I work, antibiotic-resistant bacteria are common. Powerful antibiotics kill regular bacteria but leave stronger ones alive. When I started as a doctor in the late 1990s, we learned about MRSA, a type of bacteria resistant to many antibiotics. We had a few drugs to fight it, like vancomycin. But antibiotic-resistant bacteria kept growing, and new types of resistance appeared.

We overused antibiotics in healthcare and put them in animal feed. We thought we would always have new drugs to fight bacteria, but this is not true anymore. New, more resistant bacteria have emerged. Vancomycin stopped working against MRSA, and VRSA appeared. Other bacteria also became resistant. Today, infections with highly resistant bacteria are common, and new drugs are not being made fast enough.

Antibiotics became common in the 1940s, and soon after, we saw the first signs of bacteria resistance. Now, this is a normal part of medical life. Since the first MRSA deaths in healthy children in the US in 1998, the number of deaths from MRSA has risen to tens of thousands each year, more than AIDS deaths. Hospitals are full of resistant bacteria.

To win this war, doctors need to change how they give out antibiotics, and fewer antibiotics should be used in farming. We also need to encourage drug companies to make new antibiotics, even if they are not profitable.

If we do not make big changes, we may go back to a time when many more people died from infections. Losing the fight against bacteria would be terrible.

The top doctor in England said antibiotic resistance is as big a problem as terrorism. But, every year, more people die from antibiotic resistance than from terrorist attacks. The World Health Organization says over 150,000 people die from tuberculosis because of antibiotic resistance each year. This is a serious battle.

A hundred years ago, men in the UK lived to about 47 years old and women to 50. Many kids died before age five from sicknesses. Today, a child born in Britain has a 25% chance of living to 100 years old. We can thank better health care, vaccines, and antibiotics for this.

In hospital intensive care units, there are many antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Powerful antibiotics are used often. They kill regular bacteria but not the strong ones that learned to live through antibiotics.

When I started as a doctor in the 1990s, I learned about MRSA, a bacteria that resists methicillin and other penicillins. Only a few drugs like vancomycin could kill it. But antibiotic-resistant bacteria became more common.

Doctors and farms use too many antibiotics. Farms also add antibiotics to animal feed. We thought we could always make new antibiotics, but this is not true anymore. New, stronger bacteria keep appearing. Even vancomycin stopped working against MRSA. Hospitals found VRSA, another resistant bacteria. Other bacteria are becoming resistant too.

Now, infections with very resistant bacteria are common, but fewer new antibiotics are being made. It's hard to create new drugs that work against resistant bacteria. Antibiotics cost a lot to make, are only used for short times, and stop working due to resistance.

To win this battle, doctors must change how they give out antibiotics, and less should be used on farms. Companies need reasons to make new antibiotics even if they won't make much money.

Less than 100 years after penicillin was found, we are starting to lose the fight against antibiotic resistance.

People from Rwanda and parts of Burundi are visiting Butare, a town in southern Rwanda, to try ice cream at a shop named Inzozi Nziza, which means Sweet Dreams. This is the first ice cream shop in central Africa. Customers can choose from flavors like sweet cream, passion fruit, strawberry, and pineapple. They can add toppings such as fresh fruit, honey, chocolate chips, and granola. The shop also sells black tea and coffee.

Louise Ingabire, the shop's manager, says ice cream is new to many Rwandans. She believes there is still work to be done to introduce this treat to more people. The shop has changed lives, giving jobs to people who did not have them before. For example, a 27-year-old woman now has a job and can support her family.

Butare, with 89,600 residents, is 135 kilometers south of the capital, Kigali. It is home to the National University of Rwanda. Students often visit the shop to relax and enjoy ice cream.

Kalisa Migendo, a 24-year-old agriculture student, says the shop brings people together. He mentions that it’s a good place to meet friends or dates.

The ice cream ingredients are mostly local, with milk from nearby Nyanza and some items like vanilla and cocoa brought in from other places.

Inzozi Nziza was started by Odile Gakire Katese, a theater director. She partnered with Alexis Miesen and Jennie Dundas from Blue Marble Ice Cream in New York to open the shop in 2010. They believed the shop would help rebuild community spirit and family traditions.

Miesen and Dundas initially owned the shop with the staff, but after 18 months, they gave their shares to the women running the business. The shop is a cooperative and nonprofit organization.

The shop employs nine women who also play in Ingoma Nshya, Rwanda’s first and only female drumming group. Some of these women are survivors of the 1994 genocide, where almost a million people died. The drumming group helps bring unity among Hutu and Tutsi women.

A documentary called "Sweet Dreams" by filmmakers Rob and Lisa Fruchtman tells the story of the women and their efforts to build a better future after the genocide. The film highlights resilience, hope, and the ability to change one's life.

A report by the World Health Organization (WHO) states that 35.6% of women worldwide will face physical or sexual violence, mostly from male partners. The report shows that 30% of women are attacked by partners, and 38% of female murders are committed by partners.

In Africa, almost half (45.6%) of women will experience violence. In low- and middle-income parts of Europe, it's 27.2%, while in richer countries, 32.7% of women will face violence. About 42% of women who experience violence get hurt, leading them to seek help from healthcare workers. This is often the first chance to find out about violence at home and offer support.

Violence affects women's health. Some visit hospitals with broken bones, while others have problems related to pregnancy or mental health issues.

Two WHO reports—one on violence and another on how healthcare workers can help—are led by Dr. Claudia Garcia-Moreno and Professor Charlotte Watts. They found that violence causes health issues like HIV, depression, alcoholism, unwanted pregnancies, and low birth weight babies.

Garcia-Moreno noted that violence rates are high everywhere. Even in wealthy countries, 23.2% of women will face violence from partners. More sexual assaults by acquaintances or strangers are reported in rich countries—12.6% of women will be attacked by someone they don't know, compared to 11.9% in Africa.

Better education and employment can reduce violence, but not in all areas. Watts believes society needs to rethink its views on violence against women.

Garcia-Moreno says the numbers show the importance of addressing this issue. She adds that recognizing signs of violence is crucial for healthcare workers. Training is needed to identify and help victims of violence.

A report by the World Health Organization (WHO) says that 35.6 out of 100 women worldwide will face physical or sexual violence, mostly from a male partner. About 30 out of 100 women are hurt by their partners. Also, 38 out of 100 murdered women are killed by their partners.

In Africa, almost half of all women—45.6 out of 100—will face violence. In poorer parts of Europe, it's 27.2 out of 100. Even in richer countries, 32.7 out of 100 women will face violence. Around 42 out of 100 women who face violence get hurt, and doctors can see these injuries.

Violence affects women's health. Some women go to the hospital with broken bones, while others have problems with pregnancy or mental health.

The WHO made two reports—one on violence and another on how doctors and nurses can help women. Dr. Claudia Garcia-Moreno and Professor Charlotte Watts wrote the reports.

Garcia-Moreno said, "We looked at data from all over the world on violence by partners and non-partners and its effects on health." This includes HIV, depression, alcoholism, unwanted pregnancies, and babies born too small.

Even in rich countries, 23.2 out of 100 women will face violence from a partner. Worldwide, 30 out of 100 women are attacked by partners.

In rich countries, more women report sexual attacks by people they know or strangers. In rich countries, 12.6 out of 100 women will face sexual attacks by someone who is not their partner. In Africa, it's 11.9 out of 100.

Better-educated and working women are less likely to face violence, but this isn't true everywhere. Watts said some societies think violence against women is okay.

Garcia-Moreno said the numbers show we need to pay more attention to this issue. More people now see it as a problem, but it's complex. The WHO suggests teaching doctors and nurses to spot signs of violence but does not advise asking every woman if she has faced violence.

"If a woman keeps coming back with unexplained injuries, you should ask her about domestic violence," said Garcia-Moreno.

The auction of a Banksy painting called "Slave Labour" was stopped just before it was supposed to be sold. This painting shows a child making British flags and was put on the wall of a shop in London. It was expected to sell for around $700,000 in Florida.

The auctioneer, Frederic Thut, did not say why the painting was taken off the sale list. However, community leaders in London were very happy because they wanted to stop the sale of this artwork that was taken from a shop wall.

Alan Strickland, a local leader, said they wanted the painting not to be sold and to get it back. They are glad their efforts worked.

Claire Kober, the head of Haringey Council, asked the Arts Council England and the Mayor of Miami to stop the sale. The auction house later said they convinced the owners to take the Banksy paintings off the sale list.

Some people think the auction house is selling stolen items, but Thut says the seller is the rightful owner and the sale is legal. He also said he got many messages from the UK but believed selling the artworks would help keep them safe.

Another Banksy piece, "Wet Dog," which was taken from a wall in Bethlehem, was also removed from the sale. It was expected to sell for up to $800,000.

Poundland, the shop where "Slave Labour" was originally placed, said they don't know who took it. Banksy has not commented on this issue but has spoken against selling his work before.

Stephan Keszler, an art dealer, thinks it's okay to sell Banksy's work without his permission since Banksy puts his art on other people’s property without asking.

On a special day at Liverpool Cathedral for the families of the 96 people who died at the Hillsborough football ground, one word was heard often: "the truth." The Sun newspaper used this word in a headline, but we now know the story in the newspaper was given by the South Yorkshire Police to blame the victims.

Margaret Aspinall's son James, aged 18, died at the match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest. She said the families fought for 23 years to get the truth. Aspinall, who leads the Hillsborough Family Support Group, said the families' loss would always be there, but she was happy the Prime Minister apologized for Hillsborough.

An independent group looked at 450,000 documents from the police, Sheffield Wednesday, and others. They made a 395-page report that showed the victims and other fans were not to blame. The police tried to blame the supporters, saying they were drunk or did not have tickets. But the report found no proof of this.

The police chief, Peter Wright, told a story that fans caused the disaster. They tested the victims' blood for alcohol, which the report said was unnecessary. When they found alcohol, they checked if the victims had criminal records. The report found no evidence of drunkenness, missing tickets, or violence among the fans.

The police met to create a defense story just four days after the disaster. On that day, The Sun newspaper published its headline based on information from four senior police officers. The police changed 116 out of 164 statements to remove criticism of themselves and highlight supporter misbehavior.

The first inquiry in 1989 found the police stories were false. It also found that the football ground was unsafe and the Football Association did not check if it was safe. The main cause of the disaster was the police's poor handling of the crowd. Chief Superintendent David Duckenfield made a mistake by opening a large gate and letting many people in when the area was already crowded.

The police still blamed the fans at the inquest. The coroner did not look at what happened after 3:15 pm, so the emergency response was not examined. The report found that 41 of the 96 who died might have been saved with proper help from the police and ambulance service.

After the report, the Attorney General will decide if there should be a new inquest. There may also be prosecutions of Sheffield Wednesday, South Yorkshire Police, and Sheffield City Council. Trevor Hicks, whose two teenage daughters died, said the truth is out and now it's time for justice.

In 1989, ninety-six people died at Sheffield Wednesday's Hillsborough Stadium. Twenty-three years later, the families of the victims learned the truth about what happened. The Sun newspaper had a headline saying "The Truth," but it was not true. The police gave them the wrong story.

Margaret Aspinall's son, James, who was 18, died at the match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest. She said the families fought for 23 years to learn the truth. She is happy the Prime Minister apologized for Hillsborough.

The main reason for the disaster was how the police handled the crowd. They let too many people in through one gate and did not close a tunnel. If the police and ambulance workers had done better, they could have saved 41 of the 96 lives.

Now, there might be a new investigation and some people might be punished. Trevor Hicks, whose two daughters died, said the truth is out and tomorrow is for justice.

Facebook has lost many users each month in big places like the US and UK. In the last six months, it lost almost 9 million users in the US and 2 million in the UK. Studies show that Facebook's growth in these areas has stopped. In the last month, Facebook lost 6 million US users, which is a 4% drop. In the UK, 1.4 million fewer users visited in March, a 4.5% drop.

People are also using Facebook less in Canada, Spain, France, Germany, and Japan. Most people who wanted to join Facebook in the US and UK have already done so. People get bored and try new things.

Other social networks are becoming more popular with young people. Instagram gained 30 million new users in 18 months before Facebook bought it. Path, a social network that limits friends to 150, is getting 1 million new users every week. It now has over 9 million users, including 500,000 from Venezuela who joined in one weekend.

Facebook is growing quickly in South America. In Brazil, monthly visitors increased by 6% to 70 million. In India, there was a 4% rise to 64 million users, but this is still a small part of the country’s population.

However, in developed countries, Facebook is losing users. Analysts say the number of visitors to Facebook worldwide peaked at 1.05 billion in January, then dropped by 20 million in February. By April, the numbers went up again. Since December, Facebook lost nearly 2 million users in the UK, with the total staying at 27 million.

Americans are spending less time on Facebook. They spent 121 billion minutes on Facebook in December 2012, but this dropped to 115 billion minutes in February.

People are using smartphones and tablets more than personal computers to access Facebook. Smartphone usage has doubled in a year to 69 minutes a month, but this may not make up for the decrease in desktop usage.

Facebook will report its performance to investors. Wall Street expects revenues of about $1.44 billion, up from $1.06 billion a year ago. Investors want to know how many mobile users Facebook is gaining and if advertising revenue is growing at the same rate.

At the end of 2012, mobile usage made up nearly a quarter of Facebook's advertising income, and the network had 680 million mobile users a month. Facebook might be losing younger users to other similar services. To attract more smartphone users, Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg created new initiatives like Facebook Home, which can be downloaded onto Android phones to show news, photos, and ads directly on the home screen.

Vienna is the best city to live in, while Baghdad is the worst, according to a study on quality of life. German-speaking cities like Zurich, Munich, Düsseldorf, and Frankfurt are also in the top seven. Paris fell ten spots to 37th place, partly because of terrorist attacks. London is at 39th.

London ranks low because of air pollution, traffic, and weather. Edinburgh is next at 46th. Paris dropped because of safety concerns.

The Moroccan city of Ouarzazate is famous for movie-making. It's near the Sahara Desert and has been used to film movies like "Lawrence of Arabia" and "Game of Thrones."

Ouarzazate is also home to four big solar power plants. These plants, along with wind and water power, will provide almost half of Morocco’s electricity from clean sources by 2020. Morocco wants to become a leader in solar power.

When finished, the complex will be the biggest solar power plant in the world. The first part, Noor 1, opened in November 2015. It uses curved mirrors to collect sunlight, which is more costly than regular solar panels but can produce power even after dark.

Scientists have known for years that deserts get a lot of sunlight. After the Chernobyl disaster in 1986, a scientist named Gerhard Knies found that deserts get enough sunlight in a few hours to power the whole world for a year. The challenge is to capture and transport this energy.

Noor 1 has 500,000 curved mirrors that follow the sun. When all four plants are done, they will cover an area as big as the city of Rabat and produce enough electricity for a million homes.

Morocco’s environment minister, Hakima el-Haite, thinks solar energy could change the region like oil did in the last century. She says importing 94% of Morocco’s energy costs a lot of money, so they decided to use solar energy instead.

By 2020, solar energy will make up a third of Morocco’s renewable energy, with wind and water providing the rest. El-Haite says this project is the most important solar plant in the world.

The next parts of the project, Noor 2 and 3, will store energy for up to eight hours, allowing 24/7 solar power. Morocco hopes to export solar energy to other countries, which could help stabilize regions.

About $9 billion has been spent on the Noor Complex, with funding from international banks and the Moroccan government. Workers are finishing the project, wearing safety gear and working long hours.

A global audience is interested in seeing how this project works.
