Maha el-Kadiri, from the Moroccan solar energy agency, says exporting solar energy could help keep peace between countries. Morocco is working with Tunisia and hopes to send energy to Europe too.

First, they need to build the connections to Europe. Until then, the solar energy will be used in Morocco. They might use solar energy to remove salt from sea water someday.

Swedish prisons are known for being progressive. In November 2013, Nils Oberg, the head of Sweden's prison and probation service, announced that four prisons would close because there were fewer prisoners. Even though crime rates did not go down, the number of prisoners fell by 6% between 2011 and 2012, dropping to just over 4,500. This trend continued in 2013 and 2014. Oberg hopes that the decrease is due to the prison system’s focus on rehabilitation.

Kenneth Gustafsson, the governor of Kumla Prison, the most secure prison in Sweden, says that the prison system has changed since he started working there in 1978. Although prisons used to treat prisoners very well, after several escapes in 2004, they focused more on security.

Sweden uses a humane approach to sentencing. Jail terms are usually no longer than ten years, and those given life sentences can ask to have their sentences changed to fixed terms after ten years. Sweden was the first European country to use electronic tags for criminals and tries to avoid long prison sentences by using community-based measures. These methods have helped reduce reoffending rates.

The reoffending rate in Sweden is between 30 and 40% over three years, which is about half the rate in the UK. In Sweden, children under 15 cannot be held criminally responsible, and no one under 21 can get a life sentence. This helps keep the number of prisoners low.

A big reason for the lower number of prisoners may be the support provided after release. The government offers programs to help ex-prisoners with drug, alcohol, or violence issues. About 4,500 volunteers also help support these individuals.

Peter Soderlund, who spent nearly three years in prison for drug and weapons offenses, now runs a group called X-Cons Sweden. He was helped by Kris, an organization run by former prisoners. Both groups aim to help prisoners reintegrate into society after release.

In Sweden, the belief is that rehabilitation is key. While some prisoners may not change, Gustafsson believes that most want to and should be supported in doing so.

Swedish prisons are known for being nice and new. But are they too easy?

In November 2013, Nils Oberg, who runs Swedish prisons, said four prisons will close. There are fewer people in prison, just over 4,500. This happened even though crime did not go down. Between 2011 and 2012, the number of prisoners dropped by 6%. Oberg is not sure why there are fewer prisoners, but he hopes it is because the prisons are doing a good job helping people stop breaking the law again.

Kenneth Gustafsson, who runs a big prison in Sweden, says things have changed since he started working there in 1978. Prisons used to be very nice, maybe too nice. After some prisoners escaped in 2004, they made the prisons safer.

In Sweden, people usually do not stay in prison for more than ten years. They use small punishments instead of long stays in prison. This helps stop people from breaking the law again.

About 30 to 40% of people in Sweden break the law again after getting out of prison. In the UK, about twice as many do. Kids under 15 cannot be punished for crimes. Also, no one under 21 can get life in prison. They try to keep young people out of prison.

Sweden offers lots of help after people leave prison. The government has a program to help people with drug, alcohol, or violence problems. About 4,500 volunteers help by being friends and giving support.

In Sweden, they think it is important to help people change. Most prisoners want to change, and the prisons try to help them.

You've been at the office for eight hours. The main work is finished, and what's left can wait till tomorrow. Many workers would think about going home.

But for millions of Japanese workers, leaving early could be seen as disloyal. For years, the government let companies keep workers very busy. Now, the government wants to change this overwork culture. They are thinking about making it a rule that workers must take at least five paid days off each year.

Japanese workers usually get around 18.5 paid days off per year, just two less than the global average, with a minimum of ten days plus fifteen national holidays. However, most workers only use about nine of their 18.5 days. In Britain, a two-week summer break is common, but in Japan, a short trip is seen as a luxury.

By the end of the decade, the government hopes workers will use more days off, like British workers who take an average of 20 days and French workers who take 25.

Japan’s tough work culture helped it become an economic power, but it left little time for personal life. This has led to a low birth rate and population decline. Workers are getting sick from stress, and some are dying from overwork, called karoshi.

Studies show that longer hours don't always mean more productivity. About 22% of Japanese workers put in more than 49 hours a week, compared to 16% in the U.S., 11% in France, and 11% in Germany. South Korea has even higher rates, with 35% of workers working long hours.

Erika Sekiguchi works 14 hours a day and rarely takes her paid holidays. She says no one else does either. Yuu Wakebe, a health ministry worker, puts in 100 hours of overtime a month. He says the pressure to match coworkers' hours is intense.

This fear of standing out leads to stress, early deaths, and suicides. Official data shows about 200 people die each year from karoshi.

Prime Minister Shinzo Abe, who doesn’t take long breaks himself, says companies ask too much of their workers and that working hours in Japan are too long.

You worked eight hours at the office. Most people go home after finishing their work. But in Japan, many workers stay late because they think leaving on time looks bad.

The Japanese government wants to change this. They want workers to take at least five paid days off each year.

Japanese workers can have 18.5 paid days off a year. Companies must give them at least ten paid days off plus 15 national holidays. But most workers only take nine days off.

In Britain, workers usually take 20 days off, and in France, it's 25 days. The Japanese government hopes workers will start taking more days off like they do in other countries.

Japanese workers are known for working hard, but they have little time for family or other things. This leads to fewer babies being born and a smaller population. Many workers get sick or even die from too much work.

About 22% of Japanese workers work more than 49 hours a week. In the U.S., it's 16%, and in France and Germany, it's 11%.

Erika Sekiguchi, a 36-year-old worker, works 14 hours a day and took only eight days off in 2014. Yuu Wakebe, who works at the health ministry, does 100 hours of unpaid overtime a month.

Many workers fear others will think they aren't working hard enough if they take time off. This causes stress, sickness, and sometimes death. About 200 people in Japan die each year from heart attacks and strokes due to long working hours.

British author David Mitchell recently finished a special book. It won't be read by anyone until 2114. He wrote it late one night before going to Norway. 

Mitchell's book is part of a project called the Future Library. In 2014, 1,000 trees were planted in a forest near Oslo. Every year, a different writer gives a new text. These texts will be printed on paper made from these trees in 2114. The first writer was Margaret Atwood in 2015.

Each writer goes to the forest to give their book in a short ceremony. Mitchell thinks this project gives hope for the future. He believes it shows that people will still care about books and trees in 100 years.

Mitchell enjoyed writing this book because he didn’t worry about what others would think since he won’t be alive to see the reaction. He named his book "From Me Flows What You Call Time." During the ceremony, he read a short story and a poem by William Wordsworth.

The book is now kept in a special room in Oslo’s new library. It will stay there until 2114 when all the books will be printed together.

People often talk a lot about David Mitchell's books. But this time, he isn't worried about what they say. He finished his newest book late one night. Then he went to the airport to fly to Norway. No one will read this book until 2114.

Mitchell is the second person to join the Future Library project. In 2014, they planted 1,000 trees in a forest near Oslo. The first writer, Margaret Atwood, gave her book to the project in 2015. Every year, a writer will add a book. People can only read these books in 2114 when the trees are used to make paper for the books.

Each writer goes to a special place in the forest to give their book to the project. Mitchell thinks this project gives hope. He believes it shows that in 100 years, there will still be trees, books, and people who read them.

Writing this book made Mitchell feel free because he won't be alive to know if people like it or not. He usually spends a lot of time making his writing perfect, but this time he wrote quickly. The first part of the book is perfect, but he didn't have time to fix the last part.

Mitchell's book is called "From Me Flows What You Call Time." He only shared the title during a small event in the forest. He says the book is longer than he thought it would be.

In the forest, Mitchell read a short story and a poem. The trees will grow for 98 more years before they make the books.

Mitchell knows it might seem silly to think people will care about his writing in the future. But he likes working hard on something no one will praise him for.

His book is now sealed and kept with Atwood's book in a room in Oslo's new library. Mitchell says it feels like he dropped a coin in a river.

An octopus named Inky escaped from the National Aquarium in New Zealand. Inky left his tank when the lid was not closed properly. He climbed out of the tank at night when no one was around. Then, he traveled across the floor and went down a 50-meter drainpipe that led to the sea.

Rob Yarrell, who manages the aquarium, said octopuses often escape because they are curious. Inky probably wanted to explore. One idea is that Inky moved across the floor for about three or four meters before going into the drainpipe. It is also possible that Inky squeezed into an open pipe at the top of his tank, which led to the drain.

When the staff arrived the next day and saw Inky was gone, they were surprised. Yarrell does not plan to look for Inky. Reiss Jenkinson, who takes care of the exhibits, believes Inky was not stolen. He knows octopuses can escape through small spaces.

Octopuses can fit into tiny spaces because they have no bones. They are also smart and can use tools. For example, another octopus at a different center used to visit other tanks at night to steal crabs. Another one broke a world record for opening a jar.

Inky was found by a local fisherman in a fishing pot. He looked rough and had short arms because he had been fighting with fish. Inky was about the size of a rugby ball and was very friendly. He was more popular than the aquarium's other octopus, Blotchy, who is smaller.

The aquarium does not plan to increase security because they do not think this will happen again. However, they now know more about what octopuses can do. If another octopus is brought in, they might keep it. There is a chance Inky could come back.

Rob Yarrell, who works at the aquarium, said octopuses often escape because they are curious. Inky probably wanted to explore. He likely traveled about three or four meters across the floor before finding the drainpipe that led to the ocean.

Yarrell thinks Inky wasn't stolen because the aquarium has strong security. Octopuses can fit into tiny spaces and are very smart. They can even use tools. For example, one octopus used to visit another tank at night to steal crabs and then go back to its own tank.

Inky was found by a fisherman and brought to the aquarium. He was sick when he arrived but got better. Inky was friendly and popular at the aquarium. Now that Inky is gone, the staff will be more careful. If another octopus is found, the aquarium might take it. Yarrell hopes Inky might come back someday.

Why do they do it? Future elite football referees smile when asked this question. This season, there has been a lot of criticism of referees. Even some former referees are complaining about the standards. Referees support each other a lot.

So why do they keep doing it? Why drive around the country for hundreds of hours? Why enforce rules that sometimes upset people? Why try to climb the ladder to get the chance to referee matches on TV in front of millions of people who closely watch and judge their every move?

Lee Swabey, a respected referee, gives a clue after a match where Grimsby beat Woking. He got twenty-two handshakes from players and praise from both managers. This means a lot to him. He loves the feeling of a smooth game and wouldn't spend so much time away from his family if refereeing didn't mean the world to him.

Swabey is watched by the Professional Game Match Officials Limited (PGMOL), especially by its chief, Mike Riley, and his colleague Steve Dunn. They look at every move the officials make.

Another referee, John Brooks, also wants to reach the Premier League. He had to cancel a match due to a frozen pitch. This kind of situation helps him gain experience for more important games. Clubs often don't want to postpone matches because they have to pay staff without getting gate money.

Brooks called his coach for advice and made the right decision. He received 95 pounds for his time, showing that referees don't do it for the money.

Brooks, like Swabey, faces disappointment. He wishes people understood the effort they put in. He knows he must stay focused and not worry about past decisions.

Former referees say today's referees have better support, education, and tools than they did. Brooks has a coach and a sports psychologist, Liam Slack, to help him mentally and physically.

Technology is also seen as helpful by former referees. They want anything that can minimize mistakes and make referees more effective on the pitch.

Why do people want to be football referees? Top referees smile when asked this. Some old referees say things are not as good now. Referees always help each other.

Why do referees drive long distances and work hard to be on TV where many people watch and say mean things? Lee Swabey looks very happy after a game where Grimsby beat Woking 2-1. He likes getting handshakes from players after a good game. He says it is important to him even though he misses his family.

Swabey is a new referee that the PGMOL thinks is good. PGMOL's boss, Mike Riley, and Steve Dunn watched him. A few weeks ago, Riley, Dunn, and Peter Jones watched another young referee, John Brooks, at a level-5 match. Brooks hopes to referee in the Premier League someday.

At Brooks' match, the field was too cold, so he had to cancel the game. He called his coach for help and made the right choice. The club paid the referees £95, showing they do not do it for money.

Brooks knows people will say mean things about him. He wishes people understood how hard referees work. Sometimes referees make people unhappy, but if they do not like that, they should not be referees.

Old referees say new referees have better help now. When Riley was young, he had to buy his own books. Now, Brooks has a coach who talks to him every week and helps him get better. He also has a sports psychologist and a plan to run 11km in a game.

New technology helps referees do a better job. A bad decision can stay with a referee forever.

Behind the bright lights and mirrors, cameras watch you. If you pick up a boot, a camera makes sure you don't put it in your bag. When you enter a department store, you are watched. New technology focuses less on catching shoplifters and more on knowing your age, gender, and shopping habits.

A few months ago, IT company Computer Sciences Corporation (CSC) reported that about 30% of stores use facial recognition technology to track customers. This technology identifies people by analyzing and comparing their faces to a database. Devices like Intel RealSense cameras can analyze expressions and the brands of clothes someone wears.

Joe Jensen, an Intel spokesman, says the goal of using RealSense technology in shops is not to create detailed records of specific people's lives but to build general models of people’s lifestyles and shopping habits. They don’t need to know a specific customer; they need to know that certain shoppers have certain traits and what those people tend to do.

By combining recognition technology with databases of past customer behavior, stores can predict what a person might do in the shop. For example, if a woman walks quickly toward the sock section, the store can predict she wants to buy socks and show her targeted ads for socks.

This is similar to how the online world works. If you search for something on Amazon, you'll see ads for similar products on other websites. But it's harder to bring these systems into the real world because people react differently to cameras than to browser cookies.

Hoxton Analytics, a team of data scientists in London, created a technology that uses machine learning and artificial intelligence to categorize people based on the shoes they wear. By analyzing the style and size of people's footwear, the system can identify a customer's gender with 75-80% accuracy.

Owen McCormack, CEO of Hoxton Analytics, says the focus on shoes was partly a reaction to facial recognition. He thought, "Why not look at the clothes someone is wearing?" If you see a picture of someone's body, you can guess their gender. But pointing a camera at someone's chest or hips feels as intrusive as facial recognition. So, they decided to focus on shoes instead.

Many people find in-store tracking creepy. Stores and data scientists aim to gather information without seeming intrusive. McCormack argues that no personal information is collected. Shops already do many invasive things, but people aren't aware of it. If shops know whether a customer is male or female, their advertising becomes more efficient. If everyone in the shop is male, they can advertise PlayStations instead of hairdryers.

Stores want the same information that online shops collect. Online, you get a pop-up asking you to accept cookies. But in physical shops, it's hard to ask for consent the same way.

Younger people, who grew up with online shopping, don't see online advertising as so intrusive. According to the CSC report, 72% of people aged 55 or older said they were very uncomfortable with these technologies in physical shops. Only 51% of 16-24-year-olds felt uncomfortable.

Are younger people more open because they are familiar with digital technology, or do they trust organizations offering free services? Is this kind of technology always creepy, or does it depend? In any case, there are more eyes between the shelves, and they care a lot about what you're wearing.

When you go into a big store, cameras watch you. They check if you put things in your bag. These cameras follow you around. Now, new cameras learn about your age, gender, and how you shop.

A report by a tech company called CSC says that about 30% of stores use cameras to see faces. This helps them know more about shoppers. Joe Jensen from Intel says the goal is not to know each person but to understand what kind of people come to the store and what they like.

The cameras help stores guess what you might do. For example, if a woman walks fast toward the socks, the store can show her sock ads. This is like how websites show you ads after you search for something.

Another company, Hoxton Analytics, made a system that guesses your gender by looking at your shoes. It can guess correctly about 75-80% of the time. Owen McCormack, the boss of Hoxton Analytics, says they wanted to avoid using face cameras because it feels too private. Instead, they look at shoes.

Many people feel uncomfortable with stores watching them. Older people are more worried than younger ones. The report shows that 72% of people over 55 feel very uncomfortable, while only 51% of people aged 16-24 feel uncomfortable.

Stores want to know more about shoppers, like online stores do. But in real shops, it feels different because no one asks if it's okay to watch you.

Insects are not often thought of as food in most parts of the world, but this is changing. In 2013, there will be efforts to show that eating insects is okay and to sell them in supermarkets.

In April, there will be a festival in London called Pestival 2013. This festival will talk about eating insects. A restaurant run by the Nordic Food Lab, the team behind the famous Danish restaurant Noma, will be there. Noma was named the world's best restaurant for three years. Chef Ren Redzepi says that ants taste like lemon and that a mix of fermented grasshoppers and moth larvae tastes like a strong fish sauce. Bee larvae can be used to make a sweet mayonnaise without eggs. Scientists keep finding new ways to use insects.

In March, a BBC documentary will show food writer Stefan Gates eating deep-fried locusts and barbecued spiders. The goal is to show that there are real benefits to eating insects for the environment.

The United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) has been working since 2011 to encourage eating and farming insects in southeast Asia and Africa. About two billion people already eat insects regularly. In 2012, the FAO listed 1,909 types of edible insects and plans a big meeting about this food source in 2013.

There are 40 tons of insects, so they won't become endangered. Redzepi says that eating bugs is normal in some places and asks why not in the Western world. He believes that nothing is inedible.

Insects are very important to life on Earth and are the most diverse group of creatures. Over the next 30 years, the world's population will grow to nine billion, putting more pressure on land, water, forests, and other resources. Meat costs are rising due to deforestation and methane from cows. Livestock farming produces 35% of the world's methane, 65% of nitrous oxide, and 9% of carbon dioxide.

Eating insects can help. They produce fewer gases, have high-quality protein, vitamins, and amino acids, and need less food than sheep, pigs, or chickens to produce the same amount of protein. They also produce fewer greenhouse gases and less ammonia than cows and can be raised on organic waste. China has large maggot farms, Zimbabwe has a successful caterpillar industry, and Laos received almost $500,000 from the FAO to develop an insect-harvesting project.

A study suggests that switching from pork and beef to crickets and locusts could reduce greenhouse gas emissions by up to 95%. Eating insects can also help the environment after we die, as they can break down our bodies.

In the West, people don't usually eat insects. But in other parts of the world, insects are an important food. In spring 2013, there was an effort to show that eating insects is not yucky. Soon, we might be able to buy insects at supermarkets.

In April, there was a festival in London called Pestival 2013. At the festival, there was a talk about eating insects. The Nordic Food Lab, a team from Scandinavia, had a restaurant there. This team worked with the Danish restaurant Noma, which was named the best restaurant in the world for three years by Restaurant magazine. Chef René Redzepi said ants taste like lemon, and grasshoppers and moth larvae taste like strong fish sauce. Bee larvae can be used to make a sweet mayonnaise without eggs. Scientists keep finding new ways to use insects.

A BBC documentary showed a food writer eating deep-fried locusts and barbecued spiders. The message is that eating insects is good for the environment. The UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) supports projects that teach people how to eat and farm insects in south-east Asia and Africa. About two billion people in these areas already eat insects. In 2012, the FAO listed 1,909 types of edible insects and planned a big meeting about insects as food in 2013.

There are lots of insects—40 tons for each person in the world—so they won’t run out. Redzepi said eating bugs is taboo in the West, but it's common in south-east Asia. He also said we eat honey, which is bee vomit.

Nordic Food Lab believes you can eat almost anything. Insects are very important to life on Earth. There are more than a million types of insects. Most people dislike them and often kill them.

In the next 30 years, the world’s population will grow to nine billion. One billion people already don’t have enough food. This growth will put more pressure on land, water, forests, and food supplies.

Meat costs more now, and making fields for cows destroys rainforests. Cows also make methane, a gas that harms the environment. Farming cows, pigs, and sheep makes a lot of greenhouse gases—35% of the planet’s methane, 65% of its nitrous oxide, and 9% of the carbon dioxide.

Eating insects is better because they make less gas, have high-quality protein, vitamins, and amino acids, and need less food than sheep to make the same amount of protein. They can be grown on waste. China is building big maggot farms. Zimbabwe is growing caterpillars, and Laos is working on an insect-harvesting project. Eating crickets and locusts instead of pork and beef could reduce greenhouse gas emissions by up to 95%.

The world's top energy experts say coal might become as big as oil in the next five years, which could be very bad for the environment. One reason for this is that the United States is using much more shale gas, making coal cheaper and more popular in other parts of the world.

Maria van der Hoeven, who leads the International Energy Agency (IEA), says coal use keeps growing every year and could beat oil within ten years if nothing changes. Coal is easy to find and cheap to get out of the ground, and China and India will use a lot more of it in the next five years. By 2017, the world will burn 1.2 billion more tons of coal each year than it does now.

Coal causes a lot of pollution and is the worst fossil fuel for climate change. Old power plants that burn coal without special cleaning equipment can also release sulfur, which causes acid rain, and other harmful pollutants like mercury and soot.

Van der Hoeven says that unless there is a high cost for using coal or cheaper gas, coal use will keep rising. In the U.S., more shale gas has lowered coal use, reduced pollution, and saved people money on electricity. She thinks other places like Europe and China should look at this example.

If nothing is done, the world will face more climate change because of the growing use of coal.

Coal may become as big as oil for energy in the next five years. This could be very bad for the Earth's climate.

One reason coal use is going up is because the U.S. is using more shale gas.

New research from the International Energy Agency (IEA) shows that people around the world are using more coal. In the U.S., shale gas is more popular than coal. Since the U.S. uses less coal, coal costs less everywhere. This makes coal more popular, even in Europe.

Maria van der Hoeven, who leads the IEA, said that coal use keeps growing every year. If nothing changes, coal will be used as much as oil in ten years.

Coal is easy to find and cheap to get. The IEA says China and India will use more coal in the next five years. India might use more coal than the U.S. China buys the most coal, and Indonesia sells the most coal.

The IEA says the world will burn 1.2 billion more tons of coal each year by 2017.

Coal makes the most pollution, which makes climate change worse. Old power stations that use coal make a lot of pollution. Coal also makes acid rain and other types of pollution.

Van der Hoeven says we should make coal cost more so people use cleaner energy like wind or solar power. Cheaper gas is the only way to use less coal. This happened in the U.S. because they make more shale gas.

Van der Hoeven said, "The U.S. shows that better gas markets can lower coal use, cut pollution, and lower electricity costs. Europe, China, and others should do this too."

If we don't do anything, climate change will get worse.

Many people don't get enough sleep. Dr. Paul Kelley from Oxford University suggests that schools should change their start times to match the natural body clocks of students. This would help students perform better in school and stay healthier. Not getting enough sleep can lead to problems like diabetes, depression, obesity, and weak immune systems.

Dr. Kelley found that young children naturally wake up around 6:30 AM, teenagers around 8:00 AM, and older teens around 9:00 AM. Starting school early works well for young kids but not for older students. He thinks it would be better for older teens to start school at 11:00 AM or later.

Teenagers' body clocks are controlled by light, not by trying to force them to go to bed earlier. Light tells the brain when to wake up and when to sleep. For example, waking up a teenager at 7:00 AM feels like waking up a 50-year-old at 4:30 AM.

People of different ages need different amounts of sleep. Teenagers and young adults lose about two hours of sleep each night, while those in their late 20s and early 30s lose about one and a half hours. People in their 50s usually get enough sleep.

The typical 9-to-5 workday suits older workers but not younger ones. Dr. Kelley suggests that workplaces should also have different start times based on age. This could improve people's health, mood, and job performance. There would likely be fewer accidents and no rush hour traffic if everyone started work at different times.

Parents often struggle to wake up their teenagers, causing stress for everyone. Dr. Kelley himself is 67 years old and wakes up naturally around 6:00 AM, like a 10-year-old child.

Many people do not get enough sleep. Dr. Paul Kelley from Oxford University thinks schools should start classes later to help students feel better and do better in exams. Not getting enough sleep can cause health problems like diabetes, depression, and obesity.

For kids around ten years old, their bodies want to wake up at about 6:30 AM. At sixteen, it's 8:00 AM. By eighteen, it's 9:00 AM. So, schools should start later for older students. Starting school at 11:00 AM or later might be good for older teens.

Kelley says telling teens to go to bed earlier won't help. Our bodies use light to decide when to sleep. The eyes send signals to the brain to control sleep.

Not only students, but also workers could benefit from starting work later. People between 14 and 24 lose more than two hours of sleep each night. People between 24 and 35 lose about one and a half hours. This continues until about age 55 when it balances out.

Kelley suggests workplaces should have different start times. Older people could start at 8:00 AM, people in their 30s at 10:00 AM, and young workers at 11:00 AM. This could reduce traffic jams and make people healthier and happier.

Kelley starts work just after 6:00 AM because he is 67 years old. He says it makes his day easier.

Felix Baumgartner, also known as Fearless Felix, jumped from a height of 24 miles above New Mexico. Before jumping, mission control wished him luck. Ten minutes later, he landed safely, reaching speeds of 725 miles per hour. He broke three world records: the highest altitude skydive, the highest altitude manned balloon flight, and becoming the first person to break the sound barrier in free fall at Mach 1.24.

Baumgartner wore a special suit to protect him from extreme pressure changes. Without it, his blood could have boiled, and his lungs might have exploded. He said his main goal was to return safely.

The jump took place on a sunny day. A giant balloon, measuring 30 million square feet, carried Baumgartner up. At the bottom of the balloon was a capsule where he sat in his suit. As he reached the right height, he checked 40 items with his mentor, Joe Kittinger, the previous record holder for the highest altitude manned balloon flight.

Baumgartner faced a problem with his visor fogging up, but they decided to continue. Over 8 million people watched the event live on YouTube. The trip up took two and a half hours, and the descent lasted just over four minutes.

Dr. Jonathan Clark, whose wife died in the Columbia space shuttle disaster, was Baumgartner's top medical advisor. The success of the mission suggests that astronauts might survive high-altitude emergencies by jumping from their spacecraft.

Baumgartner, known for daring stunts, practiced twice before this jump. He aimed to break five records and spent seven years planning the event, sponsored by Red Bull. Kittinger, who jumped from 19 miles in 1960, advised Baumgartner during the ascent.

After the jump, Baumgartner said he wanted to inspire others and hoped someone would break his record soon. His most exciting moment was standing outside the capsule. He thanked Mike Todd, the life support engineer, who was thrilled to see him safe.

Baumgartner promised this would be his last jump and planned to settle down with his girlfriend, Nicole Oetl, and fly helicopters on rescue missions in the US and Austria.

Felix Baumgartner jumped from very high above New Mexico. He was 24 miles up in the sky. Mission control wished him luck. Baumgartner jumped and fell for ten minutes. He went as fast as 725 miles per hour. He broke three world records. He was the first person to go faster than sound when jumping. His team cheered for him.

Baumgartner wore a special suit to protect him from big changes in air pressure. Without the suit, his blood would boil and his lungs would burst. He wanted to get back safely. He said, "Sometimes you have to go up really high to see how small you are."

He also set records for the highest balloon flight and the highest skydive. On a sunny day, he rode up in a big balloon. The balloon was 30 million square feet and very thin. In the capsule below, Baumgartner sat in his suit.

At the right height, he checked 40 things with Joe Kittinger. Kittinger had the old record for the highest balloon flight. Baumgartner had trouble seeing because of his visor. They decided to keep going. Over 8 million people watched online.

It took two and a half hours to go up. The sky turned dark. Coming down was quick. Three cameras on his suit showed his fall and when his parachute opened.

Before this, Baumgartner jumped from buildings, mountains, and into a deep cave. He practiced twice for this jump. He jumped from 71,000 feet and 97,000 feet. His big jump was near Roswell, known for UFOs.

He tried to break five records: first human to break the sound barrier, highest jump, highest balloon flight, longest fall, and biggest balloon. Kittinger, who jumped from 19 miles up in 1960, helped Baumgartner.

When asked what he would do next, Baumgartner said he wanted to inspire young people. He hoped to help someone break his record. He said the best part was standing outside the capsule. He felt like Mike Todd's son when Todd smiled after he landed safely.

Baumgartner said this was his last jump. He plans to fly helicopters for rescue work in the US and Austria.

Barack Obama flew back to Washington and his office on Wednesday after winning the election and giving a speech in Chicago. He asked the country to support him. Unlike in 2008, he may not have a smooth start to his new term.

John Boehner, the Republican leader, and Harry Reid, the Democratic leader, both said they want to work together to fix the economy. However, there might be big fights between the White House and Congress.

Obama won easily against his opponent, Mitt Romney, but the election showed that America is still divided. Obama's second term officially starts in January, but he began it on Wednesday. He wants to do better in his second term and leave a lasting impact.

Obama plans to focus on economic recovery, immigration, education, climate change, and foreign policy issues like Iran and Israel-Palestine. He won more than 270 electoral votes and got more votes overall.

Boehner and Reid both said they want to find common ground to help the economy and create jobs. However, they disagree on how to do this. The Republicans want to keep military spending, while the Democrats want to cut it. Obama wants to raise taxes on families making over $250,000, but Boehner does not agree.

Romney only won North Carolina, while Obama won several other key states. In his speech, Obama talked about the need for electoral reform and praised his family and Vice President Joe Biden. He said Americans are not as divided as their politics suggest and that they are the United States of America.

Obama mentioned his plans for changing the tax code, fixing immigration, and dealing with climate change. Before this, Romney called Obama to concede the election and wished him success. Despite a slow economy and high unemployment, Americans chose not to change presidents. It would have been disappointing if the first black presidency had failed.

Barack Obama flew back to Washington and his office on Wednesday after winning the election. He gave a speech in Chicago asking everyone to work together.

John Boehner, who leads the Republican Party, and Harry Reid, who leads the Democratic Party in the Senate, both think it's important to work together to fix the money problems in the country. But they might fight a lot about it.

Obama won against Mitt Romney. Many people liked Obama, but some were not happy with how he did in his first four years. Now, Obama wants to do better and work on things like money problems, helping people who come from other countries, schools, the weather, and problems in other countries like Iran and Israel.

Boehner said both sides need to agree on ways to help the country grow and make more jobs. Reid said they should work together to solve problems.

There will be trouble because the Republicans and Democrats disagree on some things. The Republicans want to spend the same amount on the army, but the Democrats want to spend less. Obama wants richer families to pay more taxes, but Boehner does not agree.

In his speech, Obama talked about long lines of people waiting to vote and said changes are needed. He spoke in a powerful and emotional way, like he did in 2008. He thanked his family and Joe Biden, his helper.

Obama said, "We are not as different as our politics show. We are the United States of America."

Sweden is the best country for older people, while Afghanistan is the worst. This is based on the first global index on aging. The top five countries are Sweden, Norway, Germany, the Netherlands, and Canada. Surprisingly, the United States is only eighth, and the United Kingdom is thirteenth. Sri Lanka ranks 36th, much higher than Pakistan at 89th, even though both have similar GDPs. Bolivia and Mauritius do better than expected, while Brazil and China rank relatively high, but India and Russia are much lower.

Mark Gorman, director of HelpAge International, says that history matters. Top countries like Sweden had pensions for everyone before becoming wealthy. Older people in Sri Lanka benefit from good education and healthcare. Countries must invest in old-age issues.

The index, created with the UN Population Fund, covers 91 countries and 89% of the world's older people. By 2050, there will be two billion people aged 60 and over, making up more than a fifth of the world’s population. Developing countries are aging the fastest. Over two-thirds of older people live in poor countries, and by 2050, this will be about four-fifths. Countries like Jordan, Laos, Mongolia, Nicaragua, and Vietnam are aging quickly but rank low, suggesting they need to focus more on supporting older people.

Women generally live longer than men. For every 84 men aged 60 and over, there are 100 women. Women often face disadvantages in old age due to lack of paid work, less decision-making power, and vulnerability to violence.

The report says that population aging doesn't always lead to higher healthcare costs. Long-term investments in education and healthcare for older people are important. Bolivia, one of the poorest countries, has good policies for older people, including free healthcare and a pension for everyone.

Chile and Costa Rica have helped their aging populations with good healthcare introduced decades ago. Good education systems benefit older people later in life. The Philippines and Armenia have benefited from past educational reforms. South Korea ranks low partly because it only recently introduced a pension.

The aging index uses 13 indicators under four areas: income security, healthcare, employment and education, and a positive environment. Some indicators, like pension income coverage and life expectancy at 60, have more weight. Professor Sir Richard Jolly says the index helps understand the needs and opportunities of older people worldwide.

Sweden is the best place for older people, while Afghanistan is the worst. This is from the first big study about getting older around the world. Sweden, Norway, Germany, the Netherlands, and Canada are the top five. 

The United States is number eight, and the United Kingdom is number thirteen. Sri Lanka is number thirty-six, much higher than Pakistan at eighty-nine. Bolivia and Mauritius are doing better than expected. Brazil and China are high, but India and Russia are lower.

Mark Gorman from HelpAge International says history matters. Countries like Sweden started helping older people when they weren't as rich. Sri Lanka's older people have good education and healthcare. Countries need to use their money to help older people.

The study looks at ninety-one countries with most of the world's older people. By 2050, there will be two billion people sixty and over, which is more than one in five people. Developing countries are getting older fast. Most older people live in poor countries, and by 2050, almost four out of five will be in these countries.

Countries like Jordan, Laos, Mongolia, Nicaragua, and Vietnam are getting older quickly but are in the bottom half of the list. They need to help their older people more. Women usually live longer than men. In 2012, for every 84 men over sixty, there were 100 women.

Good education and healthcare are important for older people. Bolivia is poor but has good plans for older people, like free healthcare and pensions. Chile and Costa Rica have good healthcare too. Education helps older people understand pension papers. The Philippines and Armenia have good schools. South Korea is low because it just started pensions.

All countries need to do more to help older people.

Clay Cockrell works in an office near 1 Central Park West, close to the Trump International Hotel and Tower. He holds therapy sessions in Central Park. Cockrell used to work on Wall Street but now helps rich people in New York.

He walks through Central Park and Battery Park to help very wealthy people, often called the "1% of the 1%." These people sometimes feel their problems aren't real, but they are. They feel guilty about being rich, scared to show their wealth, and often feel alone.

Since the financial crisis and movements like Occupy Wall Street, things have gotten worse. People like Jamie Traeger-Muney, who helps wealthy people, say the media makes rich people feel they must hide their wealth.

Barbara Nusbaum, a money psychology expert, says it's hard to talk about having lots of money. It's easier to say you're broke than to admit you have a lot of money. This makes rich people keep their lives private and spend time with other rich people who understand them.

In the U.S., the number of very wealthy people has grown. By 2014, there were 10.1 million households with over $1 million, not counting their homes. About 1.3 million households had over $5 million, and 142,000 had over $25 million.

After the 2008 financial crisis, the rich became more isolated. They worry if their friends like them for themselves or just their money. This fear makes it hard to trust others.

A study by the Gates Foundation and Boston College found that even the richest people face real problems. Many hide their wealth to avoid judgment. Rich people often feel misunderstood when they talk about their struggles.

Cockrell says that being rich doesn't mean you don't have problems. Money isn't everything, and your issues are real, no matter how much you have.

Clay Cockrell works in an office near the Trump International Hotel and Tower. He often walks and talks with his patients in Central Park. Cockrell used to work on Wall Street but now he helps people as a therapist.

He walks and talks with some of New York's richest people. These very rich people sometimes feel their problems aren't real, but they are.

Since the big money problems in 2008, it has been harder for rich people. Groups like Occupy Wall Street talk about the difference between rich and poor people. This makes rich people feel they need to hide or feel bad.

Barbara Nusbaum, who knows a lot about money and feelings, says rich people feel scared about how others react to them. It is hard to talk about being rich. Rich people keep much of their life private.

Because of this, rich people spend time with other rich people who understand them.

In 2014, there were 10.1 million U.S. homes with over $1 million, not counting their house. There were 1.3 million homes worth over $5 million and 142,000 homes worth over $25 million.

After 2008, it got worse for rich people. They worry if their friends like them or just their money.

A woman whose husband has about $80 million says being rich stops her from making close friends. Many rich people hide their wealth because they fear others will judge them badly.

Cockrell says rich people often make a mistake by letting money be the most important thing in their lives. He tells them that even if they are rich, they still have problems and money isn't everything.

Takahito Iguchi thinks Google Glasses aren't stylish enough. There's a website showing people wearing them look silly or arrogant. Iguchi hopes this could be Google's weakness. He is making a new type of augmented reality glasses called Telepathy One. These glasses are more like a piece of metal with a camera and a small projector. They were shown in Austin, Texas, and got $5 million in funding.

Telepathy One is simpler than Google Glass. While Google Glass lets you browse the web, read emails, and take pictures, Telepathy One focuses on sharing images and videos in real-time. You can post photos and videos from what you see directly to Facebook or send them as emails. You can also talk to friends through video calls.

Iguchi believes these glasses will help people connect better. He has worked in Japanese technology for 20 years. He thinks some people might not like the futuristic look, but he dreams of a world where everyone understands each other. With Telepathy One, you can learn more about others before talking to them.

Telepathy One is much smaller than Google, but Iguchi isn’t worried. He works in San Francisco, in a converted warehouse. He believes even small teams can win against big companies. When he was young, Japanese tech was dominant, like the Sony Walkman. Now, he’s in Silicon Valley to compete.

Tokyo is rich in fashion and culture but is isolated. Silicon Valley is diverse and global. The hardware for Telepathy One will be made in Japan, while software engineers in the U.S. will develop its apps.

Making the prototype was easy, but presenting it to the world is harder. Top manufacturers want to work with him because they have the technology but struggle to sell it. Products need a good story, like Apple’s iPod slogan "1,000 songs in your pocket."

Iguchi has confidence like Steve Jobs but sometimes struggles to be understood because of his thick Japanese accent. This inspired his idea for Telepathy One. When he visited London, he met an Airbnb host and became friends after a long conversation. He thinks Telepathy One could speed up this process of understanding.

He hopes seeing someone else's viewpoint through these glasses will help people understand each other better. As a student, he studied philosophy and learned coding. One day, he realized everything can be coded and shared between humans, which could end wars.

Takahito Iguchi from Japan does not think Google Glasses are cool. People wearing them look funny or proud, or both. There is even a picture of a big, naked man wearing them in the shower. Iguchi hopes this is a weakness for Google. He made some glasses that look better and are more Japanese.

His glasses are not really glasses; they are a piece of metal with a camera and a tiny projector. They are called Telepathy One. After showing them in Texas, he got $5 million from investors. Like Google Glass, you can buy Telepathy One in 2014.

You can post photos and videos on Facebook or send them as emails. You can also see and talk to a friend through a video image.

Iguchi says, "Telepathy One will help you get closer to your friends and family." He has worked in Japanese technology for 20 years. "I have a dream that people will understand each other," he says. "When I go to London, I am a stranger. But I believe everyone wants to be understood."

When Iguchi grew up, Japanese technology was very popular. Now, he has to go to Silicon Valley to compete. "Tokyo is rich in fashion and culture, but it's isolated. When he visited London, he stayed with someone he did not know. "He was not my friend, but after talking for three hours, we became friends. Maybe Telepathy makes that quicker."

Iguchi hopes Telepathy One will help people understand each other better. As a student, he studied philosophy and learned to code. "One day, I realized everything is code. If code can be shared between humans, that will end all wars."

The vice-president of Google, Vint Cerf, warned that many digital materials like blogs, tweets, pictures, videos, and official documents could be lost forever. This is because the programs needed to view them might stop working over time. At a big science meeting, Cerf said that our early steps into the digital world could be lost to future historians. He calls this "bit rot," where old computer files become useless.

Cerf says we need to find ways to keep old software and hardware so that we can open very old files in the future. He worries that a lot of our history could be lost because so much of our daily life is recorded digitally, like emails and tweets. We don't want our digital lives to disappear. To prevent this, we must make sure that the digital things we create today can still be seen far into the future.

Bit rot means that accessing digital content in the future could be hard. While researchers are getting better at storing digital files for a long time, the programs and hardware needed to read them are always changing and becoming outdated.

Cerf warns that important political and historical documents could also be lost. For example, in the past, historians could find physical letters to learn about history. Today, those letters would be emails, and finding them in 100 years might be very hard.

Cerf says that historians usually try to save important material, but the importance of some documents is often understood only after many years. Researchers in Pittsburgh are trying to solve the bit rot problem by taking digital pictures of computer hard drives while running different software programs. These can then be used to recreate the original computer environment.

However, getting permission to copy and store software before it becomes unusable can be difficult. Cerf suggests that we need to think about how to preserve digital items for hundreds or thousands of years when we talk about things like copyright and patents.

The vice-president of Google, Vint Cerf, said that we might lose important digital stuff like blogs, tweets, pictures, videos, and emails forever. This is because the programs needed to open these files might not work in the future. Cerf talked about this at a big science meeting. He said we could become a "forgotten generation" due to "bit rot," which means old computer files can become useless.

Cerf thinks we should find ways to keep old software and hardware working so we can still read old files. He said lots of information about our lives is in digital form, like emails and tweets. If we don't do anything, we could lose a lot of our history.

Bit rot is when old computer files stop working. Cerf is worried because we digitize things to save them for a long time, but the programs and hardware to read those files might not last. He suggests printing out important photos if you want to keep them safe.

Old civilizations didn't have this problem because they wrote things down on paper. Future historians will need special software and sometimes hardware to read today's files like PDFs and Word documents.

This problem is real. In the 1980s, people saved documents on floppy disks and bought games on tapes. Now, we can only find the machines to read them in museums.

Cerf warns that we might lose important political and historical documents because of bit rot. For example, if Abraham Lincoln's letters were emails today, they might be hard to find in 100 years.

Historians usually try to save important documents, but sometimes they don't know how important something is until many years later. Researchers are trying to solve the bit rot problem by making a computer that can read old files.

To fix this, we might need to change laws about copying and storing software. We need to think about keeping documents safe for hundreds or thousands of years.

The day started with police raids at the Baur Au Lac hotel in Zurich and ended with 16 football officials being charged with corruption in the US. This includes five current or former members of FIFA's executive committee. Among them are Ricardo Teixeira, the former Brazilian federation chief, and his successor, Marco Polo Del Nero, who recently left the FIFA executive committee.

The US Department of Justice accused these 16 individuals of fraud and other crimes in a new 240-page report. Now, 27 people have been charged, including former FIFA executive committee members. US Attorney General Loretta Lynch said the betrayal of trust is outrageous and the corruption is completely unacceptable.

Swiss police arrested Juan Ángel Napout, the president of the South American football confederation, and Alfredo Hawit, the head of the North and Central American and Caribbean governing body. Hawit took over from Jeffrey Webb in May 2015, who was arrested as part of the US operation that caused a crisis in FIFA and led to Sepp Blatter stepping down. Jack Warner, Webb’s predecessor, was also arrested in May.

The Swiss Federal Office of Justice stated that the arrested individuals are in custody awaiting extradition. They are suspected of accepting bribes worth millions of dollars. Webb and Luis Bedoya, a former Colombian executive committee member, pleaded guilty in the US.

So far, eleven current and former members of FIFA's executive committee have been charged. The investigation claims $200 million in bribes, mostly from TV and marketing contracts, and also from FIFA's development programs.

Lynch warned that everyone involved in the corruption will be caught. Teixeira, the former son-in-law of the former FIFA president João Havelange, was charged along with Del Nero and José Maria Marin, who was charged in May.

In May 2015, fourteen men were charged. A few days later, Blatter won a fifth term as president but agreed to step down as the crisis worsened. He was then temporarily suspended, along with UEFA President Michel Platini, over a $1.3 million payment to Platini. If found guilty, both could face lifetime bans from FIFA.

Others charged include Rafael Salguero, a Guatemalan who left the executive committee in May; Eduardo Deluca, the former South American confederation Secretary General; Manuel Burga, the former Peruvian football federation president; and Carlos Chávez, Bolivia's football president, who is already in jail in Bolivia.

Lynch said the Department of Justice is committed to stopping corruption in international football because of the large scale of the schemes and the damage to international principles.

Issa Hayatou, the acting FIFA President, refused to comment on the recent arrests but said neither he nor FIFA is corrupt. He claimed that only a few bad individuals caused the crisis. Hayatou, who has been president of the Confederation of African Football for over 25 years, said many people in FIFA for over 20 or 30 years have not been accused of anything.

How long can you hold your breath? I tried it now. The first 30 seconds were easy. At 45 seconds, I wanted to stop, but I kept going. After a minute, my heart started pounding. I let out a tiny bit of air, which helped. Finally, I gave up after one minute and twelve seconds. I was pretty happy with that.

Holding your breath is really important in some sports, like freediving. In 2006, I filmed a show about the lungs for the BBC. I met Sam Amps, who was the captain of the UK freedive team. She taught me some exercises to help me hold my breath longer while swimming. By the end, I could do 90 seconds. Sam could do five minutes while swimming!

Sam told me she breathed slowly for a few minutes before each dive and took a big breath before diving. Training helped her hold her breath longer than most people.

Some people think we can hold our breath because we lived in water a long time ago. They say we can lower our heart rate to hold our breath longer. But this idea isn't true. We're not the only land animals that can hold our breath. Our heart rate doesn't drop when we hold our breath on land, but it does in cold water. This is called the mammalian diving reflex. It helps us not drown.

Our ability to hold our breath is now helpful in medicine. For breast cancer treatment, patients need to stay still for several minutes while getting radiation. Doctors found that giving patients oxygen-rich air before holding their breath lets them hold it for five and a half minutes. This helps the treatment work better.

When you breathe in, you pull your diaphragm down to make room for air. Holding your breath keeps your diaphragm pulled down. If you breathe in extra oxygen and less carbon dioxide before holding your breath, your diaphragm gets tired more slowly. But eventually, you have to breathe again because the signals from your diaphragm become too strong.

On land, our heart rate does not slow down when we hold our breath. But in cold water, it does slow down. This helps us stay underwater longer.

Doctors use breath-holding in breast cancer treatment. They point radiation at the tumor. If a patient can hold their breath for several minutes, doctors can give the full radiation dose at once. Most people can't do this, but doctors in Birmingham found that if patients breathe extra oxygen first, they can hold their breath for over five minutes.

To hold your breath, you need to keep your diaphragm flat. The diaphragm is the main muscle used for breathing. If you breathe extra oxygen first, your diaphragm won't get tired as fast. But eventually, you will need to breathe again because the diaphragm sends strong signals to breathe.

The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge won a privacy case against a French magazine. The magazine, Closer, took photos of the couple at a private house in France. The court said the magazine cannot sell or reuse these photos.

The court told Closer to give the couple the digital photos within 24 hours. If they do not, the magazine must pay 10,000 euros each day until they hand over the photos. The magazine's owner, Mondadori, must also pay 2,000 euros for legal costs.

The court said the photos were very private because they showed the couple partly undressed on a private terrace far from any public road. If Mondadori publishes similar photos in France again, they will be fined 10,000 euros each time.

The decision only applies to the 14 photos already published. The magazine's editor said they might have even more private photos.

The couple are happy with the decision but want the magazine and the photographer to face criminal charges for invading their privacy. Paris police started an investigation. In France, invading someone's privacy can lead to up to one year in jail and a fine of 45,000 euros.

The couple hope this will stop paparazzi from taking private photos of them in the future. The Irish Daily Star and an Italian magazine also published the photos.

Galina Zaglumyonova woke up in her apartment in Chelyabinsk because of a big explosion. The explosion broke her balcony windows and her plant pots. She saw a large trail of vapor in the sky and heard car alarms.

"I didn't know what happened," said Zaglumyonova. "There was a big explosion followed by smaller ones. I thought it was a plane crash."

Actually, it was a ten-ton meteorite that fell to Earth in fireballs right after sunrise.

Almost 1,200 people got hurt, mostly from glass broken by the sound wave made when the meteorite fell. No one died.

The meteorite entered the atmosphere at least 33,000 miles per hour and split into pieces between 18 and 32 miles above the ground, according to the Russian Academy of Sciences.

This event scared people in Chelyabinsk, a city with over one million people near Russia's Ural Mountains. Videos showed the meteorite pieces getting brighter as they fell. The vapor trail could be seen for hundreds of miles, even in Kazakhstan.

Tatyana Bets was working in a hospital clinic when the meteorite hit. "First, we felt the wind, then the room was filled with bright light, and we saw smoke in the sky," she said. "Then, after a few minutes, there were explosions."

Three craters were found. One was over six meters wide, and another piece of the meteorite went through a frozen lake.

In Chelyabinsk, schools and universities closed, and many workers went home early. About 200 children were hurt.

Many slightly injured people came to the clinic where Bets worked, mostly with cuts from broken glass. A student building was badly damaged, and many students were brought in. "There were many shocked girls. Some fainted," Bets said.

Over 100,000 square meters of glass broke, and 3,000 buildings were hit. The damage cost more than one billion roubles (20 million).

The meteorite event happened less than a day before asteroid 2012 DA14 was expected to pass close to Earth (about 17,510 miles), but experts said these events were unrelated.

Rumors spread quickly. Some reports said the meteorite was destroyed by Russian air defense units. Vladimir Zhirinovsky, a nationalist leader, claimed it was a US military test.

People started selling pieces of the meteorite online soon after the event.

President Vladimir Putin and Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev were informed. Putin met with the Emergency Situations Ministry head. Medvedev said, "It shows that not only economies but the whole planet is vulnerable."

Glastonbury Festival wants to stop using plastic water bottles to help the environment. Every year, about one million plastic bottles are used at the festival. The festival covers 900 acres and has 140,000 people attending.

The organizers are giving stainless-steel bottles to 2,000 workers and band members. They will also sell these bottles to festival-goers so they don't use plastic ones. There will be 400 water taps for people to fill their bottles.

Lucy Smith, who works on green issues for the festival, says the UK has good water, but many people still buy bottled water. In 2015, Glastonbury plans to replace all plastic cups and utensils with reusable ones.

There is a lot of plastic waste in the world and oceans, which hurts animals and plants. Glastonbury hopes to be the greenest outdoor music festival. They want people to use public transport or share rides to the festival.

Plastic bottles take a very long time to break down. Making and transporting them uses a lot of oil and creates pollution. Only one out of five bottles is recycled in the UK.

WaterAid will set up water stations with free refills. In 2013, almost half of the trash was recycled, and there will be 15,000 recycling bins in 2014.

The world knows him, London calls him its own, but Stratford-upon-Avon plans to celebrate William Shakespeare as their local hero in 2016. Shakespeare, born in 1564 and died 400 years ago in Stratford, is known as the Bard of Avon.

Paul Edmondson, head of learning and research at the Shakespeare Birthplace Trust, says Stratford was very important to Shakespeare. Many think he left Stratford to make money in London and only returned to die. However, Stratford is where he bought land, kept his books, and spent much of his time. This year, they want to show how important Stratford was to Shakespeare.

People around the world will celebrate the 400th anniversary of Shakespeare's death. Macbeth will open in Singapore, and Romeo and Juliet in Brussels. The Shakespeare's Globe theater is touring Hamlet to almost every country. In London, a special cinema with 37 screens will show each of Shakespeare’s plays.

Many theaters, like the National Theatre and the Royal Shakespeare Company, will celebrate this anniversary. They will perform the plays in different ways, from traditional to new styles. There will also be many talks, music shows, films, and art exhibitions.

There isn't much written proof about Shakespeare's life. His plays might not have survived if his friends hadn’t collected all the copies they could find and published them in the First Folio in 1623, seven years after his death.

Mark Rylance, an actor, loves the First Folio. Many of these rare books will be shown, including ones from the British Library and a recently found copy in France. An exhibition at Somerset House in London will show some of Shakespeare's most important documents, such as his will and four of his six known signatures.

Dominic Dromgoole, director of the Globe, jokingly says Shakespeare was a true Londoner. Stratford, however, insists that the town shaped and educated Shakespeare. They are fixing up his old schoolroom to open as a tourist spot.

Shakespeare bought a big house called New Place in Stratford, where he died. According to stories, he was born and died on April 23rd. Edmondson says that after buying New Place in 1597, Shakespeare likely wrote his later plays there. The Shakespeare Birthplace Trust calls New Place the highlight of the 400th anniversary celebrations.

Sadly, Shakespeare's house was torn down 300 years ago. A new house built on the site was also destroyed in 1759 by a priest named Francis Gastrell, who was upset about taxes and tourists. He even cut down Shakespeare's mulberry tree.

Recently, part of Shakespeare's kitchen was found in the old cellars. For the anniversary, the site will be shown with the foundations marked and the garden fixed up. Edmondson says without Stratford, there would have been no Shakespeare.

On one day in August, about 1 billion people, or one in seven people on Earth, used Facebook, according to Mark Zuckerberg, the founder. In ten years, Facebook has changed how people relate, do business, and get news. It has even changed the meaning of words like "friend" and "like."

Zuckerberg believes a more open and connected world is better. It helps build stronger relationships, creates more job opportunities, and strengthens society.

1. Facebook has changed the meaning of "friend." Now, "to friend" means to add someone on Facebook, and "unfriend" means to remove them. Facebook made sharing and liking more important.

2. People care less about privacy. Most young people share personal information on Facebook. They post photos, locations, and sometimes even their phone numbers. This lets them create an online image and fanbase. Brands use this information to target ads.

3. Facebook has created many jobs indirectly. Companies hire people to manage their Facebook presence. Advertisers pay a lot for access to user data. Facebook's ad revenue reached $3.32 billion, up 46%.

4. Facebook has helped organize protests. In Ukraine, Facebook was key in organizing half of the Euromaidan protesters. Many protesters trusted Facebook more than traditional media.

5. Facebook influences news. About 71% of 18- to 24-year-olds use the internet as their main news source, and 63% of all users. Facebook often breaks news first, especially on mobile devices. Journalists use Facebook to find information.

6. Facebook has grown beyond college students. In 2014, 56% of internet users aged 65 and older had a Facebook account. More than a third of users connect with people they've never met in person.

David Kirkpatrick, author of "The Facebook Effect," says Facebook will likely stay around for a long time. It has shown it can adapt and will remain a major player.

On one day in August, about 1 billion people used Facebook. That's one in seven people on Earth. Mark Zuckerberg, the founder, said this. In ten years, Facebook changed how people talk, do business, and even changed some words.

Zuckerberg wrote, "A more open and connected world is a better world."

Here are some ways Facebook changed things:

1. Facebook changed what "friend" means. Now, "to friend" means to add someone on Facebook. "Unfriend" means to remove someone. In real life, it's hard to end a friendship, but on Facebook, it's easy. Words like "share" and "like" became more important. School reunions aren't needed anymore because you can see updates about old friends online. Seeing an ex with a new partner isn't surprising because you've probably seen photos already.

In real life, some friends are closer than others, but on Facebook, all friends are equal. This might change how people learn to get along, according to Professor Robin Dunbar.

2. People care less about privacy. Most young people share personal details on Facebook. Ninety-one percent post photos, 71% post where they live, over half give email addresses, and one in five give phone numbers. More than 80% list their interests. But 60% let only friends see their profiles.

3. Facebook created many jobs. Companies use Facebook to understand customers better. They know who buys their products and what customers think. Advertisers pay a lot for this information. Facebook made $3.32 billion from ads. But Facebook can also hurt companies when angry customers post complaints.

4. Facebook helped organize protests. Half of the protesters in Ukraine used Facebook to get information. Many people there didn't trust traditional news.

5. Facebook shares and decides news. About 71% of young people and 63% of all users get news from the internet. A third of Facebook users post about politics. Most people first read news on Facebook or other social media on their phones.

Low-income countries will face the biggest problems from climate change over the next 100 years. They will see higher sea levels, stronger storms, hotter days and nights, less predictable rain, and longer, bigger heat waves, according to a new report.

A big UN report in 2007 said temperatures could go up by 6 degrees Celsius by the end of the century. Scientists now think this is unlikely, but temperatures are still expected to rise, maybe by 4 degrees Celsius. This could destroy crops and make life very hot in many cities.

As temperatures and ocean temperatures increase, tropical and subtropical areas will see big changes in yearly rainfall. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) report, released in Stockholm and online in September, says East Africa will have more short rainfalls, while West Africa will have heavier monsoons. Burma, Bangladesh, and India can expect stronger cyclones, and other parts of South Asia will have heavier summer rains. Indonesia may get less rain from July to October, but coastal areas near the South China Sea and Gulf of Thailand will have more extreme rainfall during cyclones.

Over time, rainfall patterns will change. Countries in the north, like Europe and North America, will get more rain, but many dry and semi-dry areas will get less rain. Monsoon seasons are expected to start earlier and last longer.

Developing countries and experts welcome the report, saying it supports what they've observed. The IPCC says climate change is real and happening faster than before. People in Bangladesh and South Asia are already seeing its effects. Most developing countries are dealing with climate change now.

Scientists have reduced their predictions for sea-level rises. Depending on future greenhouse gas emissions, sea levels will rise by about 40 to 62 centimeters by 2100. However, there will be big differences in different places; many people in developing countries' big cities, like Lagos and Calcutta, are at risk.

Warmer weather will lead to more weather disasters. While the number of tropical cyclones globally may stay the same or decrease, they may become stronger with heavier rain and stronger winds.

Living in many developing country cities could become very uncomfortable, especially since city temperatures are already much higher than in nearby rural areas. Higher temperatures could shorten the growing period in some African areas by up to 20%.

Oxfam predicts that world hunger will get worse due to climate change hurting crop production and reducing incomes. By 2050, the number of people at risk of hunger could increase by 10% to 20%.

Climate change is already making it harder to fight hunger, and it's expected to get worse. A hotter world means a hungrier world.

Sometimes in life, men feel sad and think about buying a fast car. This feeling is called a midlife crisis. Scientists now say that apes, like chimpanzees and orangutans, might also go through a similar period when they are middle-aged.

A group of scientists from different countries studied over 500 apes living in zoos, sanctuaries, and research centers. They asked people who work with these apes to fill out questionnaires about the apes' moods, how much they enjoy playing with others, and how successful they are at getting what they want.

The scientists found that the apes' happiness went down in middle age and then got better again when they got older. For chimpanzees, happiness was lowest at about 28 years old, and for orangutans, it was lowest at about 35 years old.

Some experts do not agree with these findings. They think it's hard to know if apes really feel the same way humans do during a midlife crisis. But Alex Weiss, a scientist from Edinburgh University, thinks studying apes could help us understand why some humans feel sad in middle age.

Scientists think that apes, like chimpanzees and orangutans, may also have a midlife crisis. They asked people who work with apes to answer questions about the apes' moods and happiness.
