Some experts do not believe the study. But Alex Weiss thinks studying apes can help us understand why some humans feel sad in the middle of their lives.

When you hear "Amazon," what comes to mind? Is it the big forest, the long river, or the large online store? These thoughts are part of a debate about changing internet addresses.

Brazil and Peru are upset with Amazon, the U.S. online shopping company, for trying to get the internet address ".amazon." The company wants to use ".amazon" as a special type of internet address called a top-level domain, like ".com."

Brazil and Peru say this address should be used for things like protecting the environment and helping native people. They think a private company shouldn't control such an important name.

This situation is part of a bigger discussion about who controls internet addresses. Until now, different types of websites had different endings, like ".com" for businesses and ".gov" for government sites. Now, there's a plan to add many more endings.

A group called ICANN, which helps manage internet addresses, got many requests for new endings, each costing nearly $200,000. Amazon asked for endings like ".shop," ".song," ".book," and ".kindle." But the one causing the most talk is ".amazon."

Brazil and Peru want Amazon to give up its request for ".amazon." They say this name is too important for just one company to use. The Brazilian government thinks it's not fair to let companies use names of important places for their own gain.

Other countries also object to some new endings. For example, Argentina doesn't like that Patagonia, a clothing company, wants to use ".patagonia." Patagonia is a beautiful area with its own parliament and is important for Argentina's economy and tourism.

These issues will be talked about again at a meeting in Durban in July. Some new endings might be ready by the end of 2013.

When you hear "Amazon," do you think of the big forest, the long river, or the big online store? Which one is most important?

This is part of a talk about the internet. Brazil and Peru do not like that the U.S. online store wants to use ".amazon" as a web address.

Amazon wants to use ".amazon" instead of ".com." But Brazil and Peru say this stops people from using ".amazon" for things like saving nature and helping native people.

There are other arguments too, like over ".patagonia."

Right now, we know if a website is for business or government by looking at the end of the web address, like ".com" or ".gov." Soon, there will be more endings, called generic top-level domains (gTLDs).

A group called ICANN got many requests for new gTLDs. Each request costs nearly $200,000. Amazon asked for many new domains, such as ".shop," ".song," ".book," and ".kindle." But the one causing the most talk is ".amazon."

Brazil and Peru want to stop Amazon from getting ".amazon." They say a private company should not use a name for a big place.

Brazil says other countries that are part of the Amazon area agree with them.

Argentina does not like that a U.S. clothing company wants to use ".patagonia." Patagonia is a beautiful area with oil, fishing, mining, farming, and lots of tourists.

They will talk about these problems at a meeting in Durban in July. New web addresses may start being used before the end of 2013.

Joseph Roche, an astrophysicist from Trinity College Dublin, is one of 100 people chosen for the Mars One mission. However, he has doubts about the mission's chances of success. Mars One wants to send people to live on Mars starting in 2025.

Roche wrote in the Guardian that the selection process for astronauts was not strict enough. He also thinks the Dutch Mars One team is too confident they can do this $6 billion mission alone. Roche believes it is very unlikely to happen.

He is worried about how the mission picked its top ten candidates. These rankings were based on how many supporter points each candidate got, which shows how much money supporters donated to Mars One.

Mars One plans to send a lander and satellite to Mars in 2018, a rover in 2020, and cargo missions starting in 2022. People would start going to Mars in 2025, and groups of four would go every two years. They would stay on Mars forever.

Gerard t Hooft, a famous Dutch physicist, said this schedule is not realistic. He thinks it will take longer and cost more.

Roche also said that only 2,761 people applied to be astronauts, not 200,000 as Mars One claimed. At first, there were supposed to be long interviews, but then it changed to just ten-minute Skype calls.

Roche still loves the idea of exploring space. He would volunteer for a one-way trip to Mars if it ever became possible. But he does not think such a mission will happen in his lifetime.

Roche says the way they pick astronauts is not as good as other ways. He also says the Mars One team in the Netherlands is too hopeful they can do this big job alone. It costs $6 billion. Roche thinks they should know it may not happen.

The small space looks like a classroom. Its walls are made of corrugated iron and have educational charts, letters, and a map of Bangladesh. But it's hard to focus because of the constant noise of hammering and the chemicals in the air that make your throat and eyes hurt. Still, the children learning here are lucky because they don't have to work in the nearby factories.

For 14 years, SOHAY, a local non-profit group supported by the Global Fund for Children and Comic Relief, has worked in poor areas of Dhaka to help child laborers go to school. They focus on kids working in dangerous jobs.

This classroom is one of 23 centers SOHAY has built in the city. These centers teach children so they can start primary school. After starting school, the children can get help with homework at the centers.

Alamin, a 10-year-old boy who used to work in a plastic factory, now attends one of these centers. His father sells things on the street, and his mother works part-time as a house cleaner. They are all happy Alamin is in school instead of working in a factory. His friend Rabi says he likes school and wants to forget about his past in the factory.

SOHAY’s program manager, Mohammed Abdullah al-Mamun, says the centers try to make families see the value of education and change how they think about children. SOHAY also talks to parents and employers to stop child labor and gives training to help families earn more money.

Mamun says it's hard to get working children into school because they struggle to make friends and adjust to school life. Keeping them in school is also tough since many don’t finish.

Seven-year-old Zhorna Akter Sumayya has two older brothers who work—one at a restaurant and one at a local club. Her parents, who work in a rickshaw garage and as a house cleaner, couldn’t support the family without their sons’ earnings. But they wanted Zhorna to go to school, so she now attends a state primary school after being introduced to education at one of SOHAY’s centers.

In 2015, SOHAY helped 1,540 children stop working in dangerous jobs and got 2,125 more children, who were at risk of starting work, into school. About 780 more children are getting ready to start school in 2017. SOHAY is also teaching 635 working children about their rights.

Bangladesh’s Labor Law of 2006 says children under 14 cannot work, but UNICEF reports that 4.7 million children under that age are employed, and 1.3 million aged five to 17 work in dangerous jobs.

Sadia Nasrin, who runs Sonjag, another local non-profit group, says it was hard to get children into school without paying their families. So Sonjag worked closely with the community to explain why it’s important for children to go to school. They picked community volunteers who wanted to change children’s lives and formed groups with social workers, community leaders, mothers, young volunteers, and local government officials.

These groups encourage employers to let children leave work for two to three hours each day to attend school and ensure the workplace is safe. Mamun says it’s a race against time to get children into school before they grow up without an education. He adds that once children miss starting school at five, it becomes very hard to get them to go later.

A top US researcher warns that today's people might miss the peaceful sounds of nature because of loud background noise and using earphones.

Kurt Fristrup, a scientist at the US National Park Service, says that high levels of noise in some areas make people unaware of the pleasant sounds like birds singing, water flowing, and leaves rustling. He adds that these sounds can often be heard even in cities.

Listening to music through earphones makes the problem worse because it blocks out the sounds of nature. Fristrup calls this "learned deafness" and says we are training ourselves to ignore sounds around us.

Fristrup spoke about this issue at a science meeting in San Jose. He worries that the ability to hear distant sounds and enjoy nature might be lost. He explains that constant noise exposure makes us stop listening, and we lose the ability to connect with the environment as we should.

For the last ten years, the US National Park Service has measured sound levels at over 600 locations in the US, including famous parks like Yosemite, Yellowstone, and Denali. Noise from human activities like planes, motorcycles, boats, and tour buses affects all these places.

Fristrup’s team created a model showing that noise pollution more than doubles every 30 years. People use earphones or noise-canceling headphones to find quieter spaces.

High background noise limits our hearing just like fog limits our vision. In cities, there are still birds and other sounds to enjoy, but the ability to hear them is being lost.

People adapt to changes in their environment, including louder noise, and may accept worse conditions over time. Fristrup fears that finding peace and quiet will become hard, and many children will grow up without experiencing it.

Other scientists say that listening to natural sounds can improve health. Derrick Taff, a scientist at Pennsylvania State University, found that listening to recordings of nature helped people calm down faster after stressful events compared to recordings with traffic, plane, or conversation noises.

Natural sounds are important reasons why people visit protected areas. Fristrup thinks that over millions of years, humans may have linked these sounds with safety.

A US scientist says people do not hear nature sounds like birds or water because they ignore the noises around them.

Kurt Fristrup, a scientist at the US National Park Service, says more background noise makes it hard to hear nature. People also use earphones to listen to music instead of listening to nature sounds.

Fristrup told a science meeting that people are learning to ignore sounds. This means they might lose the ability to hear faraway and special sounds.

The problem is getting worse. Every 30 years, noise pollution more than doubles. In over 600 parks in the US, there is noise from planes, bikes, boats, and buses.

Fristrup worries that if it gets too noisy, kids will not know what quiet is. This is a big problem.

Listening to nature sounds can help people feel less stressed. Derrick Taff, a scientist from Pennsylvania State University, says people visit parks to hear these sounds. He says people should go to parks to enjoy what they might be missing when they use earphones.

A race engineer works between the driver and the mechanics. 

Salary: New workers start at 25,000 to 30,000. With a few years of experience, they can become junior engineers and earn over 40,000. Senior race engineers earn 50,000 to 90,000.

Job Details: A race engineer listens to the driver's feedback, analyzes data, decides on car setup changes for better performance, and tells the mechanics what to do.

Requirements: A university degree in automotive/mechanical engineering or motorsport technology. Practical experience is needed.

Skills Needed: Ability to handle stress.

Bad Part: Long hours. Race engineers work 24/7.

An ethical hacker tests a company’s computer system to find weaknesses.

Salary: New ethical hackers earn 35,000 to 50,000. Team leaders earn 60,000 to 90,000.

Job Details: A company hires an ethical hacker to break into their system to check its security.

Requirements: No specific degree needed. Many different types of qualifications and skills are accepted.

Skills Needed: Passion for technology and detail. Enjoy solving hard problems.

Bad Part: Discovering a customer's system has already been hacked.

A bomb-disposal diver searches for and disposes of underwater explosives.

Salary: Up to 100,000 for two months of work each year.

Job Details: Divers search for unexploded bombs, shells, grenades, and landmines, then recover or dispose of them safely.

Requirements: Diving qualifications and explosive-disposal training with years of experience.

Skills Needed: Stay calm under stress. Comfortable working alone in confined spaces.

Bad Part: Being away from home for at least six months a year.

A social engineer tricks employees to get confidential information.

Salary: Starts at 25,000 for graduates. With qualifications and experience, earnings rise to 50,000 to 80,000.

Job Details: Social engineers pretend to be someone else to gain access to company data or networks.

Requirements: Usually a degree in IT. Understanding psychology is helpful.

Skills Needed: Confidence to lie convincingly and fit in anywhere. Strong ethics and legal knowledge.

Bad Part: People often misunderstand the job, thinking social engineers are spies.

A power-line helicopter pilot flies near high-voltage power lines to inspect them.

Salary: 65,000

Job Details: Pilots fly close to power lines to check for faults using a camera.

Requirements: Private and commercial helicopter licenses with 2,000 hours of low-level flying experience.

Skills Needed: Steady hands and a cool head. Must fly close to power lines, sometimes only 20 feet away and 30 feet above the ground.

Bad Part: None, according to Robin Tutcher, a helicopter pilot.

Job Details: Duties include managing staff, serving meals, running errands, caring for pets, booking restaurants, handling security, cleaning, cooking, and more.

A recent report says the richest people in India will be four times richer by 2018, with many new entrepreneurs and inheritors becoming multimillionaires. This survey was based on interviews with 150 wealthy individuals. It comes at a time when there are signs of returning business confidence in India, the world's largest democracy.

In recent years, India faced weak economic growth, higher food prices, and a decrease in the value of its currency. However, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won a big election in May 2014, promising to improve the economy. Now, there are almost one-sixth more Indians worth more than $3.75 million than in 2013. Murali Balaraman, a co-author of the report, says cities are growing, the middle class is expanding, and opportunities have increased significantly.

India’s rich hold assets worth a trillion dollars, which is about a fifth of the country's total wealth. By 2018, this total could reach $4 trillion, making three times as many people multimillionaires.

There is a growing market for luxury goods among the new rich. They like to show off their wealth subtly through luxury purchases. Cars are very popular. While in 2009, local SUVs were favored, now only foreign cars impress people. Mercedes saw a 47% increase in sales in India in 2013, and BMW introduced a new $200,000 model in Delhi.

However, India's poor infrastructure limits the demand for luxury cars. Lamborghini's CEO, Stephan Winkelmann, noted that the traffic and roads in India are not ideal for expensive sports cars. Lamborghini sells two models in India: the Gallardo and the Aventador, which can go up to 217 mph. In India, Lamborghini buyers are typically in their 30s, younger than European buyers.

Real estate and jewelry remain the most popular investments. India's super-rich often surprise the world with their extravagant spending. For example, Mukesh Ambani, India's wealthiest man, built the world's most expensive home in Mumbai, a 27-story tower with helicopter pads, indoor cinemas, and over 600 staff, valued at $1 billion.

Lakshmi Mittal, a UK-based steel tycoon worth $16 billion, reportedly spent $80 million on his niece's three-day wedding in Barcelona. Guests were flown to the city for the event held in a museum.

Luxury buyers are becoming more demanding. One person ordered nine cases of Japanese whisky costing over $750 per bottle for a wedding reception. Another bought matching Louis Vuitton bags and cut some to make clothes that matched her accessories.

Traditional weddings are also changing. Instead of giving silver plates or dried fruits, top western designer brands like Rolex watches and Louis Vuitton bags are now common gifts.

Almost half of the new multimillionaires live in smaller cities, and many donate large sums to charity. Co-author Balaraman believes the increase in rich people will not cause social tensions because income and wealth gaps are accepted norms in India. People understand that some are rich and others are poor, and they continue with their lives.

Margaret Thatcher, a famous British prime minister after Winston Churchill, has passed away. The British government said she will have a special funeral at St Paul's Cathedral.

David Cameron, the current British prime minister, said he was very sad to hear about her death. He said she was a great leader and the first woman to be prime minister. He believes she will be remembered as the best British prime minister during peace times.

President Obama of the United States said that Thatcher and President Reagan stood together and showed the world that we can use our beliefs and courage to shape history.

Thatcher was the first woman to lead a major Western country. She was the prime minister for 11 years before being removed by her own party in 1990. She was 87 years old and had been sick for some time, suffering from dementia.

Politicians from different parties praised her. Ed Miliband, the leader of the Labour Party, said she changed politics for a whole generation but was also a controversial figure. Nick Clegg, the deputy prime minister, said she left a unique mark on the country.

Sir John Major, a former Conservative prime minister, described her as a political phenomenon and remembered her for her courage, determination, and kindness.

Thatcher was a close friend of U.S. President Ronald Reagan during the Cold War. She supported the breakup of the Soviet Union and was seen as a supporter of freedom in former Soviet states.

Before becoming prime minister, Thatcher was not well-known. In 1975, she became the party leader and soon became famous worldwide for her economic reforms and strong foreign policies. She faced many challenges, including a bombing attempt by the IRA in 1984.

In the UK, she is known for selling off state-owned industries and defeating powerful trade unions. She used money from North Sea oil to change the old industrial economy and defeat her opponents, even within her own party.

She got a refund for Britain from the European Union, calling it "my money." However, she had trouble controlling the European Commission, which wanted more centralized power in Europe.

For a while, Thatcher seemed unbeatable as the economy improved. But mistakes and losing allies made her less popular. A disagreement with her deputy over Europe led to a challenge for her position, and she was replaced by John Major.

After retiring, Thatcher wrote successful books and worked for the Thatcher Foundation to spread her ideas.

Her main economic policy was privatizing state-owned industries. She also fought against powerful trade unions, especially the National Union of Miners. She used money from North Sea oil to change the old industrial economy and defeat her opponents.

At first, Thatcher seemed unbeatable. But as her friends left, she made mistakes and became unpopular. In 1990, Conservative MPs voted against her, and John Major took over.

After retiring, Thatcher wrote about her life and spread her ideas around the world.

At one primary school in Stirling, Scotland, when kids hear "daily mile," they stop working and go outside to run around the school field. For over three years, all students at St Ninians Primary School have walked or run a mile each day. They do this at different times, and none of the children are overweight, even though childhood obesity is rising in the UK.

The daily mile has helped improve the children's fitness, behavior, and focus in class. Many other British schools are copying this idea. They ask students to get up from their desks and spend 15 minutes walking or running around the school or a nearby park.

Elaine Wyllie, the headteacher of St Ninians, says she gets at least two emails a day from other schools asking about the daily mile. She feels excited that her school might inspire children across the country to run every day.

According to the Health & Social Care Information Centre, one in ten children are obese when they start school at ages four or five. In 2015, a study showed that English schoolchildren are less fit than ever before. Because of this, many primary schools are starting the daily mile. In Stirling alone, 30 schools have already started or plan to start the daily mile.

The daily mile is a simple way to improve children’s fitness. It costs nothing and is easy to do. The key is that the children enjoy it. After running, they return to class feeling energized and happy. At St Ninians, teachers take their students out for their daily mile whenever it fits the schedule. Only ice or heavy rain stops them.

Researchers from Stirling University are studying the benefits of the daily mile. They want to find out if it improves physical, mental, and emotional health. St Ninians students will be compared to those from another school in Stirling that hasn’t started the program yet.

Kevin Clelland, a teacher from Leeds, visited St Ninians and decided to start the daily mile at his school. He believes it has a big positive effect. His school is building a track for the daily mile.

Active Cheshire, a sports organization, plans to bring local officials to Scotland to see the daily mile in action. If a pilot program works well, they hope to introduce it to 450 schools in their area.

Tanni Grey-Thompson, a Paralympian and chair of ukactive, a health organization, says all children should be active for 60 minutes a day. She thinks the daily mile shows leadership in improving children’s fitness and behavior. This can make a big difference in the lives of students, teachers, parents, and young people.

The Scottish government supports the daily mile too. They believe it helps teach healthy habits early in life and encourages parents to support these habits. Many Scottish schools are joining or planning to join the program.

Dancevic said the conditions were unsafe for players. He mentioned that the heat made him see things that weren't real, like Snoopy. He stated, "It's inhumane. It's not fair to the players, fans, or the sport when players collapse."

British player Andy Murray agreed, saying it looked bad for the sport when people were fainting due to the heat. Caroline Wozniacki noted that her water bottle melted a bit on the court, showing how hot it was. John Isner compared the court to an oven, and Victoria Azarenka said it felt like dancing in a frying pan.

In 2014, the tournament director, Wayne McKewen, could decide if matches should be stopped due to heat. Organizers said the temperature reached 42.2 degrees Celsius but did not stop matches because the humidity was low.

Dancevic continued playing after getting medical help but lost the match. A ball boy also needed medical care after fainting during another match. Peng Shuai, a Chinese player, said the heat made her feel sick and vomit.

Tim Wood, the tournament’s chief medical officer, said most matches finished without players needing medical help. Roger Federer believed that if players trained well, they could handle the heat. However, Dancevic argued that some players' bodies naturally handled heat better than others and that it was dangerous. He said he still couldn’t urinate an hour and a half after his match.

Sir Alex Ferguson, the manager of Manchester United, will stop working at the end of the season after 27 years. He won 13 English Premier League titles, two Champions Leagues, the Cup Winners Cup, five FA Cups, and four League Cups. 

Ferguson said he thought a lot about retiring and believes now is the right time. He feels he left the club in strong condition. He praised the quality of the team and the youth setup, which will help the club continue to do well in the future. He also thanked his family, players, and staff for their support and dedication. He said the board of directors and the Glazer family helped him build a football club, not just a team.

Ferguson told the players about his decision in an emotional meeting. Joel Glazer, who owns Manchester United, said Ferguson is a great manager and person. Avie Glazer, his brother, said Ferguson will stay with the club as a director. David Gill, the chief executive, said he enjoyed working with Ferguson for 16 years and praised his vision and loyalty. First-team coach Ren Meulensteen said Ferguson made a thoughtful decision and wished him well.

Sir Alex Ferguson, the manager of Manchester United, will stop being the manager at the end of the season after 27 years. He will then become a director of the club. He is the most successful manager in British football. He won 13 Premier League titles, 2 Champions Leagues, the Cup Winners' Cup, 5 FA Cups, and 4 League Cups.

Ferguson said, "I thought a lot about retiring. Now is the right time. I want to leave the team strong, and I think I did that." He believes the team's quality and young players will keep the club successful.

"Our training places are some of the best in sports," he added. "Old Trafford, our stadium, is one of the most important places in the world. I am happy to be a director and ambassador for the club. I look forward to the future." He thanked his family, players, and staff for their help and support.

Joel Glazer, one of the club owners, said Ferguson is a great manager and person. His brother Avie Glazer said they are glad Ferguson will stay as a director. David Gill, the chief executive, said working with Ferguson was amazing and he admired how much Ferguson cared for the club.

René Meulensteen, the first-team coach, said Ferguson told the staff about his decision. He wished Ferguson well and hoped fans would support the new manager.

In the first half of 2014, Lego's profits increased a lot because of the success of its movie, "The Lego Movie," which did very well in the US and UK theaters.

Sales went up in Europe, the Americas, and Asia as kids bought toys from the movie. The movie made over $250 million in the US and $31 million in the UK by early April. It cost about $60 million to make and was seen as great marketing. It was fun and encouraged people to buy Lego products.

John Goodwin, Lego’s finance director, said the movie helped profits in the first half of 2014. They are now waiting to see how sales will do when the movie comes out on DVD later in the year.

Jørgen Vig Knudstorp, Lego’s CEO, said it was a good result showing strong growth despite a difficult economy. This growth came from making toys that kids really want.

Lego began making plastic bricks in 1949 and became famous by the 1970s. In 2003, the company nearly failed, but Knudstorp took over and focused on just making bricks. In April, Lego opened its first factory in China and set up an office in Shanghai to grow in the country's big market.

Lego made more money in the first half of 2014 because of the Lego Movie. The movie did very well in the US and UK. In the US, it made over $250 million, and in the UK, it made over £31 million. The movie cost about $60 million to make.

John Goodwin, Lego's finance director, said the Lego Movie helped Lego sell more toys and make more money. They are waiting to see if selling DVDs will help too.

Jørgen Vig Knudstorp, Lego’s boss, said they are happy they sold more toys. This happened because kids really want Lego toys.

Lego makes toys in Billund, Denmark. They started making plastic bricks in 1949. By the 1970s, Lego became famous worldwide. In 2003, Lego almost went out of business. Knudstorp became the new boss and focused on making bricks again. In April 2014, Lego opened its first factory in China.

He lived like a rich person. He had a fancy Rolex watch and many expensive cars. He also bought modern art. Even though this Chinese businessman owned several companies and a big house in Madrid, he did not have much money in the bank. This made the Spanish government curious.

Gao Ping provided 4,000 Chinese markets in Spain. However, the government thought he was not paying taxes on the things he brought from China, such as clothes and furniture.

In 2012, when the police looked through his warehouses, they found a lot of cash. There were 100, 200, and 500 notes tied together with rubber bands. They took around 12 million euros, which was the most cash ever found by Spanish police. Gao's group is accused of cleaning up to 300 million euros each year, as well as selling fake goods and toys without proper safety labels.

Police have been concerned about 500 notes for a while. These notes are small and easy to carry compared to their value. Criminals often use them. One million euros in 500 notes can fit into a small laptop bag, but the same amount in 50 notes would need a small suitcase.

The UK stopped using 500 notes in 2010 because they were mostly used by criminals. In 2009, Italy’s central bank warned that these notes were commonly used by the mafia and terrorists. Other countries have also limited their high-value notes due to links to organized crime. For example, Canada got rid of its $1,000 note in 2000 based on advice from law enforcement.

Now, with electronic payments and contactless cards, some people wonder if we should keep printing these notes. Peter Sands, who used to lead Standard Chartered Bank, suggested getting rid of high-value notes, including the 500, the $100, the 1,000 Swiss Franc note, and the 50. Sands wrote in a report for Harvard that removing these notes would make it harder for criminals to operate. Criminals might then use smaller notes, gold, or diamonds, but these are harder to carry and easier to track.

At a meeting in London about funding terrorism, the head of Europol, Rob Wainwright, asked the European Central Bank to consider stopping the production of these notes. These notes help criminals and terrorists hide their money and fund illegal activities. According to Europol, the purple 500 note makes up 30% of all euro notes, even though most people have never seen one.

The 500 note came out in 2002 when the euro started. It replaced the 1,000 Deutschmark, the 10,000 Belgian franc, and the 500,000 Italian lira. In Germany and Austria, over half of all transactions are still done with cash and coins.

Europol wants central banks to be more responsible for how 500 notes are used. In 2013, Luxembourg issued more than twice its yearly GDP in banknotes. When Europol asked Luxembourg’s central bank to explain, they said they just give out the notes people ask for and don’t know why people want them. This surprised Jennifer MacLeod, an expert in Europol’s financial intelligence group.

EU finance ministers have asked policymakers to think about setting limits on high-value notes and to report back by May 1, 2016.

McDonald's is the biggest burger chain in the world and a symbol of American business. However, lately, things aren't going well for McDonald's. Sales dropped by 3.3% worldwide in 2013, which is considered very bad.

In China, sales fell by 23% after reports showed that a local supplier used old meat in McDonald's and KFC products. In Europe, sales went down by 4%, mainly due to issues in Ukraine and Russia. About 200 of McDonald's 450 restaurants in Russia are under investigation, and ten have been closed.

In the United States, where McDonald's has around 40% of its restaurants, the situation is worse. Sales have been falling for 12 months, with a 4.1% drop in the latest quarter. Young people are choosing other places like Chipotle instead. The number of 19-to-21-year-olds visiting McDonald's once a month has dropped by 13% since 2011.

A recent survey of over 32,000 Americans found that McDonald's burgers were rated the worst. Many people think McDonald's food is less healthy compared to places like Chipotle, which uses antibiotic-free meat and locally sourced produce.

McDonald's tried to address customer concerns through a website called "Our Food Your Questions." One question asked if they used "pink slime," a controversial filler used in burgers. McDonald's stopped using it in 2012 but still needs to clear up misunderstandings about their food quality.

McDonald's is also facing criticism for higher prices and slower service. While prices have risen by 4.8% since 2009, this is lower than the average increase in fast-food prices, which went up by 19.4%.

In the UK, McDonald's has improved its business with better breakfast options, coffee, and free Wi-Fi, making it popular among British adults.

McDonald's plans to offer more organic food and customizable burgers to improve its image. However, experts are unsure how McDonald's can simplify its menu while offering more choices.

Despite declining sales, McDonald's continues to grow globally, expecting to open 1,400 new restaurants by the end of 2014. Experts believe McDonald's will remain a top player for years to come.

McDonald's is a big burger company from America. But now, it is having some problems. Fewer people are buying food there. Worldwide, sales went down by 3.3%.

In China, sales dropped by 23%. In Europe, sales went down by 4%. In Russia, health workers checked 200 of 450 McDonald's restaurants and closed 10 of them.

The biggest problem is in the U.S., where McDonald's has 40% of its restaurants. For 12 months, sales have been going down. Young people are choosing other places like Chipotle. Since 2011, visits by 19-to-21-year-olds have dropped by 13%.

A recent survey said McDonald's burgers are the worst in America. People think they are not as healthy as burgers from places like Chipotle. Chipotle uses meat without antibiotics and fresh local foods.

In October, McDonald's asked customers what they thought. One person asked if they use "pink slime" in their burgers. Pink slime is a beef filler used for dog food. McDonald's stopped using it in 2012, but they need to make people trust their food more.

McDonald's is known for being quick and cheap. But since they raised prices, people think it costs too much and service is slow. Food experts say McDonald's prices have gone up less than other fast-food places. Queues are longer because the menu is bigger and more complex.

To fix this, McDonald's plans to add more organic food and let people build their own burgers. They also want simpler menus. Four out of 14,000 U.S. restaurants are testing the "build your own burger" idea. Some experts are not sure if this will work.

Even though sales are down, McDonald's is opening 1,400 new restaurants by the end of 2014. Experts think sales will keep going down, but McDonald's will stay the top burger place for a long time.

Will drones soon deliver packages? Amazon thinks so, but others are unsure. More technical progress is needed, along with solving public safety issues.

Paul Misener from Amazon said his company is ready once the rules are set. By June 2016, the FAA will have new rules for using drones for business. However, the technology needs improvement, and only drones weighing up to 25 kg will be allowed.

The FAA requires drones to use unique radio frequencies to prevent hacking or jamming.

Professor Sajiv Singh, who runs a cargo delivery company, explained that drones can be given simple instructions like "go to this height, do a task, return." But flying in urban areas can be tricky due to unexpected obstacles, construction, or GPS signal loss.

Maintaining radio contact with drones is crucial. If contact is lost, current drones may crash. Larger drones over 25 kg cannot be used for deliveries yet.

Jay McConville from Lockheed Martin noted that operators want easy-to-use drones that show status and video on devices like smartphones or laptops.

Daniel Huber, who works on 3D imaging, mentioned that Amazon's drones can carry a kilogram for 15 minutes. Smaller drones are safer than larger ones.

Safety is a big issue. Commercial aircraft must prove they have only one serious failure every million hours. Drones currently have one failure every 10,000 hours, which is not enough for public safety.

To improve safety, drones need to handle failures well. For example, a drone should land safely if it loses power.

One day, drones may bring packages to your house. Amazon thinks this will happen soon, but others are not sure. First, they need to create the right technology and make sure it is safe for everyone.

Amazon says they will start when the FAA makes rules for drones. The FAA plans to make these rules by June 2016. Only drones weighing up to 25 kg will be allowed. The FAA also wants drones to use special radio frequencies that cannot be blocked or taken over.

Professor Sajiv Singh from NearEarth says flying drones is easy if you tell them where to go and what to do. However, drones must avoid dangers like buildings or construction sites. If GPS signals are blocked, drones might get lost.

Daniel Huber, a robot expert, says keeping radio contact with drones is hard. If contact is lost, drones might crash. Huber believes we have most of the technology needed. His team uses drones to check phone lines and bridges.

Huber says Amazon's drones can carry a kilogram for 15 minutes. This means drones can only travel a short distance to stay safe. Longer trips are riskier.

Safety is very important. Passenger planes can only have one serious problem every million hours. Drones are much less safe. For example, the Reaper drone has one problem every 10,000 hours. Planes have high safety standards because flying is dangerous. If a drone fails, it should do something safe.

Waiters are asking for help to keep their tips. They are protesting at PizzaExpress restaurants because the company takes 8p out of every pound paid in tips by card. This makes the workers angry. PizzaExpress has 430 locations in the UK and earns about £1 million a year from this policy.

Chantal Chegrinec from the union Unite said this fee is unfair. She believes the company should give all the tips to the staff. The first protest is happening at the PizzaExpress near the British Museum in London. Unite started this campaign after talking to workers after the company was bought by a Chinese firm in 2014.

An unnamed worker said the fee costs her £3 each night. She has worked there for 15 years and is still only paid the minimum wage of £6.50 per hour. She relies on tips to make up for her low pay.

Other restaurant chains like Ask and Zizzi also take 8% of tips paid by card. Some like Cafe Rouge and Bella Italia take 10%.

PizzaExpress says the fee covers the cost of running a tronc, a system for sharing tips among staff. They say the staff decide how to share the tips. However, other restaurants like Wagamama and Pizza Hut do not take any fees from tips.

Unite gave out leaflets at ten PizzaExpress restaurants in South London. Over 5,800 people have signed their online petition. A waiter from another restaurant chain said tips make up at least a third of his income. He earns £40 to £50 in tips on an average night.

MP Andrew Percy wants to change the law to give more control of tips to restaurant workers.

Waiters are asking people to help them keep their tips. They are planning to protest at PizzaExpress restaurants. They want the restaurant to stop taking some of the tips paid by card. The protesters started an online petition. They hope people who visit the restaurants will support them.

PizzaExpress takes 8p out of every £1 in tips paid by card. This costs the workers money. The chain has 430 restaurants in the UK and makes about £1 million a year from this practice.

Chantal Chegrinec from Unite says this fee is unfair. She thinks the company should give all the tips to the workers. Unite plans to target other companies after PizzaExpress.

The first protest will be at a PizzaExpress near the British Museum in London. After a Chinese company bought PizzaExpress in 2014, many workers complained about losing part of their tips. That's why Unite started the campaign.

Other restaurant chains like Ask and Zizzi also take 8% of tips paid by card. Some take even more, like Café Rouge, Bella Italia, Belgo, Strada, and Giraffe, which take 10%.

PizzaExpress says the money they take pays for a system to share tips among staff. But other restaurants don't take any money from tips. Unite recently gave out leaflets to customers at ten PizzaExpress restaurants in south London. Customers were shocked and disgusted by the practice.

Almost 6,000 people have signed Unite’s online petition. One waiter, who works at another restaurant, said he gets about £40 to £50 in tips each night. He earns only £6.50 an hour, so the tips are very important to him.

A secret document shows that the National Security Agency (NSA) can directly access the systems of big US internet companies like Google, Facebook, and Apple. This program is called PRISM. It lets the NSA gather things like search history, emails, files, and chats. The document says the NSA collects this information straight from the company servers. The companies say they don't know about this program.

Google stated they care about user data security and only share data with the government when required by law. They also said there is no "back door" for the government to access private user data.

Tech leaders say they have no knowledge of PRISM or similar programs. For example, an Apple spokesperson said they had never heard of PRISM.

The NSA's ability to do this comes from changes in US surveillance laws made under Presidents Bush and Obama. The program allows deep surveillance on live and stored information. The law lets the NSA target any customers of these companies living outside the US, as well as Americans communicating with people outside the US.

This news came after a secret court order forced telecom company Verizon to hand over phone records of millions of US customers to the government. The involvement of internet companies in PRISM adds to debates about how much the intelligence services watch people. Unlike the collection of call records from Verizon, this surveillance includes the content of communications, not just basic information.

Some of the world’s biggest internet companies are part of PRISM, which started in 2007. Microsoft was first, followed by Yahoo, Google, Facebook, PalTalk, YouTube, Skype, AOL, and Apple.

US law requires companies to follow requests for user communications. However, PRISM gives the NSA direct access to company servers. The NSA document says the operations have the help of US communication providers.

When the FISA Amendments Act (FAA) was renewed in December 2012, some US senators warned about the high level of surveillance allowed and the lack of safeguards. Supporters of the FAA originally said the NSA couldn’t get electronic communications without the telecom and internet companies’ permission. But PRISM makes that permission unnecessary, allowing the NSA to take communications directly from company servers.

PRISM lets the NSA get targeted communications without asking service providers or getting individual court orders. The NSA can reach directly into company servers to get both stored and live communications.

An official said the PRISM program targets only non-US persons outside the US. The program is watched by the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court, the Executive Branch, and Congress. Information gathered helps protect the nation from various threats.

A secret paper says the US National Security Agency (NSA) can look at information from big internet companies like Google, Facebook, and Apple. This is part of a program called PRISM. PRISM lets the government see what people search for, their emails, files, chats, and more.

The NSA can get this info straight from the company servers. The companies say they don't know about this program. Google says they care about keeping user data safe and only share it with the government when required by law. They also say there is no special way for the government to get private user data.

Tech leaders say they didn’t know about PRISM. One leader said if it's happening, it's without their knowledge. Apple says they haven't heard of PRISM.

Rules changed under Presidents Bush and Obama let the NSA do this. The program watches live and saved information. The law lets the NSA watch people outside the US or Americans talking to people outside the US.

Since 2007, big internet companies have been part of this program. Microsoft started in 2007, then Yahoo in 2008, Google, Facebook, and PalTalk in 2009, YouTube in 2010, Skype and AOL in 2011, and Apple in 2012.

Companies must give user info if asked by the government. PRISM lets the government get info directly from company servers.

In December 2012, a law called FISA changed. Some senators were worried it would let the government watch more. Supporters said the NSA couldn't get info without the companies' permission, but PRISM doesn't need that permission.

An official said Section 702 of FISA can't target US citizens or people in the US. It only targets people outside the US. The info helps protect the country from dangers.

Do you want your child to be good at sports, play for the school team, and maybe compete in big competitions one day? Try to make sure your child is born in November or October. A study by a UK expert on children's physical activity shows that kids born in these months are fitter than others in their class.

Children born in November and October were found to be fitter, stronger, and more powerful than those born in other months, especially those born in April or June. Dr. Gavin Sandercock from Essex University and his team found that children born in autumn have a clear physical advantage.

The study included 8,550 boys and girls aged 10 to 16 from 26 state schools in Essex. They were tested between 2007 and 2010 on stamina, handgrip strength, and lower-body power. Results showed that a child’s month of birth can affect their fitness levels, muscle strength, and ability to accelerate, which are important for sports.

Children born in November were the fittest overall, with the most stamina and power, and were the second strongest. Those born in October were nearly as fit, with the highest strength scores and third for power, followed closely by December-born children.

There was a big difference in physical ability between children born in different months. For example, a boy born in November can run at least 10% faster, jump 12% higher, and be 15% more powerful than a child of the same age born in April. This could decide who becomes a top athlete because small differences in physical performance can matter a lot.

The study, published in the International Journal of Sports Medicine, found that children born in April were the least fit, followed by those born in June. This could mean these children might not make school teams and become less successful in sports.

The findings suggest that children born in the early months of the school year have both an academic and a physical advantage. The researchers think that autumn-born children’s greater exposure to vitamin D during pregnancy is the main reason for this advantage.

John Steele, the chief executive of the Youth Sport Trust, said that a good start in sports at school can help children develop better agility, balance, and coordination, making them more likely to enjoy and excel in sports as they grow up.

UK Sport couldn’t confirm if most of the 1,300 athletes they fund across 47 sports were born in November and October. Natalie Dunman, the head of performance, said that while the differences seen in teenage competitions disappear in adult competitions, many factors make a champion, and month of birth isn't a key one.

Thirty-five years ago, when singer Kate Bush last performed on stage, mobile phones were still new. Now, as she performs again, she finds a world full of phones and tablets at concerts. Before her concerts at the Hammersmith Apollo in London, Bush asked her fans to avoid using their phones during her shows. She wrote on her website that she wants direct contact with her audience, not through screens. She hopes this will help everyone share the experience together.

Bush's request might also be to keep the show a surprise for her fans. Other musicians have also spoken against the use of phones at concerts. For example, Roger Daltrey from The Who feels sad for people who focus more on their screens than the performance. In 2013, Beyoncé told a fan to stop filming and enjoy the moment instead.

This issue isn't just about music. Football fans in the Netherlands protested against introducing Wi-Fi in their stadium, saying it distracts from supporting the team. Jarvis Cocker and Johnny Marr have also criticized fans for using phones during concerts, saying it ruins the experience.

Even in classical music, pianist Krystian Zimerman left the stage because someone was filming his performance. However, Sam Watt from Vyclone, an app that encourages filming at concerts, believes that filming enhances the concert experience by creating shared memories. He thinks that if Kate Bush considered this, she might see the benefits of embracing technology.

The last time she sang, there were no mobile phones. Now, 35 years later, singer Kate Bush sees a very different world. Today, most concerts have lots of phones and tablets, but Bush wants her fans to watch her shows without using screens.

Before her concerts at the Hammersmith Apollo in London in August, Bush asked her fans to not use their phones. She wrote on her website: "Please do not take photos or videos during the shows. I want to connect with you, not with your phones."

Other singers don't like phones at concerts either. Roger Daltrey from The Who said it's strange that people look at their screens instead of the artists. He feels sorry for them because they miss out on the moment.

In 2013, Beyoncé told a fan, "Put that camera down! You can't sing while filming."

Dutch soccer fans at PSV Eindhoven protested against having wi-fi in their stadium. They held signs saying "No wi-fi" and "Support the team." Manchester United also told fans to leave big electronic devices at home.

Jarvis Cocker said it's silly to look at a small screen instead of what's happening in front of you.

A famous pianist, Krystian Zimerman, stopped playing once because someone was filming him. He said YouTube hurts music a lot.

Sam Watt thinks filming at concerts is good. He works for Vyclone, an app that combines videos from fans to make one long video of a show. He believes filming adds to the fun and that people will keep filming for memories.

Water experts have issued a very strong warning about the world's food supplies. They say that by 2050, people might need to eat mostly plants to avoid big food shortages.

Right now, humans get about 20% of their protein from meat and dairy. But to feed the extra two billion people expected by 2050, this might need to drop to only 5%, according to top water scientists.

A report by Malik Falkenmark and others at the Stockholm International Water Institute (SIWI) says there won't be enough water to produce food for nine billion people in 2050 if we keep eating like we do now, especially like people in Western countries.

If we want to have enough water, only 5% of what we eat should come from animals.

This warning comes as Oxfam and the UN prepare for another possible global food crisis. Prices for things like corn and wheat have gone up nearly 50% since June because of droughts in the US and Russia, and less rain in Asia. Over 18 million people in the Sahel region are already short on food.

Oxfam says the price rise will hurt many developing countries that buy a lot of food from other places, such as parts of Latin America, North Africa, and the Middle East. In 2008, high food prices caused fighting and riots in 28 countries.

Scientists say changing to a vegetarian diet can help save water to grow more food in a world with unpredictable weather. Eating animal protein uses five to ten times more water than a plant-based diet. One third of the world’s farmland is used to grow food for animals. Other ways to feed more people include reducing waste and trading food between countries that have extra and those that don’t have enough.

Currently, 900 million people don’t have enough to eat, and two billion are not getting proper nutrition, even though more food is being produced per person. Seventy percent of all water is used in farming, and feeding two billion more people by 2050 will use up more water and land.

The report will be shared at the yearly world water meeting in Stockholm, Sweden, where 2,500 people from 120 countries talk about water problems.

The UN says we need to make 70% more food by the middle of the century. This will put more stress on water, which is already in short supply, while we also need more water for energy and electricity for the 1.3 billion people who don’t have it.

More people are overeating, underfed, or wasting food. We need a new plan to feed everyone in the future, said Anders Jgerskog, who edited the report.

Water experts say everyone might need to eat only plants by 2050. There will be two billion more people by then. Now, people get 20% of their protein from animals, but it might go down to 5%.

A report by Malik Falkenmark and others at the Stockholm International Water Institute says there won't be enough water to feed everyone if more people eat like those in the West. If people eat less meat, there will be enough water.

Water shortages could stop food from being made. Oxfam and the UN are getting ready for another food problem. Corn and wheat prices went up almost 50% since June because of droughts in the US and Russia, and not enough rain in Asia. Over 18 million people in the Sahel don't have enough food.

In poor countries that buy food from others, like parts of Latin America, North Africa, and the Middle East, price increases will be really bad.

Eating only plants saves more water for growing food. Animal food needs five to ten times more water than plant food. One third of farmland is used to grow food for animals.

Now, 900 million people don't have enough food, and two million are not healthy because of not having the right food. We use 70% of water for farming. Feeding two billion more people by 2050 will use more water and land.

The report came out at the start of a big meeting in Stockholm, Sweden, where 2,500 people from 120 countries talk about water problems.

People eat too much, are not healthy, and waste food. We need a new way to feed the world in the future.

Cities usually don't move, but Kiruna, a town in northern Sweden, has to. This is to avoid sinking into the ground because of a big iron-ore mine.

Krister Lindstedt from the Swedish architecture firm White says moving the city is a tough decision. The city of 23,000 people needs to move away from the mine that is causing the ground to sink. If the mine stops, many people will lose their jobs. If the city moves, it can keep working.

Kiruna was started in 1900 by the mining company LK. The town grew rich from the iron ore under it, but now it faces destruction because of the same mine. "The town is here because of the mine," says Deputy Mayor Niklas Siren. "Otherwise, no one would have built a city here."

Kiruna is 145 kilometers inside the Arctic Circle and has very cold weather. It gets dark all winter, and temperatures are often below -15°C. But the iron ore keeps people there. The mine is the world's largest underground iron-ore mine and produces 90% of Europe’s iron, enough to build over six Eiffel Towers daily.

In 2004, the mining company warned that the ground would start to sink near the city. Now, cracks are appearing and getting closer to the town.

For ten years, the people of Kiruna have been waiting, unsure about making big decisions like buying a house or starting a family.

Now, the city has a plan. By 2033, the town will move 3 kilometers east. A new town square is being built, with a new town hall designed by Henning Larsen. Some buildings will be taken apart and rebuilt in the new location, like an IKEA flatpack. The famous red wooden church will be placed in a new park.

However, some things won't be saved. An old lady told Viktoria Walldin about a bench where she had her first kiss. These personal memories will be lost.

The mining company will give 320 million for new buildings like schools, fire stations, and libraries. But many people worry about where they will live and how to afford a new home.

LK will pay residents 25% more than their home's value, but this may not be enough for a new house. The new town will have straight streets and apartment buildings instead of the current winding streets and houses with gardens.

Architects see this as a chance to create a modern town that attracts young people with new cultural places and ideas like a cable car. However, many current residents might not be able to afford living there.

Cities usually do not move. But Kiruna, a town in northern Sweden, has to move. If it doesn't, the ground will sink and the town will disappear.

Krister Lindstedt, who works for a Swedish architecture company, says, "It's a bad choice." The company is moving the city of 23,000 people away from a big iron mine that is causing the ground to sink. "We can either stop mining and lose jobs, or we can move the city," he says.

Kiruna is 145 kilometers inside the Arctic Circle. It has very cold winters with no sunlight and temperatures around -15 degrees Celsius. But the iron ore keeps people there. Kiruna has the biggest underground iron mine in the world. It makes 90% of all the iron in Europe. That's enough to build over six Eiffel Towers each day.

In 2004, the mining company said the town would need to move. Digging underground would cause buildings to break and fall. Now, after ten years, cracks are appearing closer to the town.

Viktoria Walldin, who works with the architects, says, "People in Kiruna have been waiting for ten years. They cannot make big choices like buying a house, fixing up a home, having a baby, or starting a business."

Finally, the city has a plan. By 2033, the whole city will move away from the mine. They are building a new town square 3 kilometers to the east. A new round town hall is being planned by Henning Larsen, a Danish architect. Twenty other important buildings will be moved to their new locations. The red wooden church, which was built in 1912 and voted Sweden's most beautiful building, will be in the center of a new park. But not everything will be saved.

Walldin says, "An old lady walks past a bench every day where she had her first kiss. Things like that are important to people, and they will disappear."

The mining company will give £320 million to build new buildings, including a high school, fire station, community center, library, and swimming pool. But many people worry about where they will live and how they will afford a new home.

"People here pay low rent and have high income, but this will change," says Lindstedt. LK will pay people the value of their homes plus 25%, but many think this is not enough to buy a new house.

The new town will look different from the old one. The old town has houses with gardens, but the new plan has tall apartment buildings around shared spaces in long straight streets.

Architects say this is a chance for Kiruna to attract young people with new cultural places and fun things like a cable car above the main street. But many people in Kiruna may not have enough money to live there.

US researchers say that collecting phone records can threaten people's privacy. By looking at basic phone logs, two scientists at Stanford University found out personal information about people, such as their names, where they live, and who their partners are. They also discovered more sensitive details, like someone having a gun, a heart condition, a new pregnancy, or multiple sclerosis.

The scientists used only metadata, which includes the number called, the time of the call, and its duration. They combined this with public information from websites like Google, Yelp, and Facebook. This metadata can reveal a lot about someone’s life, according to Stewart Baker, a former lawyer at the US National Security Agency (NSA).

For their study, 823 people shared their phone metadata through an Android app. The app also got information from their Facebook accounts to check the results. The researchers collected data on over 250,000 calls and more than 1.2 million texts.

The scientists found out 82% of the participants' names and could place 57% of them in the right city. They also figured out who was in a relationship and who the partner was. By analyzing calls to specific places like hospitals, pharmacies, and legal services, they learned more private information about the participants.

This shows that even with limited resources, a lot of personal information can be found from phone metadata. The researchers believe this should make policymakers reconsider allowing large-scale surveillance programs because they can reveal highly private details about regular people.

Two scientists at Stanford University in the USA used information from people's phone calls and texts to learn their names, where they lived, and who their partners were. This information did not include what people said, just who they called, when, and for how long.

They also found out private things about some people. One man had a gun, and another had a heart problem. They learned that someone was having a baby and that someone else had a serious illness.

The scientists used a simple computer program to figure out who was in a relationship. Once they knew who owned a phone number, they could easily find out who their partner was.

In the last part of their study, they looked at calls to places like hospitals, drug stores, religious groups, lawyers, and gun shops. This helped them create a picture of people’s lives.

The scientists said that metadata can reveal very private information about regular people. Stewart Baker, who worked at the US National Security Agency (NSA), said metadata tells almost everything about someone’s life.

For the study, 823 people let the scientists collect information from their phones using an app. The app also got information from their Facebook pages. The scientists collected data from over 250,000 calls and more than 1.2 million texts.

The scientists found out a lot of personal information with very little money. They found out 82% of people’s names. They also figured out where people lived by looking at nearby businesses. They correctly guessed the city 57% of the time and were nearly 90% right about where people lived within 50 miles.

Angela Erdmann never met her grandfather because he died in 1946, six years before she was born. On April 8th, 2014, she got a surprise when she learned about a message in a bottle that her grandfather had thrown into the Baltic Sea 101 years ago. The bottle is thought to be the world's oldest message in a bottle and was shown to her by a museum in Germany.

Erdmann, who is 62, said she was shocked when a genealogical researcher visited her in Berlin with news about the bottle. The bottle was found by a fisherman near Kiel. Holger von Neuhoff, a museum curator, said this message is the oldest one he has seen in a bottle.

Experts think Erdmann’s grandfather, Richard Platz, threw the bottle into the sea during a walk in 1913 when he was 20 years old. Much of the message on the postcard inside was hard to read, but the address in Berlin was clear. The note asked whoever found it to send it back to his home address. He included two stamps so the finder wouldn’t need to pay for postage.

Erdmann said she felt touched by the message even though she didn't know her grandfather. He died at 54, six years before she was born. She learned that he was a writer who believed in freedom and respect for others. He traveled with his family and helped young people. Erdmann said she likes traveling and culture, just like her grandfather. She hopes the bottle stays at the museum.

The message and bottle will be on display at Hamburg’s Maritime Museum until early May 2014. After that, experts will try to read the rest of the text. Erdmann wants to share some photos of her grandfather with the museum so visitors can see who threw the bottle into the sea. She is happy to have the message but hopes people won’t throw more bottles into the sea because it is already filled with trash.

The person next to you in line seems normal, but they might be a mystery shopper. You might notice they are carrying notes about the store, timing the queue, and maybe even have a small camera. In the UK, there are about 50,000 mystery shopping trips each month. As more people shop online, stores want mystery shoppers to check how good their service is.

Simon Boydell from Marketforce, a company with over 300,000 mystery shoppers, says stores want to know if they are giving customers a better experience than online shops. Each mystery shopper visits different stores and writes detailed reports. They can earn up to £155 a day plus expenses. If they use a hidden camera, they can earn around £300 a day.

Mystery shoppers usually get money to spend in the store and can keep what they buy. Laura, a mystery shopper, gets between £5 and £20 to spend at each store. She buys things based on a given scenario but can choose what to buy and keep it.

Laura works as a self-employed mystery shopper and earns about £30,000 to £40,000 a year. She also gets free items. She enjoys seeing improvements in stores due to her feedback. However, only about 10% of registered mystery shoppers get regular work. Pay has dropped, and now many get free items instead of cash.

Hannah, a lawyer, does mystery dining in her free time. She has eaten at over 500 Michelin-starred restaurants and stayed at boutique hotels. After each visit, she writes detailed reports about the food and staff. It's hard work, requiring focus and attention to detail.

In the UK, about 50,000 mystery shopping trips happen every month. Mystery shoppers act like normal customers but they are actually checking how good the store's service is. More people are needed for this job because online shopping is getting more popular.

Simon Boydell from Marketforce, a company with over 300,000 mystery shoppers, says, "Shoppers who visit real stores want a special service and experience they can't find online. Our clients want to know if their stores are giving this."

Jill Spencer from ABa, another mystery shopping company, explains, "We send shoppers to different stores and change their locations every three months. Each day, they visit five to ten stores and spend up to eight hours there. Then, they write detailed reports for one to two hours. They can earn up to £155 a day, plus their expenses. If they use a hidden camera, they can earn around £300 a day."

Laura, a mystery shopper, says, "I usually get between £5 and £20 to spend at each store to check the service at the cash register. I am given a specific task, like buying something from a certain area or a new product line, but I can often choose what I want and keep it."

Laura works by herself and makes about £30,000 to £40,000 a year, plus free items. She likes seeing improvements in stores she visited before. "I feel like I'm helping all shoppers," she says.

Over 500,000 people in the UK signed up to be mystery shoppers, but only 10% or less get regular work. Now, mystery shopping companies mostly give free items instead of money. Marketforce pays shoppers a few pounds for a visit, or £15 to £25 plus expenses for a meal or hotel stay. They don't pay the minimum wage because they don't directly hire shoppers.

Laura says, "I'd go on a cruise for free, but I think mystery shopping companies that pay a small amount for a trip are taking advantage of people. I won't do those jobs anymore." However, many people still want to do these jobs.

Hannah, a 41-year-old lawyer, has done almost 500 visits for the Mystery Dining Company in her free time without pay or travel expenses. She has enjoyed expensive meals and hotel stays.

Hannah writes detailed reports after each visit, spending two to four hours noting everything from food quality to conversations with staff. She must remember all these details during her meal because she can't write notes openly.

A new survey by the Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development (CIPD) shows that over one million workers in Britain may have zero-hours contracts. These contracts let employers hire workers without promising any set hours or pay. Many people want the government to look into this more closely.

The survey talked to over 1,000 bosses. It found that 38% of people with zero-hours contracts work full-time, usually more than 30 hours a week. About one-third of non-profit groups and one in four public service groups use these contracts.

Peter Cheese from the CIPD says there should be a better look at what zero-hours contracts mean. He thinks about the good and bad sides for both businesses and workers.

Sports Direct, a big sports store, has been in the news. They use zero-hours contracts for almost all of their 23,000 workers. Other places like movie theaters and Buckingham Palace also use these contracts.

Vidhya Alakeson from the Resolution Foundation says if one million people really have these contracts, it's a big deal. She thinks it's too many to ignore.

Trade unions say employers force workers to take these contracts to save money and avoid giving benefits. Dave Prentis from the union Unison says most workers don't choose these contracts. They make it hard for workers to complain.

People with zero-hours contracts often find out their work hours just before they start. They don't get sick pay, but they should get holiday pay.

The National Trust, a charity, uses these contracts for seasonal workers. They say it helps them deal with changes in the weather.

Chuka Umunna, a politician, thinks these contracts should be rare. Some workers like the flexibility, but others feel unsure and insecure.

Some think these contracts helped keep unemployment down during tough times.

The survey found that 17% of private companies use these contracts, while 34% of non-profits and 24% of public services use them. Industries like hotels, schools, and hospitals use them the most.

More than one million workers in Britain might have jobs with zero-hours contracts. This comes from a survey of over 1,000 bosses by a group called CIPD.

Some places in the UK, like stores and Buckingham Palace, have been criticized for using these contracts. Workers on these contracts often don't get paid time off or sick pay. They also need permission to work somewhere else.

People with zero-hours contracts often find out their work hours just before they start. They must be ready to work extra hours with little notice. They might get holiday pay, but not sick pay.

Chuka Umunna, a politician, says while some workers like the flexibility of these contracts, others feel unsure and insecure about their work.

The survey shows that 17% of private bosses use zero-hours contracts, less than the 34% of volunteer groups and 24% of public groups.

Jobs in hotels, restaurants, and fun places are most likely to use these contracts. Also, schools and hospitals use them a lot.

A new count shows there are more tigers in Nepal than there have been since the 1970s. This gives hope to those trying to save the big cats, whose numbers have been going down in South Asia for 100 years.

The number of wild Bengal tigers in Nepal has gone up to 198, which is a 63.6% increase in five years, according to a government study. Maheshwar Dhakal, an ecologist with Nepal's Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation, said this is very good news.

The count was made using pictures from over 500 cameras in five protected areas and three wildlife corridors. More than 250 conservationists and wildlife experts worked on the survey, which cost about $250,000. Dhakal said a similar survey was done in India, and the results from both countries will be released later in 2013. India, which has 1,300 tigers in several protected areas, will take a few more months to complete its survey. Nepal has promised to double the number of tigers by 2022 from 121 in 2009.

Tiger skins and body parts used in traditional Chinese medicine are becoming more expensive because of increasing wealth in Asia. Criminal groups pay poor local Nepalis to kill tigers. The skins and bones are then passed to middlemen who take them to India, where the main dealers are located.

Some high-ranking officials help the criminal networks involved in the trade. Experts think the increase in tiger numbers is due to better protection of national parks and better management of tiger habitats in Nepal, where forests cover 29% of the land. However, Nepal needs to do more to protect the places where tigers live and the animals they eat.

As the number of tigers has grown, conflicts with villagers have also increased. In 2012, seven people were killed by tigers near national parks, compared to four in 2011. Villagers want better protection. The government is planning ways to protect tigers but should also plan to protect people from tigers, said Krishna Bhurtel, a village leader. Wildlife officials caught a tiger that had killed two people, including one who was dragged from his bed in May.

Once, thousands of tigers lived in the forests of Bangladesh, India, and Nepal. Now, only about 3,000 remain, a 95% decrease over a century. Chitwan National Park in central Nepal has the most adult tigers, with 120, followed by Bardiya National Park (50) and Shukla Phanta Wildlife Reserve (17).

Diwakar Chapagain, who leads a World Wildlife Fund Nepal unit that watches wildlife trade, said tiger skins are popular in Tibet, where rich people wear them during festivals. In Nepal, kings used to stand on tiger skins for special events, and some wealthy Nepalis still display tiger heads in their homes. Tiger bones are used in traditional Chinese medicine, and selling tiger parts is very profitable, bringing thousands of dollars in illegal markets, Chapagain said.

I got a Dyson vacuum cleaner, but I'm not sure if I really want it. I just grabbed it, said Louise Haggerty, a 56-year-old hairdresser and waitress, at the end of her trip to the Black Friday sales at 1 AM. It was very chaotic inside. It was crazy and dirty.

Haggerty went to a 24-hour Sainsbury's supermarket in north-east London with a friend. She hoped to buy a cheap flat-screen TV. But many people pushed in the queue, so we didn't have a chance, she said. A woman who was second in line was pushed out by a group of young people. She didn't get anything. People were acting badly—it was terrible, she said. I only saw two security guards.

Frustrated that she couldn't buy a 40-inch TV that was reduced from £299.99 to £149.99, Haggerty quickly picked up a vacuum cleaner that was reduced from £319.99 to £159.99. I don’t even know how much it costs; I’m not sure if I will keep it. I just wanted something, she said. There are guys in there with three, four, five TVs. It’s not fair.

One of those guys was Andy Blackett, 30, who had two carts full of deals. I got two coffee makers, two tablets, two TVs, and a stereo, he said. I can’t tell you the prices, but I know they’re good deals. But his friend Henry Fischer wasn’t as lucky. Someone took my TV from me—I’m the smaller one.

Blackett, Fischer, and some friends drove to Sainsbury's at 12:45 AM after leaving a chaotic Tesco 24-hour supermarket, where the Black Friday sale started at midnight. Tesco was scary, so we came here instead, Blackett said.

More than a dozen police officers went to another Tesco store because fights broke out between eager and frustrated shoppers. Customers removed cardboard barriers that were holding back sale items until midnight. Tesco delayed selling its most popular items—TVs—for almost an hour until police controlled the situation. One officer criticized the manager for not having enough security and suggested stopping the sale.

Police stepped in at several other stores just before midnight. Manchester Police said that at least two people were arrested at Black Friday sales. South Wales Police also received calls from Tesco staff who were worried about the large crowds.

TV sales at the Tesco store began just before 1 AM. One of the first buyers of a flat-screen TV was James Alled. He bought two and was already trying to sell one to someone else in the queue. I bought them for £250. I’ll sell it to you for £350, £300 cash, he said. Further back in the queue, Christine Ball, 62, was not happy. I got here at 10:15 PM and I’m further back now than when I arrived, she said. These people don’t know what a queue is.

Ball hadn’t heard of the US-inspired Black Friday sales until now, like most of the shoppers. She said she came out to buy her grandson a TV for Christmas. Not one of those big ones; just a normal one for around £100, she said. In her basket was a pint of milk and a loaf of bread. TV, milk, and bread—the necessities, she said.

Mel Mehmet, 23, had been to Black Friday sales in 2013 and expected long lines, but she said the atmosphere in Tesco scared her this time. It’s crazy having the sale at midnight—the police must have more important things to do at night than come to sales. We’re going to PC World first thing tomorrow—their sale starts at 8 AM.
