Barack Obama told young people to stay hopeful and talk to those with different ideas if they want to change the world.

During his last trip to Britain as U.S. president, Obama spoke to 500 young leaders in London. He said, "Don't believe that we can't control things. Problems made by humans can be fixed by humans." He added that young people have better tools than ever to make a difference. He told them to avoid being negative and to know that progress is possible, but it needs hard work, self-discipline, and trust.

Obama acknowledged that young people face many challenges. He mentioned big events like 9/11 and 7/7, and how social media often shows bad news. The audience cheered when he was introduced. He talked about his policies on healthcare and education.

He advised the crowd to meet people with different views: "Talk to people who disagree with you. It helps you learn to compromise."

Obama was proud of his healthcare reforms and the U.S. response to the 2008 financial crisis. He also highlighted diplomatic deals with Iran and handling the Ebola crisis. He said, "I'm proud; I've been true to myself."

When asked about the Transatlantic Trade and Investment Partnership (TTIP), he said, "The answer to globalization isn't to close borders, but it's important to protect workers' rights."

Tanya Williams, a community officer, said she was excited to hear Obama because he inspired many people to vote. Oliver Sidorczuk, 26, said everyone was eager to hear Obama speak and planned to ask him about voting rights.

Obama answered a question from a young Sikh Londoner about racial profiling at airports. He said it's important to live together peacefully and praised American Muslims who are integrated.

Furqan Naeem, a campaigner, noted that Obama celebrated America's diversity and united communities. Kenny Imafidon, a youth organization manager, remembered Obama's advice on talking to people with different views and making compromises.

Later, Obama met with Jeremy Corbyn for a 90-minute discussion. They briefly talked about Britain's EU membership. Afterward, Obama played golf with David Cameron and attended a dinner with the British prime minister and U.S. ambassador Matthew Barzun before traveling to Germany.

It's well known that millennials use a lot of technology. Over eight out of ten say they sleep with a mobile phone near their bed. Almost two-thirds admit to texting while driving. One in five has posted a video of themselves online, and three-quarters have made a profile on a social networking site. However, a small number of millennials don't use social media at all. Here are four of them:

Celan Beausoleil, 31, from Oakland, California, is a social worker. She has had a Facebook account on and off. She last deactivated it in December 2015 because she found the amount of personal information shared by others too much to handle, especially with her demanding job. In her job, she listens to people’s lives all day, and it became overwhelming to see every detail of everyone's lives on social media, even those she doesn’t know well. 

Beausoleil loves how social media connects the world. She enjoyed exploring friends' connections on Facebook and ending up on someone's page from another part of the world.

Jason Mathias, 26, from Baltimore, Maryland, had Facebook and Twitter accounts for years before deleting them both in November 2012. He realized he was spending too much time on social media and wondered what he could do with that time instead. Now, he enjoys reading news articles and books during his free moments. He relies on friends to invite him to parties since he no longer follows them online.

Lauren Raskauskas, 22, from Naples, Florida, is very private. She recently deleted her Twitter account and deactivated her Facebook account two years ago because she didn’t like everyone knowing what she was doing. Her privacy concerns outweigh the benefits of social media. During a breakup, she appreciated not having to worry about changing her profile photo or status.

Hariharan Rajagopalan, 18, from Boston, Massachusetts, is a student at Boston College. He doesn’t see any problem with not using social media. Classmates who post about parties and events on Facebook also text him directly. He only joined Facebook to contact his future roommate before starting college, but he doesn’t use it anymore. As a sports fan, he knows Twitter is where most news first appears, but he refuses to get an account because he doesn’t need one to read tweets.

A new report says that six-year-old kids know more about computers and phones than 45-year-old adults do. This happened because fast internet came in the year 2000. Kids today learn to use phones and tablets before they can talk.

Jane Rumble from Ofcom, a group that checks UK communication, says kids use technology differently from older people. Even 16- to 24-year-olds use technology differently from kids.

Ofcom gave a test called "DQ" to 800 kids and 2,000 adults. The test checks what people know about tablets, smartwatches, fast internet, 4G phones, and apps. It also sees how happy people are using these things.

Kids aged 6 to 7 got an average score of 98 on the test. Adults aged 45 to 49 got 96. Kids aged 14 to 15 did best with an average score of 113.

Now, anyone can take a short test to get their DQ score. The website also gives tips on how to understand technology better and stay safe online.

How kids talk to each other is very different from how older people do. Before, teenagers talked on the phone for hours. Now, kids aged 12 to 15 spend only 3% of their time talking on the phone. All adults spend 20% of their time talking on the phone, and young adults spend 9%.

Today's kids mostly send messages or share photos and videos. Over 90% of their time using devices is spent sending messages on social networks like Facebook or WhatsApp. Only 2% of their time is spent emailing. But adults spend 33% of their time emailing.

When kids aren't using phones, they watch different things. Half of their TV time is spent watching live TV, while adults watch almost 70% live TV. Kids spend 20% of their time watching short videos on YouTube or news clips on Facebook. They also watch DVDs, Netflix, and recorded TV shows.

A new study shows that large predators like brown bears, wolves, and lynx are doing well in Europe. Many people think these animals will disappear because of more humans and overuse of resources. However, the study says their numbers are steady or increasing.

These animals live in about one-third of mainland Europe, mostly outside protected areas. This shows that better attitudes and conservation efforts are helping these animals that were once hunted a lot.

There are about 17,000 brown bears, 12,000 wolves, and 9,000 Eurasian lynx in Europe. Countries like Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg, like Britain, do not have these animals. But the lead researcher and others say these animals can live in places with lots of people, so even Britain could have them.

Wolves sometimes live near cities where there are up to 3,050 people per square kilometer. On average, wolves live where there are 37 people per square kilometer, lynx where there are 21 people, and bears where there are 19 people. In the Scottish Highlands, there are only nine people per square kilometer.

Guillaume Chapron from Sweden's University of Agricultural Sciences says we don't need to move people away to have wolves. He believes that letting people and predators share the same space works better than separating them.

Chapron says that while there can be conflicts, it’s important to handle these issues. Wolves can cause problems, but the real issue is disagreements between people about predators.

This sharing method could work in other parts of the world. Reasons for its success in Europe include political stability, more prey like wild deer, and help for farmers to protect their animals without killing predators. The EU Habitats Directive, which forces countries to protect rare species, has been very important.

George Monbiot, who is starting a charity called Rewilding Britain, supports bringing back wild landscapes and extinct species. He thinks Britain should do more to bring back large mammals like bears and wolves, which are returning to other parts of Europe.

The study also shows that the Eurasian lynx lives in 11 groups in 23 countries, with only five being original populations. This shows that reintroducing these animals is working. Monbiot believes that bringing lynx back to Scotland could work too.

A new study shows that brown bears, wolves, and lynx are doing better in Europe. Many people thought these animals might disappear because of more humans. But the study says their numbers are getting bigger or staying the same.

These animals live in about one-third of Europe, not counting Belarus, Ukraine, and Russia. They mostly live outside protected areas, showing that people are helping them more.

There are about 17,000 bears, 12,000 wolves, and 9,000 lynx in Europe. Some countries like Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg have no big wild animals. Britain also has none, but the study says these animals could live in Britain too.

Researchers found wolves near places with lots of people. Wolves live where there are about 37 people per square kilometer, lynx where there are 21, and bears where there are 19. The Scottish Highlands only have nine people per square kilometer.

Guillaume Chapron from Sweden says wolves can live near people. This shows that sharing land with wild animals works. It's different from keeping animals far away in protected areas.

Chapron says living with wild animals can cause problems, but it's important to solve those problems. Countries can use this way of sharing land because there are more wild deer for the animals to eat, and there is money for electric fences to protect farm animals.

The EU Habitats Directive helps protect rare animals. Without it, these animals might not be doing so well.

George Monbiot is happy about the increase in wild animals. He wants to bring back more wild animals to Britain. He thinks Britain can have more wild animals like the rest of Europe.

The visitors' center at the southern part of Doñana National Park in southern Spain offers a great view for bird lovers: 200,000 hectares of wetlands that are important for birds in western Europe. Many birds that migrate from Africa stop here each year. Doñana is also home to some of Europe's rarest birds, like the Spanish imperial eagle.

This beautiful place is fragile. In 1998, almost two billion gallons of acidic water mixed with waste metals flowed into the park from the Los Frailes mine 45 kilometers away. The polluted water went into the Guadiamar river and damaged the park. After the accident, over 25,000 kilograms of dead fish were collected, and nearly 2,000 birds, chicks, eggs, and nests were lost.

This was Spain’s worst environmental disaster, costing 90 million euros to clean up. Spain then spent another 360 million euros, partly from the EU, to restore the land. In the 1950s and 1960s, parts of the wetlands were drained to grow rice and cotton. Now, some of this farmland is being turned back into wetlands.

While restoration has been expensive, it has helped. However, Doñana still faces problems due to modern life. Plans include building an oil pipeline and new hotels and golf courses, which would use a lot of water. Soil from nearby farms is also clogging the channels in Doñana.

Conservationists are worried about the Andalusian government's decision to reopen the Los Frailes mine, which caused the 1998 disaster. Laurence Rose from the RSPB says, "Doñana is a crucial bird sanctuary for both native species and migrating birds. Bringing back the mine that caused the disaster is very concerning."

The reopening of the mine is partly due to economic reasons. Spain's bank crash in 2008 hurt the region, and unemployment is high. The mine could provide over 1,000 jobs. Vicente Fernandez Guerrero, an energy spokesman, says, "There are valuable minerals here that locals need. Modern mining techniques will prevent past mistakes."

Some people in the area support the mine, while others oppose it. Carlos Davila from the Spanish Ornithological Society warns, "Reopening the mine is a bad idea. They claimed it was safe before, but we had a major disaster."

Tourism is significant due to the park's birdlife. Visitors often carry cameras and binoculars. The park is special, with a vast sky above and many birds flying around. During a visit, a stork even stood in front of a car until it was ready to fly away.

Laurence Rose adds, "Spain doesn't have the same resources as before. Another disaster would be much worse." Davila agrees, saying, "After the disaster, Spain worked hard to clean and protect the park. Now, it seems we're forgetting those lessons. It's very disappointing."

The Doñana National Park in southern Spain is a great place for bird-watchers. It has 200,000 hectares of wetlands where many birds from western Europe rest during migration. Some of Europe's rarest birds, like the Spanish imperial eagle, live there too.

In 1998, a big disaster happened when toxic water from a mine 45 km away flowed into the park. Over 25,000 kilos of dead fish were found, and nearly 2,000 birds, chicks, eggs, and nests were lost. This was Spain's worst environmental disaster, costing €90 million to clean up. Spain then spent an extra €360 million to restore the wetlands.

Today, Doñana is still in danger. Plans to build an oil pipeline and new hotels and golf courses could harm the park. Also, sand and soil from nearby farms block the park's channels.

Recently, the Andalucían government decided to reopen the mine that caused the 1998 disaster. This worries many people. The RSPB says it is very worrying to bring back the cause of the disaster.

The government wants to reopen the mine to create jobs. Spain's banks crashed in 2008, causing high unemployment in Andalucía. The mine could create over 1,000 jobs.

Some people think the new mine will use safe technology, but others worry it could cause another disaster. Many tourists visit Doñana to see the birds, making it a special place.

Spain doesn't have as many resources as before, so another disaster could be even worse. After the 1998 disaster, Spain worked hard to clean up and protect Doñana. Now, it seems those lessons are being forgotten.

In the UK, restaurants don't have to give tips to workers. The government wants to change this. They asked workers, bosses, and customers what they think about tipping. The government thinks tips should go directly to workers and not include any fees.

Some waiters lose up to 15% of tips as an administration fee when customers pay with cards. The government might stop this practice. They also want restaurants to tell customers clearly about their tipping policies.

Here's what some waiters think:

Rodri, 37, from London, says about half of a waiter’s income comes from tips. He gets around £60 in tips each shift. He thinks the US treats waiters better. In 2015, many restaurants were caught taking money from tips. Some restaurants still take 4% of sales to pay chefs and cover fees, even if customers don’t tip. This makes waiters unhappy and can lead to bad service.

Elle, 22, from Edinburgh, works in a cafe and a restaurant. At the cafe, tips are shared equally. At the restaurant, she doesn’t get tips but earns minimum wage plus £2.50 per hour. She thinks France treats waiters better because being a waiter there is a secure job with a good income.

Ashley, 22, from London, works in a pub and a restaurant. Tips are shared among staff and used to pay for breakages. He thinks it’s unfair that tips are shared and used for breakages. He relies on tips because he only earns £7 an hour. He prefers a higher base wage like in Australia.

Tom, from Manchester, worked at a place where waiters kept 80% of cash tips and 40% of card tips. Tips helped him pay his rent. He thinks Italy treats waiters better. In Italy, customers usually round up their bills instead of adding a service charge. Waiters there often make a career out of waiting tables.

Introduction
In the UK, there is no rule that says restaurants must give tips to workers. The government looked at what people think about tipping. They want to change the rules so that low-paid workers get the tips customers leave.

Some waiters have to pay 15% of card tips as an admin fee. The government wants to make tipping clear and tell customers that tips are not required.

Waiters share their thoughts on tipping:

Elle, 22, Edinburgh:
She works three jobs. At her café job, tips are shared equally. At her restaurant job, she gets the minimum wage plus £2.50 per hour and does not get tips. At her event job, there are no tips. She thinks the system is better in France where waiters get good pay and job security.

Ashley, 22, London:
He works in a pub and a restaurant. Tips are shared at the end of the night, but money is taken out for broken items. He makes about £20 in tips but often only gets £10-15 after deductions. He prefers getting a higher base pay like in Australia.

Tom, Manchester:
At his old job, he kept 80% of cash tips and 40% of card tips. He makes about £40 in tips per shift. Good nights help him pay rent. He thinks Italy has the right system where customers round up their bills instead of leaving large tips.

Tea, baked beans on toast, and fish and chips are traditional British foods. However, tastes have changed over time. The National Food Survey, started in 1940 by the government due to health and food access concerns, shows these changes.

People in Britain love tea, but they drink much less now. Tea consumption fell from 68 grams per person per week in the 1970s to 25 grams. People now drink about eight cups of tea a week, down from 23 cups in 1974. Coffee is now more expensive than tea.

The survey includes data from 150,000 households between 1974 and 2000, plus information from 2000 to 2014. It shows that diets have become healthier, with more low-calorie drinks, skimmed milk, and fresh fruit. However, chips, pizza, crisps, and ready meals are eaten more often now.

There has been a big change from white to brown bread, but people are eating less bread overall, from 25 to 15 slices a week over the last 40 years. Baked bean consumption has dropped by a fifth, even though other convenience foods like Italian dishes have risen. Adults now eat 75 grams of pizza each week, compared to none in 1974, and pasta consumption has nearly tripled.

Fresh potato consumption has decreased by 67% since 1974, when adults ate 188 grams daily. Sales of vegetables like cucumbers, courgettes, aubergines, and mushrooms have gone up. Takeaway food consumption has almost doubled since 1974, from 80 grams per person per week to 150 grams. Chips (33 grams) and meat (56 grams) are popular, along with kebabs (10 grams), chicken (7 grams), burgers (5 grams), and meat-based meals (32 grams).

Fruit consumption has increased by 50% since 1974. In 2014, UK adults ate an average of 157 grams of fruit daily. Bananas are the most popular fruit, with 221 grams per adult per week in 2014, more than apples (131 grams) and oranges (48 grams). Low-calorie soft drinks made up half of all soft drinks consumed in 2014. People now spend 11% of their salary on food, compared to 24% in 1974.

Elizabeth Truss, the UK Environment Secretary, said food is central to society. The data shows what people ate 40 years ago and how culture has changed eating habits. By studying this data, we can understand past habits and predict new food trends. This information can help grow the food and farming industry.

Tea, baked beans on toast, and fish and chips are very popular in Britain. But, things are changing. According to the National Food Survey, British people drink much less tea now than in the 1970s. They used to drink 68 grams of tea per week, but now they drink only 25 grams. That's about eight cups of tea a week instead of 23 cups.

The survey got information from 150,000 families between 1974 and 2000, and from 2000 to 2014. It shows that people are eating healthier food. They drink low-calorie drinks, use skimmed milk, and eat more fresh fruit. But, they eat more chips, pizza, crisps, and ready meals.

People are also eating more brown bread instead of white bread. They eat fewer slices of bread now—15 slices a week instead of 25 slices. They eat less baked beans too, about 20% less. But, they eat more Italian food like pizza and pasta. Now, adults eat about 75 grams of pizza a week, and they eat three times more pasta than before.

People eat fewer fresh potatoes now. In 1974, adults ate about 188 grams of potatoes every day. Now, they eat much less. They eat more vegetables like cucumbers, zucchini, eggplants, and mushrooms. They also eat more takeaway food, almost twice as much as in 1974. About 33 grams of this is chips and 56 grams is meat. Kebabs, chicken, burgers, and meat-based meals are popular.

British people eat more fruit now. In 2014, they ate about 157 grams of fruit per day. Bananas are the most popular fruit, followed by apples and oranges. Half of all soft drinks are now low-calorie drinks. People spend less money on food now—11% of their salary compared to 24% in 1974.

Elizabeth Truss, the UK Environment Secretary, says that food is important to British people. She thinks that people care more about where their food comes from and enjoy different kinds of food from around the world. The National Food Survey helps us understand how food habits have changed and can help predict new food trends.

Agios Efstratios is a remote Greek island in the northern Aegean Sea. It's so far away that there isn't even an ATM or credit card machine on the island. Before Greece’s financial problems, the island did well. People came to visit its beautiful beaches and enjoy fresh seafood. However, since the banks closed, life has become very difficult. Islanders must travel nine hours to get cash, and tourists can’t find enough money to visit. This year, tourist numbers dropped by 80%. Mayor Maria Kakali says they have almost no bookings for August, which is usually their busiest month.

The mayor is trying to get the government to install an ATM soon, but she fears it might be too late for this season. Tourism is the main way people earn money on the island. The government also plans to end a tax break that helps islands. This tax break lowered prices for goods and services, making it easier for people to live and visit the islands. Without it, Mayor Kakali says, "We will all die on the island."

On Agios Efstratios, food and fuel are already more expensive than on the mainland. There are only three shops, two restaurants, and no official hotels. Everything has to be imported, and each seller adds profit, raising prices. The island and its neighbor, Lemnos, were starting to attract more visitors after getting better ferry service. But the bank closures hurt tourism badly. Lemnos has many wild beaches and cultural sites, but it will face higher taxes soon. Both islands are worried about losing young people if taxes increase.

Mayor Kakali hopes the tax rise can be avoided. If not, she plans to go to Athens to remind the government of the impact. She says the government doesn’t pay much attention to northern Aegean islands, so she wants to bring schoolchildren to show them the island is still alive.

Agios Efstratios is a faraway Greek island. It's ignored by banks, the government, and most people. There are no ATMs or credit card machines. Before Greece had money problems, the island did well. Every summer, people filled up the few rooms for rent and enjoyed the beaches, sea, and food.

Now, because the island only uses cash, closing the banks made life hard. Islanders must drive nine hours to get money. Fewer tourists visit because they don't have enough cash. Mayor Maria Kakali says tourist numbers dropped by 80%. Even people born there who live in Athens aren't visiting.

Kakali asked the government and a bank to put in an ATM, which should come soon. But she thinks it might be too late for this summer. She worries about next year because the government wants to end a tax break for islands.

The tax break helped people stay on islands when many left. For Agios Efstratios, losing the tax break is very bad. "If we have to pay 23% tax, we will all struggle," says Kakali. Food and fuel are already more expensive. In summer, there are only three shops, two restaurants, and no hotels.

Nearby Lemnos also faces problems. New ferries brought more visitors, but then banks closed. "It went from the best to the worst season in a week," says a travel agent. Lemnos has wild beaches, some nightlife, and cultural spots. It will pay higher taxes in fall 2015. The mayor says this will hurt the economy.

If taxes rise, more young people will leave. Agios Efstratios won't pay higher taxes until 2017. Kakali hopes things improve by then. If not, she plans to go to Athens with school children to show the government how bad it is.

Scientists have linked the brains of two animals, allowing them to share sensory information. This is a big step toward making what they call the world's first organic computer.

A US team put special devices called brain-to-brain interfaces on two rats. These devices let the rats work together on simple tasks to get rewards like water. In one test, the scientists used the internet to connect the brains of two rats far apart—one in North Carolina, USA, and the other in Natal, Brazil.

Miguel Nicolelis, who leads the research, is known for helping paralyzed people control computers and robotic arms with their thoughts. He says their new work could connect many brains to share information. Nicolelis stated, "We are creating what I call an organic computer."

First, the scientists showed that rats can share and use each other’s sensory information through tiny grids of electrodes placed in the brain area that handles movement.

The rats learned to press a lever when a light turned on above it. If they did it right, they got water. To test if the rats could share brain information, they put the rats in separate areas. Only one area had a light above the lever. When the rat pressed the lever, its brain activity was sent electronically to the other rat's brain. In tests, the second rat correctly responded to the brain signals and pressed the lever 70% of the time.

Amazingly, the communication was two-way. If the second rat failed, the first rat didn't get water and seemed to change its behavior to help its partner. In other tests, the rats worked together to tell the difference between narrow and wide openings using their whiskers.

In the last test, the scientists connected rats on different continents and used the internet to send their brain activity. Even though the rats were far apart, they could still communicate, according to Miguel Pais-Vieira, the lead author of the study. This shows that a network of animal brains in different places could work together.

Nicolelis said his team is trying to connect several animals' brains to solve harder tasks. He said, "We cannot predict what might happen when animals start interacting as part of a brain-net." In theory, a group of brains could find solutions that single brains can't.

Anders Sandberg, who studies the ethics of brain technologies at Oxford University, said the work helps understand how brains process information. However, the future uses of this technology could be much broader. Sandberg noted that humans dominate the planet because we are good at communicating and working together.

Sandberg added there is no risk of super-smart rats from this. There is a big difference between sharing sensory information and planning. He is not worried about smart rats taking over.

Little is known about how people encode thoughts or how to send them to another person's brain, so that won’t happen soon. Much of what is in our minds is just ideas that we don’t always act on or want to share. Most of the time, we are glad not to be in someone else's head.

Thousands of people protested on Australian beaches against a shark cull happening in Western Australia. They asked the state's leader to stop the policy. RSPCA Australia and Richard Branson also opposed it. The cull started after several shark attacks on Western Australia’s coast. In November 2013, a 35-year-old surfer died, making six deaths in two years. However, Australia averages only one shark-related death per year over the past 50 years.

Kate Faehrmann from the Sea Shepherd Conservation Society said the policy wouldn't work. She noted that drumlines, which are used to catch sharks, can harm any size of shark and other animals like dolphins and turtles. Protests happened in Perth, Sydney, Adelaide, and other places. Faehrmann said Australians want to protect sharks. Surfer Anthony Joyce, who had a close encounter with a shark, added that killing sharks won't make a difference.

The government hasn't said how many sharks were killed, but some sharks smaller than three meters were reportedly released. Conservationists argue there's no proof the cull will reduce shark attacks since no previous cull used only drumlines. Researchers believe the rise in attacks might be due to Western Australia's fast-growing population, not more sharks.

Richard Peirce from the Shark Trust said the cull is ineffective and could attract more predators. He criticized the government for ignoring good advice. Worldwide, in 2012, there were 80 shark attacks, seven of which were fatal, while humans kill almost 100 million sharks yearly.

RSPCA Australia stated there's no evidence that more sharks caused the attacks. Instead, it's likely due to more people in the water. Richard Branson said the policy isn't working and could hurt tourism.

People are against killing big sharks in Western Australia. Many people went to beaches to ask the leader to stop this. Some famous people like Richard Branson also said it's not right. The government started killing sharks longer than three meters after six people died from shark attacks in two years. But, in Australia, only one person dies from shark attacks each year on average.

Kate Faehrmann, who works to protect animals, says catching sharks won't help. The traps catch many kinds of animals, not just big sharks. People in Perth, Sydney, Adelaide, and other places showed they want to save sharks. Even someone who had a shark bite him before thinks killing sharks won't stop attacks.

The government won't say how many sharks they've killed. Some small sharks were let go after being caught. Scientists say there's no proof that killing sharks will stop attacks. More people live in Western Australia now, so there might be more chances for shark attacks.

Richard Peirce, who helps protect sharks, says the plan won't work and might bring more sharks close to the beach. In 2012, there were 80 shark attacks worldwide, but seven people died. Humans kill almost 100 million sharks every year.

RSPCA Australia says the shark cull isn't needed. They think more people in the water cause more attacks, not more sharks. Richard Branson said the plan might scare people away from visiting Western Australia.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) wants the USA to fix its money problems. The US avoided a debt crisis and federal workers came back to work after a 16-day stoppage.

US President Barack Obama said the country needs to stop dealing with crises all the time. IMF leader Christine Lagarde asked for more stability.

The Senate made a deal that didn't give much to the conservatives who caused the crisis. The Republican-controlled House of Representatives approved the deal at the last moment.

The World Bank also felt relieved that the global economy avoided a big problem. Its leader, Jim Yong Kim, told politicians worldwide to keep focusing on policies that help economic growth and create jobs.

Stock markets in Japan, China, Hong Kong, and South Korea first showed relief when the Republicans gave up trying to block Obama's healthcare changes. However, markets in Asia and Europe didn't react much, as traders expected another fight in Washington in early 2014.

The shutdown cost the US $24 billion. China's news agency said the US put other countries' dollar assets at risk. China is the biggest lender to the US government.

Obama signed the bill just after midnight on Thursday. The Senate supported the bill from all sides. It gives a short-term solution, funding the government until January 15 and raising the debt limit until February 7.

Obama hopes this deal will end the uncertainty that has been affecting the country. He said he expects no serious budget fights or shutdowns in 2014.

Republican Senator Mike Lee said there might be more trouble ahead, but polls showed voters blamed Republicans for the crisis.

US Shutdown: Christine Lagarde Calls for Stability After Debt Crisis Is Avoided

James Meikle, Paul Lewis, and Dan Roberts  
October 17, 2013

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) wants the USA to handle its money better. Many workers came back to their jobs after the government closed for 16 days. President Obama said the US needs to be more careful with money. Christine Lagarde, who leads the IMF, asked for more stability.

The Senate made a deal that did not include what the conservatives wanted. Conservative Republicans almost caused a big money problem because they did not like Obama's health care changes. The House of Representatives agreed to the deal just in time.

The World Bank was happy that the world's economy avoided a big problem. Its leader, Jim Yong Kim, asked politicians everywhere to make rules that help the economy and create jobs. The shutdown cost the US $24 billion. Obama signed the law shortly after midnight on Thursday. The bill passed easily, with support from everyone in the Senate. It is a short-term fix. It gives the government money until January 15 and lets them borrow more until February 7.

Obama said he does not think there will be another big money fight or shutdown in 2014. At the White House, Obama said he hopes the deal will remove the worry that has been over the country recently.

"When this agreement comes to my desk, I will sign it right away," he said. "I hope next time it won't be so late. We need to manage our money better."

A reporter asked Obama if the crisis would happen again soon. Obama said no.

Earlier, Republican Senator Mike Lee said there would be more problems: "People keep asking if it was worth it. My answer is yes, it is always worth it to do the right thing." He added, "This is not over."

But the deal on Wednesday was very bad for Republicans. They did not get anything they wanted, and most people blamed them for the crisis.

What is it like to see the last of something? Sudan is the last male northern white rhino left on Earth. If he doesn't mate with one of the two female northern white rhinos at Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Kenya, there won't be any more northern white rhinos. Sudan is 42 years old, which is quite old for a rhino, and attempts to breed him have not worked yet. Besides Sudan and the two females at the conservancy, there are only two other northern white rhinos in the world, both females in zoos.

Sudan is protected by armed guards, which shows care but also highlights the danger he faces from poachers who kill rhinos for their horns to sell as medicine in Asia. Even though Sudan's horn has been removed to stop poachers, he is still in danger.

Sudan doesn’t understand how special he is. He walks around the reserve with his guards, and his big, wrinkled face has a sad-looking eye. His head is strong and made of tough skin, showing great power, but it is also very vulnerable.

Sudan looks similar to a rhinoceros drawn by artist Albrecht Dürer in 1515. Dürer drew this exotic animal from another land. In 1515, a live Indian rhinoceros was sent from India to Portugal’s king, who planned to give it to the Pope, but the animal died when the ship sank.

Humans often harm the animals they love. Since the Ice Age, humans have been killing animals they admired. Ancient paintings of European woolly rhinos in French caves show their power and gentleness. These rhinos were painted up to 30,000 years ago, and the same people who painted them may have helped drive them to extinction.

Today, many people love rhinos, but poaching is increasing. Rhino horn is believed to cure many diseases, leading to more rhino deaths. In 2007, 13 rhinos were killed by poachers in South Africa. By 2014, that number rose to 1,215.

The northern white rhino is almost extinct despite all efforts to protect it. Other types of African rhinos are also being hunted by poachers, and the situation is out of control. The Javan rhinoceros is also close to extinction. India has protected the Indian rhinoceros, but poaching remains a problem. Sudan is a magnificent creature. Have we learned nothing since the Ice Age?

What is it like to see the last of something? Sudan is the last male northern white rhino left on Earth. If he does not have a baby soon with one of the two female northern white rhinos at Ol Pejeta Conservancy in Kenya, there will be no more northern white rhinos. Sudan is 42 years old, so he might be too old to have babies. There are only two other northern white rhinos in the world, and they are both females in zoos.

In the picture, it looks like humans are being nice because armed men guard Sudan. But humans are also being mean because poachers try to hurt Sudan. Poachers kill rhinos to take their horns and sell them for medicine. Sudan's horn was cut off to protect him, but he is still in danger.

Sudan does not know how special he is. He walks around the reserve with his guards. His head is strong and powerful, but it is also very vulnerable.

Sudan looks similar to a rhinoceros drawn by artist Albrecht Dürer in 1515. Dürer made a drawing of an Indian rhinoceros that died when its ship sank.

People often kill animals they love. This has happened since the Ice Age. Ancient paintings of woolly rhinos in French caves show these animals were gentle and strong, just like Sudan. But the same people who painted these pictures also helped kill all the woolly rhinos.

Today, people love rhinos, but they also kill many rhinos for their horns. Northern white rhinos are the rarest African rhinos. Southern white rhinos and black rhinos are more common. But in some places, more people want rhino horns for medicine, which makes poaching worse. In 2007, 13 rhinos were killed by poachers in South Africa. In 2014, 1,215 rhinos were killed for their horns in South Africa.

Northern white rhinos are almost gone because of poaching. Even with guards, the poaching is out of control. The Javan rhinoceros is also nearly extinct. India protects the Indian rhinoceros, but poaching is still a problem there. Sudan is a majestic animal. Have we learned nothing since the Ice Age?

James Bond films are one of the world's longest-running and most successful movie series, with 23 films and over $6 billion earned worldwide. The latest film, Skyfall, broke records in the UK in 2012, earning $1.1 billion. There is a lot of excitement about the 24th film, titled Spectre. People wonder if Spectre can do as well as Skyfall.

Charles Gant, a film editor, thinks Spectre is on the right track. Skyfall was both modern and nostalgic, appealing to fans of Daniel Craig and older Bond fans. With the same writers and Daniel Craig returning, it looks like another success. Sam Mendes, the director of Skyfall, is also back. He brought top actors like Ralph Fiennes to the film. Before Mendes and Craig, the series felt a bit old. Each new Bond actor changes how the series feels, and some work better than others.

The early Bonds were very popular, sexy, and exciting. Adjusting for inflation, some 1960s films like Thunderball, Goldfinger, and You Only Live Twice did even better than recent ones. Licence to Kill is the worst-performing Bond film, and A View to a Kill is the second worst. Despite ups and downs, the Bond brand remains strong. Eon Productions, the company behind the films, fought off other companies trying to use the Bond name. They now have full control over the books Casino Royale and Thunderball.

In 1995, Martin Campbell directed GoldenEye, which included an impressive stunt where Bond freefalls into a plane. This scene helped modernize the series and attract a new audience. The GoldenEye video game also contributed to the film's success.

James Bond films are very old and popular. There are twenty-three films. They made more than $6 billion in movie theaters. Skyfall, from 2012, made $1.1 billion and was the biggest film in UK cinemas.

People are excited about the 24th film called Spectre. Charles Gant, who works for Heat magazine, thinks Spectre can be as good as Skyfall. Skyfall was both modern and old-fashioned, which made many people like it.

Eon Productions makes the official Bond films. They want the new film to do well. They are using the same team from Skyfall. Daniel Craig will be Bond again, and Sam Mendes will direct. Mendes is good with actors like Ralph Fiennes.

Before Mendes and Craig, the films were getting boring. Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, and Pierce Brosnan all played Bond. Dalton only did two films, and Lazenby did one. Brosnan was more successful, but Craig is the best.

Skyfall made the most money, but some 1960s films were close. Thunderball, Goldfinger, and You Only Live Twice did well too. Licence to Kill made the least money, and A View to a Kill made the second least.

GoldenEye, from 1995, had a big stunt where Bond falls into a plane. This made the films more modern and got new fans.

An agreement to make clothing factories in Bangladesh safer might face legal issues because factory owners want money for closing and fixing their buildings. Repairs can take months, and owners say they can't pay workers when factories are closed. This problem started after the Rana Plaza building collapsed in Dhaka in 2013, killing 1,138 people.

Under the Accord on Fire and Building Safety in Bangladesh, hundreds of factories each month are checked for fire and structure problems. Over 170 international brands like Primark and Marks & Spencer support this accord, along with trade unions like IndustriALL.

One factory owner, from Softex Cotton, plans to sue the Accord because his factory was closed due to structural issues. He wants $100 million in compensation.

Another owner said that if a factory closes, even for a short time, it may never reopen. He thinks the Accord did not clearly state who pays for factory closures because they wanted many brands to join after the Rana Plaza disaster.

Jenny Holdcroft, a policy director for IndustriALL, said the Accord ensures factories won’t lose orders during closures. Brands agreed to keep buying from suppliers for two years. Twelve factories need major repairs, but some can still operate on other floors. The Accord also says brands must pay workers during closures.

Holdcroft explained that the Accord left payment details open so that factory owners who could afford repairs would pay. She said some disruption was expected for real change to happen.

A rival group, the Alliance for Bangladesh Worker Safety, backed by Walmart and Gap, set aside $5 million to help pay workers for up to two months while buildings are fixed. They found five factories in four buildings that need to stop production.

Shaidullah Azim, a director of the Bangladeshi Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association, said there is confusion about who pays workers. He asked the Accord to help pay workers or explain how they will support them.

An agreement to make clothes factories in Bangladesh safer might face legal problems. Factory owners want money for closing their factories and fixing them. Repairs can take months, and owners say they can't pay workers when factories are closed. They also can't pay for making buildings safe. These repairs started after a building called Rana Plaza fell down in 2013, killing 1,138 people.

Every month, hundreds of Bangladeshi clothes factories are checked for fire and building problems under an agreement called the Accord. The Accord is supported by over 170 international companies like Primark and Marks & Spencer, and trade unions like IndustriALL.

One factory owner in Dhaka, Softex Cotton, says he will sue the Accord because his factory was closed due to building problems. He wants about $100 million.

Another owner said that if a factory closes, even for a short time, it might never open again. He said the Accord does not clearly state who pays for factory closures.

Jenny Holdcroft from IndustriALL, part of the Accord, said the agreement ensures factories won't lose orders during closure. Companies agree to keep buying from suppliers for two years. The Accord also asks companies to make sure workers get paid during closures. Holdcroft said owners who can afford repairs should pay.

"Companies don't want to pay so that rich owners can keep profits without spending on their factories," Holdcroft said. "It's not surprising there is disruption. If there was no disruption, there would be no change."

A spokesman for the Accord said talks about payments and lawsuits won't stop their work to improve safety.

Now, there is more pressure on the Accord to help pay workers when factories close. Another group, the Alliance for Bangladesh Worker Safety, supported by Walmart and Gap, gave $5 million to help pay workers for up to two months.

"The Alliance is helping pay workers' salaries with factory owners, causing confusion. We met with the Accord to ask them to help or how will we support our workers?" said Shaidullah Azim from the Bangladeshi Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association.

Oxfam says the wealth of the world's richest 100 billionaires is making inequality worse and making it harder to fight poverty. The charity argues that when rich people get richer, it often means fewer good jobs and lower wages for poor people. This makes it harder for those who depend on aid or low wages to escape poverty.

Oxfam claims that the $240 billion earned by these 100 billionaires in 2012 could end extreme poverty four times over if given away. Usually, charities don't criticize the wealthy because they rely on them for funding. However, only some billionaires like Bill Gates and Warren Buffett have promised to donate much of their wealth, but details about how much they give each year are unclear.

In a report called "The Cost of Inequality," Oxfam calls on world leaders to reduce inequality to levels seen in 1990. The report shows that the richest 1% have increased their incomes by 60% over the last 20 years, and the financial crisis has sped up this trend.

Barbara Stocking, Oxfam’s Chief Executive, says that creating wealth for a few does not help everyone; often, it hurts the majority. She adds that inequality affects all parts of the world. In the UK, inequality is getting as bad as it was in the 19th century. In China, the top 10% earn almost 60% of the income, making it one of the most unequal countries, similar to South Africa, which is the most unequal country globally.

In the U.S., the top 1% now take home 20% of the national income, double what it was in 1980. Members of the richest 1% also pollute up to 10,000 times more than the average American.

Oxfam suggests that world leaders should follow examples like Brazil, which has grown while reducing inequality. Stocking urges leaders to agree to reduce inequality to 1990 levels. She also suggests closing tax havens, which hold up to $31 trillion, to collect an extra $189 billion in taxes.

Oxfam says the richest 100 billionaires in the world are making inequality worse and stopping the fight against poverty. If these 100 richest people gave away the money they made in 2012, we could end extreme poverty four times over. They made $240 billion in 2012.

Charities usually don't criticize rich people because rich people give them money. Some rich people like Bill Gates and Warren Buffett say they will give much of their money to help others, but we don't know exactly how much they give each year. Russian, Middle Eastern, and Chinese billionaires don't give as much to charity as American billionaires do.

Oxfam wants world leaders to stop big income differences and make things more equal. In the last 20 years, the richest 1% of people have increased their money by 60%. Barbara Stocking, the head of Oxfam, says we cannot pretend that wealth for a few helps everyone – it often does the opposite.

This problem is everywhere. In the UK, inequality is back to levels not seen since the 1800s. In China, the top 10% earn almost 60% of the money. China's inequality is now like South Africa's, the most unequal country in the world. In the US, the top 1% got twice as much of the total money in 20 years, from 10% to 20%.

The richest 1% pollute 10,000 times more than an average person in the US. Oxfam says world leaders should learn from countries like Brazil, which grew fast and made things more equal at the same time. Stocking says world leaders should aim to make inequality as low as it was in 1990. Closing tax havens, which hide up to $31 trillion, could get $189 billion in extra taxes.

The UK's prime minister, David Cameron, said the Scottish independence vote was clear. Scotland chose to stay with England and Wales by 10.6 points. Cameron promised big changes for Britain. He said there would be no arguments or repeats of the vote.

Scotland’s first minister, Alex Salmond, spoke at a party in Edinburgh. He said Scotland didn’t choose independence this time. Salmond called the vote a win for democracy. He said he would work with the UK government for Scotland and the rest of the UK.

The "yes" side won in Glasgow, Dundee, and North Lanarkshire. But the "no" side won in 28 areas, including Edinburgh, Aberdeenshire, and the Western Isles. In the end, "no" got 2,001,926 votes (55.3%), and "yes" got 1,617,989 votes (44.7%).

Cameron said there would be changes to the rules, but not until after the next big election. He said changes would happen in both Scotland and England.

Cameron said the people of Scotland decided to keep the UK together. He was happy about this. He asked everyone to work together now.

Ed Miliband, the Labour Party leader, said the vote showed Scotland wanted changes. He promised stronger powers for Scotland and changes for the whole UK.

Nick Clegg, the deputy prime minister, said the vote meant changes for Scotland and the UK. He said they need to give Scotland more power.

Nigel Farage, the UK Independence Party leader, said Cameron’s plan for England wasn’t enough. He said English people want a fair deal too.

Cameron will talk again about the results. He will explain how he will give Scotland more power over taxes and welfare. He wants to act quickly to keep promises made during the campaign.

The "no" side felt relieved because recent polls showed the vote was very close. The "yes" side almost won after getting more support.

David Cameron, the UK prime minister, is happy because Scotland voted to stay with England and Wales. 55% of people in Scotland wanted to stay together, while 45% did not. Cameron promised to give Scotland more power.

Alex Salmond, Scotland's first minister, said he accepted the decision. He called the vote a win for democracy and said he would work with the UK government.

In some cities, more people voted to leave, like in Glasgow where 53% wanted to leave. But overall, more people voted to stay together. The "no" side got 2,001,926 votes, and the "yes" side got 1,617,989 votes.

Cameron said there would be changes after the next election. He also said England would get changes too. He is glad Scotland stayed and wants everyone to work together.

Ed Miliband, the Labour Party leader, said Scotland wants change. He promised to give Scotland more power and to make changes in other parts of the UK too.

Nick Clegg, the deputy prime minister, said people voting to stay does not mean they don't want change. He thinks Scotland should get new powers.

Nigel Farage, the UK Independence Party leader, said Cameron's plan for giving England more power is not enough. He thinks English people want a fair deal.

Cameron will talk more about how he will give Scotland more power. He wants to act quickly to keep the promises made during the vote.

Brazilian singer Anitta has become very popular by making favela music famous, but she is in the middle of a debate about skin color.

Some people say that to be successful in Brazil's mostly white middle-class market, Anitta had to appear less dark-skinned. This idea started when photos showed her skin looking lighter after signing with Warner Music.

Jarid Arraes, a psychology student and blogger, criticized the media for promoting lighter skin as better. She says that in Brazil, white is seen as rich and successful, while black is seen as poor and unsuccessful.

Anitta, born Larissa de Macedo Machado, started singing in church and later became known in Rio de Janeiro’s baile funk scene. Now, she has a hit song called "Show das Poderosas" with over 52 million views on YouTube.

Her marketing team wants her to connect the poorer, darker neighborhoods with richer, whiter areas. However, some people question if she changed too much.

In Brazil, white workers earn about twice as much as black workers. Until 2011, black students went to school for two fewer years on average. Most top jobs are held by white people, while black and mixed-race people often do lower-paid work.

According to the 2010 census, out of 197 million people, 82 million said they were mixed race, 15 million were black, 2 million were Asian, and 0.5% were indigenous.

Sylvio Ferreira, a psychology teacher, thinks Anitta became popular by making rebellious music more acceptable to everyone. Maycon de Mattos Batista, who worked with Anitta, believes her image changed due to makeup and styling, not because she became lighter-skinned. He says her natural personality helped her succeed.

Anitta, a famous singer from Brazil, has many fans, but some people are talking about her skin color. They say she made her skin lighter to be popular with white people who have money.

Photos show Anitta's skin was darker before she became famous. After signing with a big music company, her skin looks lighter in pictures. This makes people wonder if having light skin helps someone be successful in Brazil.

Anitta, whose real name is Larissa de Macedo Machado, sang in church when she was young. Later, she became known for dancing and singing in Rio de Janeiro.

Now, she has a very popular song called "Show das Poderosas" that many people like. Her team wants her to connect poor black and mixed-race people in Rio with richer white people.

But some people think she changed too much. This is a big issue in Brazil, where many people have African roots. Lighter-skinned people often have better jobs and more money than darker-skinned people.

In Brazil, white workers earn twice as much as black workers. Black and mixed-race students used to go to school for less time than white students.

Most top jobs are held by white people, while black and mixed-race people often do harder jobs.

A 2010 count showed Brazil has 197 million people. Eighty-two million are mixed race, 15 million are black, two million are Asian, and 0.5% are indigenous.

Maycon de Mattos Batista, who worked with Anitta, says her look changed because of makeup and styling, not her skin color. He thinks her natural talent helped her become famous.

Pope Benedict XVI became pope in 2005. In February 2013, he decided to stop being pope because he was old and weak. He announced this in Latin, a traditional language. On February 28, 2013, at 8 PM, he officially stopped being pope. A new pope would be chosen.

A Mexican cardinal named Monsignor Oscar Sánchez Barba was there when Benedict announced his decision. They were in a room called the Sala del Concistoro in the Vatican. Benedict read from a piece of paper.

Everyone was surprised and silent. Cardinal Angelo Sodano, who knew about the decision, spoke briefly. He said they were confused and did not expect this. Afterward, Benedict blessed everyone and left. Everyone else left quietly too.

John Thavis, a reporter who wrote a book about the Vatican, thought Benedict might resign. In a 2010 interview, Benedict said he would step down if he could not do his job well. Thavis guessed the date incorrectly.

Soon after the announcement, Vatican officials said Benedict's decision was brave. He was not sick but was tired. Some think he might know more about his health than he shared publicly.

Benedict explained that being pope needs both mental and physical strength. He felt his strength was getting weaker. People will probably talk about why he resigned. Some think he might have been protecting himself from future problems, but the Vatican will deny these ideas.

Julia Rochester, a person from London who used to be Catholic, wondered how someone chosen by God could decide to stop being chosen. Many Catholics will ask similar questions to their priests.

In 2005, Pope Benedict XVI said he was a simple worker for God. In February 2013, he told cardinals he would stop being Pope. He said, "Starting February 28, 2013, at 8 PM, there will be no Pope, and a new one will be chosen."

A Mexican cardinal, Monsignor Oscar Sanchéz Barba, was there. He said the cardinals were surprised and sad. The Pope read from a paper and then left. Everyone left in silence.

John Thavis, who wrote about the Vatican, thought the Pope might quit. In 2010, the Pope said he would quit if he could not do his job well. Thavis guessed the date wrong.

The Vatican said the Pope's decision was brave. He is not sick but feels too tired to do the job well. Some people think there may be a secret reason, but the Vatican says there isn't.

Julia Rochester from London did not understand why the Pope would stop being Pope if he was chosen by God. Many Catholics will ask this question.

The school at Chemin des Dunes has a plastic roof and old chairs, but the students are working hard and hoping for a new life in France.

Kamal, a 29-year-old electrical engineer from Darfur, Sudan, studies French for three or four hours daily. He says, "The French language is very hard, but we try our best. If we come every day, maybe our dreams will come true." He believes keeping the mind busy is good.

Kamal is one of many refugees in the Calais camp who have asked for asylum in France and want to learn French. He is upset about how the media talks about the camp, saying it only shows people trying to sneak onto trucks or trains to the UK. He wants people to know that many want to stay in France.

France has more than 250,000 refugees, which is more than twice as many as the UK, even though both countries have similar populations. In France, there are 56,000 asylum seekers waiting for permission to stay, while in the UK, there are 36,000.

While waiting for their applications, France does not give asylum seekers money or let them work. This process can take many months. The camp provides a free meal and shelter under a plastic roof. Many choose to live in these conditions to avoid losing their chance to stay in France by working illegally.

The school started in July when some asylum seekers felt bored and nervous about starting a new life without knowing French. Zimarco Jones, a Nigerian man who came to Calais in 2013 and is still waiting for his application, founded the school. The small classroom holds 30 students and has classes in French, English, art, and tai chi. French classes are the most popular.

George, another Darfur refugee, used to want to go to the UK because he speaks English, but now he is happy to stay in France and learn French. He waits more than half an hour before class starts.

Local teachers volunteer at the school during their summer break. Jenny Flahaut, a 33-year-old teacher at a children's home, volunteers because she wants to help the people in Calais. She is upset about how migrants are shown in the media and by politicians who have not visited the camp.

The volunteers plan to set up a separate classroom for around 200 women and two dozen children. There are ten times more men than women in the camp, and many women feel uncomfortable studying with unknown men.

Zimarco hopes to start a football team for migrants and change the camp's name from "jungle" because it makes people think the residents are not human. He says, "We have a discotheque, a house, a mosque, a school, shops. We are not animals."

The school at Chemin des Dunes has a plastic roof and old chairs, but the students study hard. They hope to start a new life in France. Kamal, a refugee from Sudan, says, "The French language is hard, but we try. If we come every day, maybe our dreams will come true." He goes to classes for three or four hours daily. 

Kamal is one of many refugees living in the "jungle" camp near Calais. They have asked for safety in France and want to learn French. He says, "Not everyone wants to go to the UK. Many want to stay in France."

France has more than 250,000 refugees and 56,000 people waiting to know if they can stay. While waiting, they cannot work or get money from France. The camp gives them a free meal and a plastic roof. Many choose to live there and not work illegally so they can stay in France.

The school started in July. It was created by refugees who were bored and worried about starting a new life without knowing French. Zimarco Jones, a Nigerian man who came to Calais in 2013, started the school. He hopes to build another school soon.

The small room holds 30 students. There are five rows of desks, a big green chalkboard, and pictures of cartoon animals for each letter of the French alphabet. Classes in English, art, and tai chi are also offered, but French is the favorite. Teachers are volunteers from Calais and other places.

George, another student, says, "French is harder than English, but I decided to stay in France." He waits more than half an hour before class starts.

Volunteers include local teachers who give up their summer break. Jenny Flahaut, a 33-year-old teacher at a children's home, volunteers after seeing an ad on Facebook. She says, "These people are good. They want to improve their lives."

Teachers and Zimarco plan a separate classroom for about 200 women and 20 children. There are ten times more men than women in the camp. Women feel uncomfortable in classes with unknown men.

Zimarco dreams of making the camp a better place. He wants to start a football team and change the camp's name. He says, "We have a disco, a house, a mosque, a school, and shops. We are not animals."

In the Arctic parts of Canada, the sun shines for over 20 hours a day in summer. This is a big change from the dark winters. But for the growing Muslim community in Iqaluit, Nunavut, it makes the month of Ramadan very hard. During Ramadan, Muslims usually fast from sunrise to sunset.

Abdul Karim, a 29-year-old man who moved from Ottawa in 2011, says he hasn't fainted while fasting. He eats at about 1:30 AM before the sun comes up and breaks his fast at about 11 PM when the sun goes down. He will only stop if it harms his health.

Ramadan is almost over for Muslims worldwide. Fasting is important, but so is community work, prayer, and reflection. However, in Iqaluit and other Arctic Muslim communities, the long days force changes in how they fast.

Most Muslims in Iqaluit follow the timetable of Muslims in Ottawa, which is about 1,300 miles south. This follows advice from Muslim scholars who suggest using the timetable of Mecca or the nearest Muslim city. This means fasting for around 18 hours a day, according to Atif Jilani, who moved from Toronto.

The community of about 100 people often breaks their fast together at the city's new mosque. They eat traditional foods like dates and curries while the sun shines through the windows.

Muslims in other northern Canadian mosques face similar challenges. Many follow the Ramadan timetable of Edmonton, Alberta. Some follow Mecca's timings, like Awan, who wants a more manageable 15-hour fast for his 12-year-old son who just started fasting.

In Inuvik, a small town 125 miles north of the Arctic Circle, it is impossible to follow the local sun. They follow Edmonton's timetable. Ahmad Alkhalaf moved from Toronto to Inuvik in 2001. His first Ramadan was in December when there was no sun. They used Edmonton time then too.

Sometimes, it's hard to follow the clock instead of the sun. They break their fast when the sun is up, which is unusual.

In Inuvik, the Muslim community tries to balance Ramadan with local culture. Their iftar meal includes dates and curries, as well as local game like reindeer.

In Iqaluit, some think 2016's Ramadan was one of the hardest due to the long days. But Karim says that because of the lunar calendar, Ramadan will eventually fall during winter when the sun rises and sets quickly. He plans to follow those hours too.

Google has made maps of many places like mountains, oceans, and forests. They did not make maps of the Arctic before. Now, Google wants to make maps of the Arctic too. They went to Iqaluit, a big town in Nunavut, Canada. The team brought warm clothes, computers, and a big camera. They took pictures and collected information for four days. An Inuit expert helped them. 

In July 2013, people could see the town on Google's Street View. Usually, Google uses cars with cameras to make maps, but in Iqaluit, they had to walk because some roads are made of ice and melt in summer. They also walked on a long road called the Road to Nowhere, even though there were warnings about polar bears. 

Google found that some roads were missing on their old maps. Many homes and businesses get mail at the post office, so putting those addresses on the map would put everything in one spot. About 30 people from the town helped Google fix this by showing where things should be on the map.

Arif Sayani, who plans things for the town, said the maps would help people who want to visit or move there. It could also help make decisions faster. Google hopes to do this in other northern towns, but it costs a lot to move people and equipment. So, they might send equipment and ask volunteers to finish the maps.

The US Senate Intelligence Committee approved a bill that would make the National Security Agency's (NSA) collection of US phone records more open but still allow it to happen. The bill, introduced by Chairwoman Dianne Feinstein, lets the NSA keep collecting phone data from millions of Americans and storing it. The bill passed the committee with an 11-4 vote and will now go to the full Senate for a vote.

The bill allows analysts to look at the data if they think there is a good reason to suspect someone is linked to international terrorism. It also lets the NSA continue watching foreigners who come to the US for up to 72 hours.

This bill goes against another bill by Senator Patrick Leahy, which would stop the NSA from collecting domestic phone records. It was also opposed by Senator Mark Udall, who said it doesn't do enough to protect privacy. Udall believes the NSA's surveillance of Americans' private information does not respect constitutional rights and needs major changes.

Feinstein defended the NSA's program, saying it helps national security, but admitted more needs to be done to gain public trust. She said the bill would improve transparency and add checks on the NSA. For instance, someone who improperly accesses data under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) could face up to ten years in prison. There would also be limits on how many contacts an analyst can get from a request for bulk communication records.

Feinstein strongly supports the NSA's main domestic program, saying it is very important for protecting the country. However, some legal experts disagree. Elizabeth Goitein from the Brennan Center for Justice said the bill and another bill called the USA Freedom Act show different views on how much the government should know about law-abiding Americans.

Senator Ron Wyden, a Democrat, thinks the focus on spying on foreign leaders has distracted from the issue of mass surveillance in the US. He wants to stop the large-scale monitoring of millions of Americans. Wyden also opposes the NSA's spying on foreign leaders like German Chancellor Angela Merkel.

Wyden stated that Americans want to keep their constitutional rights and won't accept giving them up for security. He plans to keep fighting against the NSA's practices. 

Feinstein's support for collecting domestic phone records shows she is not ready to criticize the NSA as much as she did when opposing its spying on foreign leaders. Wyden added that with global communication systems, spying on foreigners can affect US citizens too.

The US Senate Intelligence Committee agreed on a bill that lets the National Security Agency (NSA) keep collecting US phone records. It also makes the NSA's work more open.

Dianne Feinstein, the committee's leader, made the bill. The bill lets the NSA collect information about phone calls from millions of Americans and keep the data. Eleven people voted for the bill and four voted against it. The full Senate will vote next.

The bill lets analysts look at the data if they think someone might be linked to international terrorism. It also lets the NSA watch foreigners in the US for less than 72 hours.

Another bill, called the USA Freedom Act, was introduced by Senator Patrick Leahy. This bill stops the collection of phone records in the US. Feinstein said the NSA program is legal and makes the country safer, but people don't trust the NSA. She thinks they need to make the NSA more open and get public support for privacy.

Feinstein said the bill would make the NSA more open and add rules. For example, if someone looks at data without permission, they could go to jail for up to ten years.

Independent experts worry about the Intelligence Committee's bill. Elizabeth Goitein said the bills show different ideas about how the government should treat Americans' private information. Ron Wyden said the focus on spying on foreign leaders takes attention away from the bigger issue of checking Americans' data.

Feinstein disagrees with spying on foreign leaders like German Chancellor Angela Merkel but agrees with collecting Americans' phone records. Wyden said Americans want to keep their freedom and will keep fighting this issue.

Ship noise might bother animals like killer whales and dolphins more than we thought before. New studies show that underwater sounds can make it hard for these animals to talk to each other and find food. For a long time, people knew that the low hum of ships bothered big whales. Now, US researchers found that medium and high-frequency noises, especially at 20,000Hz, where killer whales hear best, can also cause trouble.

These noises can make it difficult for killer whales to communicate and use sound to find their food. Dolphins and porpoises, which also hear at high frequencies, might have similar issues. The findings suggest that noise from ships could affect the endangered killer whales living near the shipping lanes along the west coast of the USA.

Scott Veirs, who led the research, says even a small increase in sound can make it harder for whales to use echolocation. Echolocation is when animals use sound to locate objects, like prey. Since the prey, chinook salmon, is already rare, hearing the faint clicks of a salmon is very tough for killer whales. More noise makes it even harder.

Researchers used underwater microphones to measure the noise from about 1,600 ships passing through Haro Strait in Washington State, USA. Over two years, they recorded the sounds from 12 types of vessels, including cruise ships, container ships, and military vehicles, which passed through the strait about 20 times a day.

Some ships are quieter than others, but the average noise level next to all ships was 173 underwater decibels, which is like a loud rock concert. Whales would hear noise of about 60 to 90 decibels, similar to a lawnmower or vacuum cleaner.

Veirs said scientists knew about the impact of underwater noise on large whales. However, the new research shows that smaller whales, dolphins, and porpoises are also at risk. Ships were thought to make mostly low-frequency noise, but the study found that the ocean's background noise is higher in frequency too, which could be a significant problem.

Ship noise may bother animals like killer whales and dolphins more than we thought. New studies show that underwater noise can stop these animals from talking to each other and make it hard for them to find food. We know ship noise bothers big whales. Now, US researchers found out it also bothers smaller sea animals like killer whales, also called orcas. Dolphins and porpoises might have the same issues.

Scott Veirs, who did the research, said, "Even a little more sound can make it hard for whales to find food using echoes." This is bad because the whales' food, salmon, is already rare. Hearing a salmon's click is very hard for killer whales. It's even harder when there's lots of noise around.

The researchers used underwater microphones to measure noise from about 1,600 ships passing through Haro Strait in Washington State, USA. They studied sounds from 12 types of ships, like cruise ships, container ships, and military ships, which passed through the strait about 20 times a day.

Some ships are quieter than others. The average noise next to all ships was 173 underwater decibels, which is like 111 decibels in the air—about as loud as a loud rock concert. Whales don't usually swim right next to ships, so they would hear noise of about 60 to 90 decibels—around the level of a vacuum cleaner.

All six numbers matched, so it's time to buy that Audi, plan a trip to the US, and call a real estate agent. That’s what most lottery winners do, according to a study.

Since 1994, the UK lottery has made 3,000 millionaires who have won over £8.5 billion, averaging £2.8 million each. Their winnings have also created 3,780 more millionaires among their children, family, and friends, says Oxford Economics.

Most winners (59%) stop working right away, while 19% keep working and 31% do volunteer work. Good for the economy, 98% of the money winners spend stays in the UK. Each winner’s spending supports six jobs for a year.

Winners have added almost £750 million to the GDP and paid over £500 million in taxes. They mostly spend on homes, with £2.72 billion on their main properties and £170 million to pay off debts. Investments cost £2.125 billion, gifts to family and friends were £1.17 billion, and £680 million went to cars and vacations.

Based on 100 winners who won over £1 million, the 3,000 winners bought 7,958 houses or apartments, spending £3.3 billion. Most (82%) moved to a new home, spending an average of £900,000.

New homes often include a hot tub (29%), a walk-in closet (28%), electric gates (24%), and a games room (22%). Some even installed a snooker table (7%).

Winners hired cleaners (30%) and gardeners (24%), and a few (5%) got a beautician. Audis were the favorite car (16%), followed by Range Rovers and BMWs (11% each), Mercedes (10%), and Land Rovers (5%). They spent £463 million on 17,190 cars, with an average price of £46,116.

For vacations, most (68%) picked five-star hotels abroad. The US was the top choice (27%), then the Caribbean (9%). Some (10%) bought caravans, adding £7.4 million to sales.

Some winners (15%) started their own businesses, 9% helped others start businesses, and 6% invested in or bought other businesses. These businesses employ 3,195 people.

Andy Logan, who wrote the report, said: "A win affects not just the winners' lives but also their friends, family, and the UK economy."

Scientists studied DNA from a wisdom tooth of a hunter-gatherer who lived in Spain about 7,000 years ago. This man had blue eyes, dark hair, and dark skin. He likely could not digest milk well and had trouble with starchy foods.

Farming began later and brought people and animals closer together. People developed better immune systems to fight animal diseases. However, this man already had strong immune genes that some modern Europeans still have today.

In 2006, cave explorers found two skeletons in a cave in Spain. The skeletons were very well kept because of the cool cave. Tests showed they were about 7,000 years old, before farming came to Europe. Scientists used DNA from a tooth to get the whole genome of one man. This is the first time they did this for a European who lived before farming.

The DNA showed the man had dark skin and blue eyes. This means blue eyes came before light skin in Europe. Artists usually show these people with light skin, but they should show them with dark skin and blue eyes.

The man's DNA was most similar to people now living in Sweden and Finland. The most surprising finding was that this man already had good immune genes, even though he lived before farming.

Carles Lalueza-Fox led the study at the Institute of Evolutionary Biology in Barcelona. He was surprised by what he found.
