Scientists have been waiting for new elements to be found, and now four have been discovered by researchers in Japan, Russia, and the US. These four new elements are the first to be added to the periodic table since 2011. They complete the seventh row of the periodic table, making science textbooks outdated.

The International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC), which controls chemical names and measurements, confirmed the elements on December 30, 2015. The scientists who found them need to give them official names. Right now, they use temporary names based on Latin: ununtrium, ununpentium, ununseptium, and ununoctium. These names show their atomic numbers, which are 113, 115, 117, and 118. An atomic number is the number of protons in an atom's nucleus.

IUPAC said a team from Russia and America found elements 115, 117, and 118. Element 113 was found by a team from the RIKEN Institute in Japan. This makes Japan the first Asian country to name an element. New elements can be named after myths, places, countries, or scientists.

In 2012, elements 114 and 116 were named flerovium and livermorium after the labs where they were found. Kosuke Morita, who led the Japanese team, plans to search for element 119 next. Jan Reedijk from IUPAC said the chemistry community is excited to finish the seventh row of the periodic table.

The Japanese team is thinking of naming ununtrium as japonium, rikenium, or nishinarium. Polly Arnold, a chemistry professor, said this work helps understand radioactive decay and can help improve dealing with nuclear waste. It also leads to new technology.

Scientists must also suggest two-letter symbols for the elements. After getting the suggestions, IUPAC will review them for five months. People can object if they think the symbols are not good.

To find the elements, researchers combined lighter nuclei and watched for radioactive decays. Ununtrium and ununpentium might be metals. Ununseptium could be a metalloid. Ununoctium might be a gas like helium, neon, and argon. It is hard to know for sure because so few atoms of each element have been made.

Paul Karol, who checked the elements for IUPAC, said it will take a long time to find practical uses for the new elements.

Prince Harry finished a four-month trip to Afghanistan. While there, he said he killed enemy fighters while flying his Apache helicopter. He talked about wanting a quieter life away from being a royal.

Harry expressed frustration with some parts of the media and mentioned his dad often told him to act more like a royal. As a pilot of a high-tech helicopter, he said he fired at the Taliban to help ground troops and save injured people. He felt he was just doing his job.

During his stay at Camp Bastion in Helmand Province, he discussed the challenges of balancing his different roles. In the army, he was called Captain Wales. He had one role in the army, one in his personal life, and one with his family.

Sometimes, he acted in ways that disappointed him, saying he might be too much like a soldier and not enough like a prince. He wanted privacy too.

In another talk, he criticized newspapers like the Sun, Daily Mail, and Daily Telegraph. He disliked articles comparing his job as a helicopter gunner to pilots in World War II. He said it wasn't the same at all.

His distrust of the media came from how his family was treated when he was young. Even though he read stories about himself, it upset and angered him. His dad often told him not to read them because they were usually bad.

Four years earlier, he had to leave Afghanistan during his first tour due to a media mistake by an Australian magazine. This time, the Ministry of Defence announced his deployment but asked newspapers and TV to avoid constant coverage so he could focus on his work. Reporters from BBC, Sky, and ITN visited once to report on his time there.

When asked if he felt more comfortable as Captain Wales than Prince Harry, he said yes. His dad often reminded him of his royal duties, but in the army, everyone wore the same uniform and did similar jobs. He enjoyed his work and got along well with others.

Before going to Afghanistan, he was photographed naked in Las Vegas at a private party. He said he let himself and his family down but also blamed the media for invading his privacy.

When asked why he and his brother liked helicopters, he joked that it was because only a few people could fit inside, so no one could follow them.

A new study shows that the Earth might get much hotter than scientists thought before. If we don't reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the Earth could warm up by at least 4 degrees Celsius by 2100. This is twice as hot as what world leaders think is dangerous.

The study found that as the Earth gets warmer, fewer clouds form. Fewer clouds mean less sunlight is reflected back into space, making the Earth even hotter. Professor Steven Sherwood from the University of New South Wales in Australia led the study. He says the research is important because it explains how clouds change and supports the idea that the Earth will warm up more than expected.

A 4-degree increase would be very bad. It would make living in many tropical areas hard or impossible. It would also melt parts of the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets, causing sea levels to rise by several meters.

Scientists measure how sensitive the Earth's climate is to greenhouse gases by looking at how much the temperature goes up when the amount of CO2 doubles compared to before people started using lots of fossil fuels. This doubling is likely to happen in about 50 years. For the last 20 years, scientists thought the temperature rise would be between 1.5 and 5 degrees Celsius. The new study narrows this range to between 3 and 5 degrees Celsius by focusing on how clouds form.

Some people doubt climate models, but Sherwood says these models are not perfect but are getting better. He adds that the models predicting less warming are more likely to be wrong. Some say the Earth's temperature hasn't risen much since the late 1990s, but this might be because most of the extra heat is going into the oceans. Also, a recent study suggests the pause in warming might be due to not having enough temperature data from the poles, where warming is the strongest.

Sherwood says his team's work on clouds doesn't completely rule out lower temperature increases, but there's no evidence to support this. A 4-degree rise would seriously hurt the world and many countries' economies if we don't cut emissions.

Scientists use computer models to guess future temperatures. These models need to include how clouds form. Sometimes, water vapor rises high enough to form clouds that reflect sunlight. Other times, it doesn't rise high enough and doesn't form clouds. Models that include both possibilities predict much higher temperatures.

Sherwood said, "Some people doubt climate models because they are not always right. But the models that predict less warming are usually wrong."

He also said that the pause in rising temperatures since the late 1990s is probably temporary. The Earth's average air temperature has risen slowly since 1998, partly because of an ocean event called El Niño. However, more heat is trapped by greenhouse gases, and over 90% of this heat goes into the oceans. Recent studies suggest the pause might be because we didn't have temperature readings from the poles, where there is the most warming.

Sherwood says that while his team's work on clouds doesn't prove that temperatures will rise by 4 degrees Celsius, it would have a big impact on the world and many countries' economies if we don't cut emissions.

There are many creative ways to make cities better places to live, like trees that glow at night, underground bike storage, and bins that use solar power. Living in a city can be great, but it's not always easy to live sustainably. Cities often face issues like pollution, traffic, and a lack of green spaces. Here are ten unique solutions to improve city life:

Pop-up parks: Many cities seem designed more for cars than people. Pop-up parks turn unused parking spots into small parks. This idea began as an art project in San Francisco and has now spread worldwide. People can create temporary gardens and ecology projects in these spaces.

Underground bike storage: With more people choosing bikes over cars, there's a need for secure bike storage. A Japanese company called Giken created an underground bike storage facility. This cylinder-shaped storage can fit 204 bikes and is only seven meters wide. Bike owners can get their bikes back quickly with a button press.

Glow-in-the-dark trees: Dutch artist Daan Roosegaarde made plants that glow in the dark. He combined DNA from glowing sea bacteria with plant DNA to create a glow similar to a jellyfish. His goal is to develop this technology to replace regular street lights.

Energy-harvesting floors: In London’s West Ham area, a special floor captures energy from people walking on it and uses it to power streetlights. This floor has smart tiles that turn the energy from footsteps into electricity. The company behind this, Pavegen, has also installed similar systems at London’s Heathrow Airport and other places.

Supertrees: Singapore’s Gardens by the Bay features giant man-made trees. These steel-framed structures, up to 50 meters tall, have flowers growing on them. They also absorb and release heat, collect rainwater, and provide air ventilation for nearby conservatories. Eleven of the eighteen trees have solar panels on their branches.

There are fun ideas to make cities better places to live, like trees that glow, bike parks under the ground, and bins that use sunlight.

1. Pop-up parks: Use empty parking spots to make small parks. This idea began in San Francisco and now it's used around the world.

2. Underground bike storage: In Tokyo, there is a deep hole in the ground that holds 204 bikes safely.

3. Glow-in-the-dark trees: A Dutch artist made plants that glow like jellyfish. He wants to use them instead of street lights someday.

4. Walking power: In London, a walkway uses the steps of people to make electricity for street lights. There is a similar walkway at Heathrow Airport too.

5. Big trees: In Singapore, there are tall fake trees called "supertrees." They grow flowers, catch rainwater, and have solar panels on top.

Every morning in Delhi, before it gets hot, a few old friends meet near the India Gate monument. They stretch, breathe deeply, and meditate on the dry grass.

Arvind Singh, a 42-year-old salesman, says this is the best way to start the day. He does breathing exercises at 6:15 am and thinks it's much better than eating breakfast or drinking tea.

Many people in India do yoga, especially in crowded cities where there is still some green space. On June 21, the new International Day of Yoga, Prime Minister Narendra Modi hopes many people around the world will join in.

Up to 45,000 people will do yoga for 35 minutes near India Gate. Modi, who is 64, and his government will join in. They hope some famous people will come too.

Modi wants more people to do yoga. After winning the election in 2014, he asked schools to make students attend yoga events on June 21, even though it is a Sunday. The police, who are often out of shape, might have to do yoga too. Three million civil servants and their families will get free yoga lessons every day. Even Air India plans to teach yoga to new pilots.

Modi first suggested an international yoga day when he spoke to the United Nations in New York in 2014. He said yoga is a valuable part of India’s old traditions. It helps people feel united with themselves, the world, and nature.

Yoga is between 3,000 and 6,000 years old and started somewhere in India. It has been linked to religions like Buddhism, Jainism, and Hinduism, which 80% of Indians follow.

Some people say Modi’s idea of Indian culture leaves out other traditions. But a US court said yoga is not always religious. Two Christian parents in California thought yoga in schools was a Hindu practice, but the court disagreed.

Amish Tripathi, who writes popular books about Hindu myths, says yoga was part of daily life in ancient India. Suneel Singh, a yoga teacher, says yoga is for everyone, just like tai chi or football. It is a good and cheap way to stay healthy.

Harvey Goldsmith, a famous rock promoter, says the big British summer music festivals, like Glastonbury, are ending. Goldsmith has worked with many big music stars, such as the Who, the Rolling Stones, and Madonna. He thinks there aren't enough new big bands to replace the old ones.

Goldsmith spoke at the Hay Festival in Wales. He said the peak time for festivals was about two years ago. There are too many festivals and not enough big acts to perform at them. This is a big problem in the music business. New bands like the Rolling Stones, Muse, and Arctic Monkeys are not being created.

In 2014, there were about 900 music festivals in the UK from May to September. Goldsmith believes they cannot all continue. Future events may include things like poetry, books, and magic shows, not just music. Small festivals offering extra activities will grow, instead of large fields where people struggle to find toilets.

Goldsmith, who is 69, is now working on a new theater in Wembley, London, for a stage version of "The Hunger Games" in June 2016.

At the Hay Festival, Goldsmith shared stories from his career. For example, Keith Moon used dynamite to clear a blocked toilet in a Sydney hotel. John Lennon had stage fright before a show in Madison Square Garden in 1974 and was pushed onto the stage while vomiting.

Goldsmith also solved a mystery about Elvis Presley. Elvis never performed outside North America because his manager, Colonel Tom Parker, was an illegal Dutch immigrant and didn't want to leave the U.S.

Freddie Mercury was Goldsmith's favorite performer. He called Mercury the best live performer ever. However, Goldsmith says there isn't a new band like Queen. Coldplay was the last big act, and that was ten years ago.

Without big acts to headline, there won't be big shows. Glastonbury, the top festival, can't find new big acts anymore.

Two people from the Marshall Islands found a small fibreglass boat on a remote beach. Inside, they found a very thin man with long hair and a beard. He said he had been floating in the ocean for 16 months after leaving Mexico, which is over 12,500 kilometers away.

The man, named Jos Ivan, was wearing only underpants. He said he left Mexico for El Salvador in September 2012 and had been alone in the boat since his friend died. His boat was 7.3 meters long and its engines lacked propellers. He survived by catching turtles and birds with his hands. There was no fishing gear on the boat, but there was a turtle inside when it washed ashore.

Ola Fjeldstad, a Norwegian student studying on Ebon Island, said the man's health was poor but improving. Islanders took him to another island to see the mayor, Ione de Brum. The mayor contacted officials in Majuro, the capital of the Marshall Islands. Officials planned to send a boat to pick up the man and bring him to the capital.

Jos Ivan stayed at a local council house and a family fed him. He had a basic health check and was found to have low blood pressure but could walk. He was given plenty of water and was regaining strength.

Fraser Christian, who teaches survival skills, said it was possible to catch turtles and small fish by hand because they are curious and might come close to a boat. However, the main dangers for someone stranded at sea are exposure and dehydration. Drinking water is essential to digest protein.

In 2006, three Mexicans survived nine months at sea by eating raw fish, seabirds, and drinking rainwater. But Cliff Downing, who teaches sea survival, doubted the man's story, saying it seemed unlikely due to many risks at sea.

Two people on a faraway island saw a small boat on the beach. They went to look and found a very thin man with long hair and a beard. The man said he was in the boat for 16 months after leaving Mexico, which is over 12,500 kilometers away.

The man, named José Ivan, was only wearing underpants. He said he left Mexico for El Salvador in September 2012. His friend died at sea a few months earlier. 

Ola Fjeldstad, a student from Norway, said the man's health was bad but improving. José Ivan caught turtles and birds to stay alive. The boat looked old and wet. 

The people who found him took him to another island to see the mayor. The mayor called the government in the capital city. The man is now staying in a town house and a family is feeding him. He had a health check and had low blood pressure but could walk. He is getting stronger with lots of water.

In 2006, three Mexicans were found after nine months at sea. They ate rainwater, raw fish, and seabirds. Another expert said he did not believe this story.

Other people have survived at sea too. Poon Lim stayed alive for 133 days after his ship sank. Dougal Robertson and his family were saved after 38 days. Three Mexican fishermen were found after nine months. Two men from Kiribati were rescued after 33 days. A Panamanian fisherman survived 28 days but his two friends died.

SeaWorld's profits have dropped by 84% because many people stopped visiting the park after claims that they mistreated orca whales.

SeaWorld trains dolphins and killer whales to do tricks for audiences. Since a 2013 documentary called "Blackfish" accused SeaWorld of mistreating orcas, attendance, sales, and profits have gone down. The documentary suggested that SeaWorld's treatment of orcas led to violent behavior and the deaths of three people. After the film came out, SeaWorld lost more than half its value on Wall Street, and its former CEO left the company.

Animal rights activists argue that orcas in tanks live shorter lives than those in the wild. To counter this, SeaWorld launched a marketing campaign to prove otherwise. They also lowered ticket prices and spent $10 million on marketing. However, SeaWorld CEO Joel Manby admitted that the company still struggles to change public opinion about how they treat their whales.

Manby stated, "We realize we have much work ahead of us." He added that while early feedback on their campaign has been good, fixing their image in California will be tough. He promised to fight with the facts, saying, "The facts are on our side."

In 2015, Manby gave a presentation on his vision for SeaWorld’s future. Plans include a new shark exhibit in Orlando and a dolphin swimming attraction in San Antonio.

SeaWorld’s financial report from August 6th showed that profits in the second quarter dropped from $37.4 million in 2014 to $5.8 million in 2015, a decrease of 84%. Revenue fell from $405 million to $392 million. Attendance dropped by over 100,000 visitors, from 6.58 million to 6.48 million.

Analysts will watch SeaWorld’s sales and attendance numbers in the third quarter, which usually brings in the most profit during the summer holidays. In July 2015, another scandal emerged when it was claimed that a SeaWorld employee spied on animal rights protesters.

Jared Goodman, director of animal law for PETA, said, "SeaWorld has a spying scandal, animals are dying in its tanks, and tens of thousands of people oppose its plan to build a new orca prison. Families don't want to see orcas in small tanks. SeaWorld's orcas won't recover, and neither will its profits, until it builds coastal sanctuaries instead of keeping them in tanks."

SeaWorld's stock price fell from $39 in 2013 to just under $18 in August 2015.

On a nice summer evening, I went swimming at Doolin Pier in County Clare, Ireland, where I moved in 2012. A woman was swimming with Dusty, a friendly dolphin who often swims with people. Dusty came to Doolin around 2008, and many people have swum with her, thinking she is very tame.

The woman was tickling Dusty's belly, which looked fun. About 20 people were watching from the pier. After I entered the water, Dusty suddenly became aggressive. She hit me with her nose, pushing me forward forcefully. Everyone on the pier was shocked.

Dusty stayed in the water, flapping her tail. I was scared she might hit me again and I could drown. I couldn't climb out due to my injuries and called for help. A man pulled me onto the steps. Another man, an orthopedic surgeon, checked me and said I likely had broken bones. Later, I learned I had six spinal fractures, three broken ribs, and a damaged lung.

In the hospital for five days, I missed work for five months. I also developed post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). I felt anxious, struggled with loud noises, and had memory problems. I had to close my health-food shop because I couldn’t work.

With therapy, osteopathy, and massage, I recovered and now run my own osteopathy practice. I understand patients better because I was one.

I am thankful to be healthy and want to warn others about the danger. Dolphins can seem friendly, but they are wild animals. Many people were hurt that summer. After the attack, Dusty seemed sorry. Our eyes met, and the fear ended. I made peace with her.

That day, a woman was playing with Dusty. About 20 people watched from the pier. After I entered the water, Dusty became angry and hit me with her nose. It hurt a lot. Everyone on the pier was shocked.

Dusty stayed in the water, moving her tail fast. I was scared she might hit me again. I couldn't get out because I was hurt. A man helped pull me out. Another man, a doctor, said I might have broken bones. Later, I learned I had six broken back bones, three broken ribs, and a hurt lung.

I stayed in the hospital for five days and couldn't work for five months. I was in pain and had post-traumatic stress. I felt anxious and had trouble with loud noises and remembering things. Now, I work as an osteopath and understand how patients feel.

I am glad to be healthy now. I want to warn others about the danger of swimming with wild animals like Dusty. Several people were hurt that summer. After the attack, Dusty seemed sorry. I forgive her.

We often see our friends and coworkers using e-cigarettes. But is vaping becoming less popular? Some statistics show that vaping among smokers and recent ex-smokers, who make up most vapers, may be decreasing. E-cigarette companies have invested a lot of money in this technology, thinking it would grow in popularity.

In 2014, the health charity Action on Smoking and Health (ASH) reported that the number of adult e-cigarette users in Britain tripled from 700,000 in 2012 to 2.1 million in 2014.

However, the Smoking Toolkit Study, which tracks smoking trends, shows that vaping's popularity may be falling. Vaping rates among smokers and ex-smokers increased until the end of 2013, when 22% of smokers and ex-smokers were vaping. But this rate stopped rising in 2014 and dropped to 19% by the end of the year. Professor Robert West, who collects these figures, says the drop is significant.

Smokers are the main group for e-cigarette companies because seven out of ten vapers are smokers. Only about 1% of people who have never smoked have tried an e-cigarette. The number of people who use e-cigarettes while still smoking is going down, West said. We've only been studying vaping for a little over a year, so it's a short time period, but we're not seeing growth in the number of long-term ex-smokers or never smokers using e-cigarettes. Vaping rates might change, but right now, they seem to be staying the same.

Vaping has stopped growing in popularity in the UK, which seems different from what is happening in the US, where the technology has been heavily promoted and appears to be growing in popularity. However, West questions the interpretation of US data, which does not clearly distinguish between people who have tried an e-cigarette once and those who vape regularly.

Experts think it is unlikely that vaping will become popular among young non-smokers. Only 1.8% of children are regular users, according to the ASH study. Instead, e-cigarettes seem to be most popular among adults who want to quit smoking. While the figures show that the use of electronic cigarettes by smokers has stopped rising, they also show a big increase in use since May 2011, said James Dunworth of ecigarettedirect.co.uk. Our customers are still very happy with the product, and improvements in technology are making the user experience better and helping them switch from traditional cigarettes.

E-cigarettes act like a nicotine patch, West agreed. They are more popular than nicotine patches and may or may not be more effective. One-third of quit attempts use e-cigarettes, making them the most popular method of stopping smoking.

Hazel Cheeseman, director of policy at ASH, said it is too early to say if vaping has reached its peak. Although there are signs that the market hasn't grown in the UK for about a year, there doesn't seem to be a decline in the number of people using electronic cigarettes to help them quit smoking.

The European Commission (EC) is considering increasing taxes on e-cigarettes, which could affect their popularity. A new EC tobacco directive coming into force in 2016 will limit the amount of nicotine in e-cigarettes to below current levels. This may mean vapers will need to use more e-cigarettes to get the same effect, making them more expensive.

West suggested that policymakers should view e-cigarettes as a tool to stop smoking and not regulate them the same way as regular cigarettes. Some local authorities and organizations treat e-cigarettes like regular cigarettes and ban them in public places and outdoors. This can make it seem like they are targeting vapers and undermine public health messages. We have to be careful not to stigmatize e-cigarettes.

Numbers show that smokers and people who recently stopped smoking, who are most of the vapers, may be using e-cigarettes less often now. Big e-cigarette companies are looking closely at these numbers because they spent lots of money on making e-cigarettes.

"The number of people who use e-cigarettes while still smoking is going down," West said. "We've only studied vaping for a little over a year, so it's a short time, but we're not seeing more long-term ex-smokers or people who never smoked using e-cigarettes. Right now, it looks like the number of people vaping is staying the same."

Experts think vaping won't become popular with young people who don't smoke. Only 1.8% of kids regularly use e-cigarettes. But e-cigarettes seem to be most popular with adults who want to stop smoking. "The numbers this month show that the use of e-cigarettes by smokers has stopped growing. But the numbers also show how much more people are using them since May 2011," said James Dunworth from ecigarettedirect.co.uk. "E-cigarettes are like a kind of nicotine patch," West agreed. "They are more popular than nicotine patches, but we don't know if they work better. One-third of people who want to quit smoking use e-cigarettes. They are the most popular way to stop."

The European Commission wants to put higher taxes on e-cigarettes, which could make them less popular. A new rule from the European Commission will start in 2016. It will lower the amount of nicotine in e-cigarettes. This might mean vapers will need to use more e-cigarettes to feel the same effect, making them more expensive.

Scarlett Johansson is suing a French writer named Gregoire Delacourt for 50,000 euros. She says his book makes false claims about her life.

Delacourt's book, "The First Thing We Look At," is about a French model who looks exactly like Johansson. In the book, the model has many adventures pretending to be Johansson and dies in a car accident.

Johansson's lawyer, Vincent Toledano, says the book uses Johansson's name, reputation, and image without permission. He also says the book has untrue things about her private life. He wants to stop the book from being translated or made into a movie.

Delacourt says he used Johansson because she represents beauty today. He says his character is not really Johansson. On the radio, he said it is sad that a judge might be involved just because he mentioned her in a book.

Delacourt is a popular French writer. His last book, "My List of Desires," was translated into 47 languages and is becoming a movie. He was surprised Johansson sued him. He thought she might want to meet him for coffee instead.

Delacourt believes it should be easy for writers to use brands, monuments, or actors in their books. He thinks Johansson probably hasn't read his book because it isn't translated yet.

A spokesperson for the book's publisher says it is crazy to sue over this. The book is not about Johansson but about a woman who looks like her.

In the U.S., the book would be protected by the First Amendment, which means it would probably not go to court there. But in France, personality rights are very important, so the situation is more complex.

Delacourt thought Johansson might like the book because it is a kind of love letter to her, but she did not understand it that way.

Hundreds of young Cubans are using the first free, open-access internet service in Cuba. This service is available at a small cultural center in Havana, provided by the famous Cuban artist Kcho. The state-owned telecommunications company, Etecsa, has approved this service.

People say the internet is slow, especially when many people are using it. In Cuba, only about 5% of people have unrestricted internet access. So, a place that offers free and unrestricted internet is very popular.

Many people are excited because they can now visit international news websites, talk to friends and family abroad, and use social media sites like Facebook and Twitter. Adonis Ortiz, a 20-year-old, uses the service to video chat with his father in the U.S., whom he hasn't seen in nine years.

As relations between the U.S. and Cuba get better, companies like Google and Apple may enter the Cuban market soon. Cuba has also set up a high-speed fiber-optic cable from Venezuela and uses some Chinese equipment for internet access.

About a quarter of Cubans have internet access, but this mostly means they use a restricted domestic network with limited websites and email.

Kcho, whose real name is Alexis Leiva Machado, allows the public to use his personal internet connection. He says he wants to help Cubans learn about the internet. Kcho, who has close ties to the Cuban government, got approval from the Ministry of Culture for this project.

At the center, young people spend their days using laptops, tablets, and smartphones. Cuba has very low internet connectivity rates, with dial-up connections tightly controlled and home broadband services rare and expensive. Kcho pays $900 a month to offer the free Wi-Fi.

Since 2013, Cuba has opened many internet cafes where an hour online costs $4.50, but the speed is much slower than at Kcho's center, which has a speed of around 2 Mbps. In the U.S., average internet speeds are around 10.5 Mbps, and in South Korea, they are 23.6 Mbps.

When many people use Kcho’s Wi-Fi, the speed slows down. Some users go there late at night when it's less crowded and find the internet to be much faster.

Scott Kelly stayed sane during his 340 days in space by thinking about Himalayan lakes, doing spacewalks, and following the US presidential campaign. He said it felt like he lived there forever. Kelly and his Russian colleague, Mikhail Kornienko, spent almost a year on the International Space Station (ISS) to study how weightlessness, radiation, and tight spaces affect humans. NASA thinks this research is important for a future trip to Mars.

Kelly found the mission's length the hardest part. He felt more sore when he came back to Earth than after shorter trips. He and his twin brother, Mark, took many physical and mental tests before, during, and after the mission to help NASA understand how the body deals with space travel.

When Kelly returned, he noticed the fresh air mixed with the sweet smell of the spacecraft that had gone through re-entry. He felt amazed by the size of the ISS, which is as big as a football field and has the space inside of a six-bedroom house. It runs on solar power and was built by an international team.

Kelly shared amazing photos of Earth on social media, showing cities, landscapes, oceans, and the atmosphere. He saw how thin the atmosphere is and noticed large areas of pollution. He could see smoke from wildfires in the US and constant pollution over parts of Asia. He believes it’s up to us to protect the air and water we need.

Kelly kept himself busy with tasks like waiting for new crew members, doing spacewalks, and running science experiments. He also followed the 2016 US presidential election. Being back on Earth with lots of people still felt strange to him.

Kelly doesn’t plan to fly with NASA again, but he wouldn’t rule out flying with private space companies like SpaceX in the future. He thinks in 20 years, people might be able to buy tickets for short visits to space.

Now back on Earth, things feel strange to Kelly. He may not fly with NASA again but might work with private space companies. He hopes one day people can easily visit space.

Junior Smart knows a lot about gangs. He is 36 years old now. His life can be split into two parts. When he was a teenager, after his mother died, he joined a gang in south London. The gang filled a big hole in his life. They became his new support group. At first, it was just fun, but then it turned into something more serious, involving crime. He left college and got a job in administration and worked as a DJ. But he also made money illegally with the gang.

He was caught for serious drug crimes and went to prison for 12 years. The night he was arrested was a big wake-up call. He realized he had been living a double life. In prison, he thought about changing his ways. Today, Junior runs a team of 12 full-time workers and six volunteers. Their goal is to help young criminals and gang members stop doing bad things. Many of his team members were criminals too. Some are still in prison but can leave during the day to help. They work with the police, probation services, and other groups to help people who feel stuck in violent gangs.

Junior's journey from gang member to helper started in prison. He saw many people keep coming back. He realized that the prison system only deals with the main crime, not the underlying issues. For example, one man had a drug habit and paid for it by stealing. He knew he needed to change, but no one helped him with his addiction.

Junior started helping new prisoners as a prison listener. Later, he planned to start his own program to use the experiences of former criminals to help others avoid going back to prison. He was released early after five years and started his project.

Junior thinks the police have done some good work in arresting gang members, but he is not happy with the government's approach. He believes that arresting gang leaders can sometimes make things worse. When a leader is arrested, others fight for power, leading to more violence. This can make the streets more dangerous.

Gangs are now recruiting very young children, even as young as eight to eleven years old, called "tinies." These young members do tasks like selling drugs or even hurting people to protect older gang members.

Junior finds it hard to help young people who earn a lot of money illegally, especially with high unemployment and less money for benefits. But his project, which helps over 1,000 people, is working well. Less than 20% of those who get help go back to crime. Junior believes everyone deserves a second chance.

Wales will be the first country in the UK to assume people want to donate their organs after they die unless they choose not to. The Welsh Assembly approved this new rule by 43 votes to 8, with 2 people not voting. Some religious groups and others worry this might upset grieving families.

Health Minister Mark Drakeford said this is great news for the 226 people in Wales waiting for organ transplants. He believes this will help more people get the organs they need.

Right now, many families refuse to let their loved ones' organs be used because they don't know what the person wanted. This new law aims to make people's wishes clearer and increase organ donations.

Opponents are concerned that hospitals might ignore the wishes of the deceased and their families. However, the government says the wishes of the deceased will be respected and families will have the right to object if they know the person did not want to donate.

Wales needs more organs because there aren't enough for everyone who needs a transplant. About one person dies each week in Wales while waiting for an organ.

Currently, only about a third of people in Wales are on the organ donor register, even though surveys show that over two-thirds of people are okay with donating their organs. Many just haven't signed up.

The new law applies to anyone over 18 who lived in Wales for at least a year before dying. Organs can go to anyone in the UK who needs them.

Doctors support this change because the number of people needing transplants is growing. While efforts to increase organ donations have had some success, more organs are still needed.

Some religious groups disagree with the new law, saying it could cause more distress to families. They believe organ donation should be a voluntary act of kindness, not something assumed unless objected to.

Wales will be the first place in the UK where people will be assumed to want to donate their organs after they die, unless they say no. The Welsh Assembly agreed to this plan. 

Mark Drakeford, the Welsh Health Minister, said, "This is a big day for Wales and for the 226 people waiting for organ transplants." He added that he is proud that Wales is taking this step to help more people get the organs they need.

When families know that the person who died wanted to donate, they usually agree. This new law will make it easier to know what people want about organ donation, which should lead to more donations.

The law is controversial, but the government promises to respect the wishes of both the dead person and their family. Family members can still say no if they believe the person did not want to donate.

Drakeford explained that Wales needs more organs for people who need transplants. About one person dies each week while waiting for an organ. Only about a third of people in Wales are on the organ donor list, even though more than two-thirds say they are okay with donating.

The new law will apply to anyone over 18 who lived in Wales for at least a year before dying. Organs donated from Wales can go to anyone in the UK.

Doctors are happy about this change. They have worked hard to get more people to sign up as organ donors and have improved how they talk to families about donation. However, they still need more organs.

Some religious groups do not like this plan. They think organ donation should be a choice made out of love and generosity, not something that happens unless you say no.

John Lewis's 2015 Christmas ad focuses on a lonely old man living on the moon. The ad has become a big part of the start of the Christmas shopping season. John Lewis plans to raise lots of money for Age UK and encourage people to help older folks who may be alone during the holidays.

The company spent 7 million on the campaign, which includes a TV ad, a smartphone game, and special items like glow-in-the-dark pajamas. They also made moon-like areas in 11 of their stores.

This year’s ad tells the story of a little girl named Lily who sees an old man living in a small house on the moon. She tries different ways to reach out to him, like sending a letter and shooting a note with a bow and arrow. Finally, she sends him a telescope tied to balloons, allowing them to communicate.

The ad’s message is "Show someone they’re loved this Christmas," which matches Age UK’s campaign: "No one should have no one at Christmas." Money from mugs, gift tags, and cards will go to the charity.

Rachel Swift, the head of marketing at John Lewis, says the ad reminds people to think about neighbors who might be alone. The ad uses the song "Half the World Away" by Norwegian artist Aurora.

The ad cost 1 million to make. The moon scenes were filmed at Warner Bros Studios, where Harry Potter movies were made. The set was designed by someone who worked on the Star Wars movie, "The Force Awakens."

John Lewis used a teaser campaign on TV and social media with the hashtag #OnTheMoon. A full moon happened on Christmas Day 2015, but this was just a coincidence.

Last year, John Lewis made an ad with a penguin and a boy, which got 22 million views on YouTube by early January. This year, John Lewis kept the same strategy of thoughtful gifts and going the extra mile for loved ones at Christmas.

Sarah Vizard, the news editor of Marketing Week, thinks John Lewis still does the best emotional ads. She believes people will find this campaign very sweet.

John Lewis made a Christmas ad in 2015. It shows an old man living alone on the moon. The ad helps raise money for Age UK. John Lewis asks workers and shoppers to help older people who are alone during the holidays.

John Lewis spent £7 million on the ad and other things like a phone game and special pajamas. They also made moon-like areas in 11 of their stores.

The ad tells a story about a girl named Lily. She sees an old man on the moon with her telescope. She sends him a letter and a telescope with balloons. This helps them become friends.

The ad's message is "Show someone they're loved this Christmas." Money from mugs, gift tags, and cards goes to Age UK.

Rachel Swift, who works at John Lewis, says the ad makes people think about helping others near them who might be alone.

The ad music is "Half the World Away" by Aurora. It cost £1 million to make. The moon scenes were filmed at Warner Bros Studios, where Harry Potter movies were made.

John Lewis showed a short video on TV and social media before the full ad. There was a full moon on Christmas Day 2015, but this was by chance.

In 2014, John Lewis made another Christmas ad with a penguin. It got 22 million views on YouTube by January.

Swift says John Lewis wants to make something good for the holidays that customers will love.

Sarah Vizard thinks John Lewis makes the best emotional ads for Christmas. She believes people will think the ad is very sweet.

Europe will be the first place to make car makers use real-world tests to check how much pollution their cars make. Right now, tests happen in labs where conditions are perfect. The new tests will show how much pollution cars make on real roads and in traffic. 

The European Commission approved these tests. They want cars to make no more than 80mg of nitrogen oxide per kilometer. Only one out of every 16 cars meets this limit right now.

Diesel cars make a lot of pollution, including nitrogen oxide, carbon monoxide, and tiny particles. This pollution causes at least 25% of the 29,000 deaths each year in the UK due to pollution.

The current test is very old and doesn't work well anymore. Car makers can change the results by doing things like taping doors and windows to reduce air resistance or driving on very smooth roads.

Lucia Caudet, who speaks for the Commission, says the new tests will help check cars better in real driving situations.

Greg Archer, who works on clean vehicles, says car makers cheat the tests, making more pollution on the road. He thinks the new tests are a big step to fight air pollution in cities.

In 2014, a study found that actual nitrogen oxide emissions were seven times higher than the 80mg limit, with some cars being 22 times over. About one-third of all nitrogen oxide pollution comes from cars, mostly diesel ones. In cities, this can be as high as 64%.

Car makers want to delay the new rules, saying it takes time to make changes. But the European Automobile Manufacturers Association (ACEA) accepted that the new rules will start in September 2017 for new car types.

The new rules will go to commissioners for final approval before starting in September. By 2017, the first real-world tests for CO2 emissions will begin. People around the world will watch how this works in Europe.

Europe wants to make the air cleaner. They will be the first place to make car makers use real-world tests for how much pollution cars make. These tests will show how much pollution cars make on real roads, not just in labs.

The European Commission says the tests are okay. All cars must make less than 80mg of nitrogen oxide per kilometer. Right now, only one out of sixteen cars meets this rule.

In the UK, 29,000 people die each year because of pollution. Diesel cars make a lot of this pollution.

The old test for checking car pollution is 25 years old and needs to change. Car makers can trick the tests by doing things like taping doors and windows to make the car smoother.

A study in 2014 found that actual nitrogen oxide from cars is seven times more than the 80mg per kilometer rule. Some cars are even 22 times over the limit. Cars cause about one-third of all nitrogen oxide pollution, and in cities, it can be as high as 64%.

Car makers want more time to make changes, but the new rule will start in September 2017. Countries around the world will watch how the EU does these new tests.

Some cities have pigeons, but Lima has black vultures. These birds fly in groups over the city and sit on buildings. They look like reminders of the city's problems with poverty and dirt.

However, these birds' habit of eating dead and rotting things is now seen as helpful. Environmental workers are putting small video cameras and GPS trackers on the vultures. This way, the birds can help find places where people throw away trash illegally.

Ten healthy black vultures, like Samuel, are part of this project. They fly over the city, find hidden garbage dumps, and record the locations on a map.

Alfredo Correa, who trains the vultures at Lima’s Huachipa Zoo, says the birds can eat dead animals without getting sick because they have strong stomachs that protect them from germs.

USAID and Peru's Environment Ministry are working together on this project to solve Lima's trash problem. A funny video shows the vultures as heroes fighting disease, while humans ignore the danger.

The project highlights a serious issue. With only four landfills for almost ten million people, many people dump trash illegally. About one-fifth of the city's trash ends up in these illegal dumps. This waste pollutes Lima's main water sources, the Rimac, Chillon, and Lurin rivers, which flow into the Bay of Lima.

OEFA, an environmental agency, reports that three poor neighborhoods—Villa Maria del Triunfo, Villa El Salvador, and El Agustino—have the most illegal dumps. These areas have 12% of Lima's population but account for most of the illegal trash.

One reason for this problem is that many people do not pay their taxes. This means some of the 43 district municipalities don't have enough money for basic services like trash collection.

Javier Hernandez, the project director, says they share the vultures' GPS locations with the municipalities. It's the municipalities' job to clean up the trash and change how residents handle waste.

The project encourages residents to report illegal dumping, reduce their own waste, and recycle. Some people are helping by posting photos of illegal dumps on social media.

A new report warns that up to a billion people could still be in extreme poverty by 2030 if countries do not address the reasons why people stay poor. The report by the Chronic Poverty Advisory Network says that even though many people might earn more than $1.25 a day, they can fall back into poverty due to issues like drought, illness, or conflict.

In rural Kenya, South Africa, and Ethiopia, 30 to 60% of people who escaped poverty fell back into it. In Indonesia and Vietnam, 20% of people who escaped poverty also slipped back.

For example, Amin from Bangladesh lost his livelihood because of his and his wife's illnesses, his son's marriage expenses, his father's death, and losing fishing nets. Lovemore from Zimbabwe became one of the poorest in his village after losing his job due to health issues and taking in five grandchildren after his daughter died.

Andrew Shepherd, the main writer of the report, says that just reaching $1.25 a day does not mean someone is permanently out of poverty. Many families fall back into poverty because they cannot recover from personal or larger problems.

The UN believes it is possible to end extreme poverty by 2030, but the report argues that more needs to be done. Although extreme poverty dropped from 1.9 billion in 1990 to 1.2 billion in 2010, progress in the next 15 years will be harder. Climate changes and deep poverty in parts of Africa will slow progress.

The report suggests focusing on people who are poor for many years and preventing others from becoming poor. Governments have helped people cross the poverty line, but they have not solved long-term poverty.

To help the poorest, the report recommends three policies: social assistance, education, and economic growth that benefits the poorest. These policies will cost money, so countries will need more tax revenue and aid. Many developing countries spend less than $500 per person each year, and even wealthy Nigeria spends only $650 per person.

The report also says that reducing conflicts and addressing inequalities, like access to land and fair labor markets, can help reduce both poverty and inequality. Governments should work with civil society to represent the poorest and change harmful social norms.

A new report says that almost one billion people will still be very poor by 2030 if countries do not fix the big problems that keep them poor. The report says that even though many people might earn more than $1.25 a day, they often become poor again when they face problems like sickness or drought.

In rural Kenya and South Africa, 30 to 40% of people who were not poor became poor again. In Ethiopia, this number went up to 60%. Even in countries like Indonesia and Vietnam, 20% of people who were not poor became poor again.

For example, Amin from Bangladesh became poor again because he and his wife got sick, his son's wedding cost a lot, his father died, and he lost his fishing nets. Lovemore from Zimbabwe lost his job due to illness and had to take care of his five grandchildren after his daughters died.

Andrew Shepherd, who wrote the report, said, "We need to make sure that people who are not poor stay that way. Many families become poor again when they have problems. Just earning $1.25 a day does not mean the problem is solved."

The UN thinks it is possible to end extreme poverty by 2030, but the report says countries must change to reach this goal. Extreme poverty dropped from 1.9 billion in 1990 to 1.2 billion in 2010, but the report says it will be harder to continue this progress.

The report suggests helping people who are poor for a long time and stopping others from becoming poor. It says countries should focus more on reducing long-term poverty. The report gives three ideas: giving help to the poorest, improving education, and making sure economic growth helps the poorest.

These ideas will cost a lot of money, and the report says higher taxes and aid will be needed. The report also says governments should create plans to help the poorest and stop customs that make poverty worse.

The best-selling book in the U.S. is a coloring book for adults by Scottish artist Johanna Basford. Her book "Secret Garden" has sold 1.4 million copies around the world. Her next book, "Enchanted Forest," has sold nearly 226,000 copies. Celebrities like Zooey Deschanel and South Korean pop star Kim Ki-Bum have shared images of the books on social media.

Eleanor Blatherwick, who works for the book's publisher, Laurence King, said the success has been amazing. She noted that while they knew the books would be beautiful, they didn't expect such huge sales.

Adult coloring books are becoming very popular. In the UK, other coloring books like Richard Merritt’s "Art Therapy Coloring Book" and Millie Marotta’s "Animal Kingdom" are also doing well. Half of Amazon’s top ten bestsellers in the UK are adult coloring books.

Ana McLaughlin from publisher Michael O'Mara says the popularity of these books is partly because they are marketed as a way to relax. The first coloring book they published in 2012 did well, but sales really increased in 2014 with the release of "Art Therapy."

The "Mindfulness Coloring Book" suggests that coloring can help reduce stress. It encourages people to spend a few minutes each day coloring to find peace and calm.

Basford says coloring is relaxing and creative. Many people find a blank page intimidating, but with a coloring book, they just need to add color. There is also a sense of nostalgia, as some people used to color secretly when their children were young.

Basford was surprised by the success of her first book, "Secret Garden," which came out in 2013. She thought it would appeal to people like herself who enjoyed coloring. Now, she is working on a third book.

McLaughlin believes the trend will continue. People share their colored pictures on social media and feel proud of their work.

Not many exercise classes have a tea break in the middle. But Margaret Allen's class does. After warming up and doing some quick exercises, the 93-year-old great-grandmother lets her group take a break with tea and a rest.

Some in the group of eight need more rest than others. Allen, wearing a thick shirt, knitted vest, pants, and sensible shoes, isn't even sweating. Even though she has a painful trapped nerve in one leg and needs a new knee, she looks like she could keep going for hours.

It’s usually not a good idea to eat right before or during sports. But when I visited Allen’s class in Saltburn-by-the-Sea near Middlesbrough, the ladies were having fruitcake during the break. The cake was made by Allen’s 89-year-old sister, Joan, to celebrate Allen’s birthday.

After finishing their cake, Allen leads the group through a lively Scottish dance with lots of toe pointing and leg kicking. The class lasts another 45 minutes.

Allen, a former volunteer with the charity Red Cross, has led classes in the town for 45 years. She wasn’t very sporty in school but started playing the piano for a fitness class during World War II. In her 40s, she took over when the previous instructor retired.

At one point, Allen’s class had more than 18 regular members, each paying £1 per session. Now, the group is smaller. During the tea break, they talked about a funeral they had attended that week for a younger member who had died at age 68.

Allen is the oldest, followed by her sister. The youngest in the group is 60-year-old Jean Cunion, who feels she might be the least fit. Ruth Steere, 76, says Allen always knows what’s happening, even with her back to the class. She yells if anyone makes a mistake.

Allen, who loves dancing, has never had formal training as a fitness instructor. She creates her own moves based on five tapes from the BBC’s first fitness expert, Eileen Fowler. Allen believes her good health comes from staying busy, especially since her husband died in 1997. She started writing poetry at 80.

Allen still plays the piano and gives speeches. At 88, she took a computer course. She admits aging isn’t fun, recalling a doctor who thought she was only 78. She told him, "Thank you, doctor. You can go now."

Allen has a straightforward view on weight gain: People shouldn’t eat too much. When she hears someone say they can’t lose weight, she suggests using tape to close their mouths. Her motto is “everything in moderation.”

In early 2013, Allen watched the news and saw a woman receiving the British Empire Medal. The woman said she was the oldest fitness instructor in the country at 80. Allen thought, "No, you’re not." But she won’t write to Buckingham Palace about it.

It started with a fake scallop, but a menu scandal has hit some of Japan's top hotels and department stores, hurting the country's food reputation.

After a luxury hotel chain admitted to lying about their menu ingredients, Japanese media found similar problems in other famous hotels and department store restaurants.

The Hankyu-Hanshin hotel chain in Osaka admitted to giving false descriptions of over 78,000 menu items from 2006 to October 2013. They claimed a flying fish egg dish was red salmon caviar, which is less common.

Hankyu-Hanshin’s president, Hiroshi Desaki, announced a 20% pay cut for himself and a 10% cut for other executives, but this did not calm consumers. Desaki later quit, saying the hotel group had betrayed customers. A head chef refused a government medal because of the scandal.

So far, the company has refunded 20 million yen to over 10,000 customers, with the total cost expected to be around 110 million yen. Customers who thought they ate expensive shrimp were told they had cheaper black tiger shrimp.

The scandal began when a customer wrote in a blog that a scallop dish at the Prince Hotel in Tokyo was actually a cheaper shellfish. The hotel investigated and fixed over 50 menu items at many of its restaurants. This made other hotels admit to similar issues.

The Hotel Okura chain, visited by Barack Obama, said they had added fat to beef to make it juicier and called tomatoes organic when they weren't. They apologized for letting down their clients.

Other frauds include selling carton orange juice as fresh, using Korean chestnuts instead of French ones, and passing off store-bought chocolate as homemade. Imported beef was sold as expensive wagyu.

Japan's top spokesman, Yoshihide Suga, said the labeling issues had lost consumer trust.

This scandal happened at a bad time. Japan is trying to convince South Korea and others to allow food imports again after the Fukushima nuclear accident. UNESCO is also considering adding Japanese cuisine to its cultural heritage list.

A local newspaper said "Japan's proud food culture is crying," and another paper was shocked by the industry's low morals.

Experts say the global financial crisis in 2008 pushed luxury hotels to cut costs while still attracting diners with detailed menus. Hotels used different foods when they couldn’t get the right ingredients.

The biggest issue may come from Japan's picky customers. In 2009, 72% of diners said the origin of food was the most important factor when choosing from a menu, followed by calorie and nutrition details.

A big problem at fancy hotels and stores in Japan is hurting how people see Japanese food. Some hotels said they told lies about what was in their food.

The Hankyu-Hanshin hotel group said they gave wrong information about food from 2006 to 2013. For example, they said "red salmon caviar" was on the menu, but it was really flying fish eggs.

Hiroshi Desaki, the hotel group's leader, said he would take a 20% pay cut, and other bosses took 10% cuts. But customers were still upset. Desaki quit his job because he felt the hotel group let their customers down.

The company gave back 20 million yen to over 10,000 people and plans to return 110 million yen in total. They also told customers that the expensive shrimp they thought they ate was actually a cheaper kind.

This problem started when someone wrote in a blog that a "scallop" dish at the Prince Hotel in Tokyo had a different, cheaper shellfish. The hotel checked and fixed over 50 menu items at many of their restaurants. This made other hotels admit they also lied to customers.

The Hotel Okura group, where President Obama once stayed, said they added fat to beef to make it taste better and called regular tomatoes organic. They said sorry for lying.

Other lies included selling carton orange juice as fresh, using Korean chestnuts instead of French ones, saying store-bought chocolate was homemade, and calling imported beef Wagyu.

This happened at a bad time for Japan, which is trying to sell more food to South Korea and other countries after the Fukushima accident.

Experts say the 2008 money problems made fancy hotels save money. They made nice-sounding menu descriptions but used different foods when they couldn't get the right ingredients, according to Hiroshi Tomozawa, a hotel and restaurant helper.

Philip Pullman, the author of the His Dark Materials series, says that downloading music or books without paying is like stealing. He thinks it is wrong and compares it to taking money from someone's wallet. Pullman, who is also the president of the Society of Authors, wrote this in an article for Index on Censorship. He believes that artists work hard for years to create something people enjoy, but then they cannot earn money from their work because of piracy.

Pullman says that if people want to enjoy someone’s work, they should pay for it. This idea has not changed even though technology has advanced.

Cathy Casserly, the head of Creative Commons, disagrees. She thinks that copyright laws, which were made a long time ago, do not fit well with today's technology. Casserly believes that people should be able to share and change other people's work more easily.

Rachael Jolley, the editor of Index on Censorship, agrees with Casserly. She says that current copyright laws do not work well in the digital age and might make regular people break the law. New ways are needed for artists to earn money from their work.

A lot of people illegally download things. Between November 2012 and January 2013 in the UK, 280 million music tracks, 52 million TV shows, 29 million films, 18 million ebooks, and 7 million software or game files were pirated. Ofcom, which checks on communication rules in the UK, found that 18% of internet users over 12 years old admitted to pirating content, and 9% were worried about getting caught.

British Prime Minister David Cameron talked about this issue with music industry leaders. He asked Mike Weatherley, a Conservative MP, to help solve the problem. The BPI, which represents the music industry, hopes that Weatherley and the Prime Minister will support copyright laws to protect artists and creators.

When Larry Pizzi first heard about electric bikes almost 20 years ago, he wondered why anyone would put a motor and batteries on a bike. This question still puzzles some people today. In the US, bicycle shops rarely sell e-bikes, even though they've existed since the late 1990s.

Now, Pizzi is the CEO of Currie Technologies, the top e-bike seller in the US. He thinks things are changing. Other bike makers like Trek, Raleigh, and Specialized also think the market will grow soon.

In the US, electric bikes are different from motorcycles or mopeds. They are bicycles that can be pedaled with or without help from an electric motor. Riding an e-bike feels like having a strong wind pushing you. The motor helps you go faster or climb hills. E-bikes are allowed on bike paths and can't go faster than 20 mph.

For e-bikes to succeed in the US, they need to overcome legal, cultural, and financial challenges. E-bikes are banned in some states, such as New York. Some bike shop owners don't like adding motors to bikes because it makes them heavier. Some e-bikes weigh close to 30 kg.

E-bikes are also expensive. Cheaper models start at $700, but a good e-bike with a good battery costs at least $1,500. The best ones cost more than twice that.

E-bike companies believe they can solve these problems. Battery technology is improving, making batteries smaller, lighter, more reliable, and longer-lasting. Big companies like Bosch and Shimano are entering the e-bike market, which may help convince bike shops to sell them.

More cities are building bike lanes, making cycling more popular. According to the US Census Bureau, the number of bike commuters increased from about 488,000 in 2000 to 786,000 in 2012. E-bikes make commuting easier and more enjoyable by helping with hills, headwinds, tiredness, and sweat.

Many customers are older baby boomers who want to cycle again but stopped because of hills. Companies like Pedego and ElectroBike are opening their own stores. Pedego has nearly 60 stores in the US and has sold bikes to tour companies in San Francisco and Washington, DC.

ElectroBike, which has 30 stores in Mexico, opened its first US store in Venice Beach, California, in fall 2014. It plans to open 25 US stores within a year. The CEO, Craig Anderson, wants to reduce traffic, lower carbon emissions, and promote a healthy lifestyle. He tells customers, "Ride this once and try not to smile."

Pedego and ElectroBike will face competition from bigger companies like Trek and Currie. Currie was bought by the Dutch company Accell Group, which is Europe's biggest e-bike maker. Accell owns Raleigh and Haibike.

Accell sees a bright future for e-bikes in North America. While baby boomers are important, many young people are using e-bikes for transportation instead of cars. Accell's Yuba brand sells a cargo bike with a stronger motor and a rear rack. It can carry two children or 45 kg of groceries, making it a minivan alternative.

Is streaming music about to become really popular? In 2014, only 41 million people used music streaming services worldwide. Even though it's growing fast, it's still small. Many users got it with their phone plans, so we're not sure how often they use it. Apple wants to reach 100 million users, which could bring in $12 billion a year. In 2014, the whole music business was worth just under $15 billion. Apple is good at making things popular, but it’s not perfect.

Will downloading music end? The iTunes Store opened in 2003 (2004 in Europe) when piracy was common. Apple convinced people to buy downloads and became a big player with 70% market share. In 2014, downloads were still 52% of digital music sales. Apple is the largest music seller globally. Download sales peaked in the UK in 2013 at £283 million and dropped to £249 million in 2014. In 2013, download sales also fell in the US, so Apple bought Beats for $3 billion to enter the headphone market and move from selling downloads to streaming. Apple can't abandon downloads yet, so both will exist under the Apple brand. Most people like music but aren’t willing to pay $120 a year for it. In 2014, the average UK music buyer spent only £39.52. Apple will find it hard to make people triple their spending on music.

Is Apple Connect making Apple friendlier to artists? Apple tried to be artist-friendly with iTunes, but it didn’t work. Apple Connect is different, combining features of YouTube, Facebook, and SoundCloud. Artists can post music, videos, and photos. Apple has good relations with the music industry and artists. Compare this to Spotify, which has faced criticism from artists like Thom Yorke and Taylor Swift. Apple wants to be on the right side of artists.

Will Apple get exclusive deals with artists? Getting exclusive albums is key for streaming services. Spotify paid a lot for Led Zeppelin and Metallica. Apple has AC/DC and the Beatles for downloads on iTunes. They may try to get these artists for streaming too. Apple got Beyoncé’s surprise album in 2013. Exclusive deals are easier for downloads since iTunes dominates that market. But for streaming, it’s different. Streaming now affects album charts in places like the UK and US, so artists won’t want to limit their audience by being exclusive to one service.

Will Apple Music hurt Spotify? Some think Apple Music will beat Spotify, but it’s not that simple. Apple is new to this market, while others have years of experience. The winner will likely be the company with the most money. Apple’s competitors are ahead but losing lots of money. Spotify lost €93.1 million in 2013. Apple started 2015 with $178 billion in the bank. If Apple Music loses money, Apple might stop it, but they’ll try to beat the competition first.

Is streaming music becoming popular?

In 2014, only 41 million people used music streaming services worldwide. This is a fast-growing area in the music business, but it's still small. Many users get streaming with their phone plans, so we don't know if they actually use it. Apple wants 100 million users paying $120 each year, which would make $12 billion. In 2014, the whole music business was worth about $15 billion. Apple can make things popular, but it's hard.

Is downloading music ending?

The iTunes Store opened in 2003 (2004 in Europe). Apple got people to buy downloads and became the biggest music seller with 70% of the market. In 2014, downloads were 52% of digital music sales. Apple makes most of this money. But in 2014, UK download sales dropped from £283 million to £249 million. In 2013, US download sales also fell. So, Apple bought Beats to switch from selling downloads to streaming. Apple needs both downloads and streaming now. Most people spend only about £39.52 on music in the UK, so getting them to pay $120 is tough.

Is Apple Connect good for artists?

Apple Connect lets artists post music, videos, and photos. Apple has good relations with artists and the music industry. Some artists don't like Spotify, so Apple tries to win artist support.

Will Apple have exclusive artists?

Exclusive rights to big albums are important for streaming. Spotify paid a lot for Led Zeppelin and Metallica. Apple has AC/DC and the Beatles for downloads, but it's unclear if they'll move to streaming. Artists often choose iTunes for downloads, but streaming is different.

Will Apple kill Spotify?

Some think Apple Music will beat Spotify. But Apple has no streaming experience. The winner might be the company with the most money. Spotify lost €93.1 million in 2013. Apple, however, started 2015 with $178 billion in the bank.

When talking about climate change, we often only talk about the problem and forget about the solutions. Solutions include faster recycling, reducing emissions, and finding better ways to use plastic, air conditioning, smartphones, and fast fashion.

Recently, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change met in Copenhagen to share a new report about climate change. They talked about the risks and challenges but also the solutions. The report shows that climate change is happening on every continent, and we need to work harder to reduce emissions before it gets worse.

At the meeting, the Sustainia Award, led by Arnold Schwarzenegger, honored ten top sustainable solutions used in 84 countries. These solutions cover areas like food, fashion, energy, transportation, education, and health. They show that there are ways to avoid the bad future we often hear about.

For example, in California, they found a way to make plastics from greenhouse gases that cost the same as regular oil-based plastics. In Switzerland, they have a better way to recycle and reuse old clothes and shoes. In Canada, they use smartphones to make bike-sharing easier.

One project, Wecyclers from Nigeria, won the Sustainia Award 2014. Wecyclers helps poor communities earn money by collecting and recycling waste in Lagos. Families can trade garbage for goods through an SMS-based point system. Recycling companies buy the sorted waste and turn it into things like mattresses, pillows, and trash bags. This helps solve the local waste problem, where only 40% of the city's rubbish is collected. Over 5,000 households are involved, and they plan to expand to other cities in Nigeria.

While many solutions to climate change involve advanced technology to cut emissions, we also need different types of solutions. Sustainability isn't just about lowering emissions; it's also about using natural resources wisely and improving our health. Some solutions may not be high-tech, but they can still make a big difference for whole communities.

To tackle the many challenges of climate change, we need to focus more on the solutions that inspire people and lead to positive changes.

When talking about climate change, we often focus on the problem and forget the solutions. Solutions include recycling, reducing emissions, and finding better ways to make things like plastic, air conditioners, phones, and clothes.

In Copenhagen, a big group talked about climate change in their new report. Climate change is happening everywhere. We need to work harder to stop it. They talked about both problems and solutions.
