One solution makes plastic from greenhouse gases. It's good quality and not too expensive. Another solution recycles old clothes and shoes better. Another one uses smartphones to make bike-sharing easier.

Wecyclers won the Sustainia Award in 2014. In Lagos, Nigeria, people collect street waste. Bicycles pick up the waste, and people earn points. They can use points to get things they need. Recycling companies buy the waste and turn it into products like mattresses and trash bags.

Only 40% of Lagos' waste is collected. More than 5,000 families are part of Wecyclers. They plan to start in other Nigerian cities.

To fix climate change, we need different solutions. We need to reduce emissions, use natural resources better, and live healthier lives.

BB King made much of his music in the blues style, but he liked other types of music too. He connected different cultures through his warm and skilled performances. It's hard to think of another blues musician who will be as great as King. He influenced many musicians and fans over his 65-year career.

Riley B King was born in Mississippi to African-American farm workers. He learned guitar basics from a family friend and improved his singing with a gospel group. In his early 20s, he moved to Memphis.

Soon after, he played at a bar in West Memphis and became a radio DJ. His stage name, The Beale Street Blues Boy, was shortened to Blues Boy King and then to BB. In 1949, he recorded his first song in Nashville. In 1950, he started recording for Modern Records in California.

His first big hit came in 1952 with "Three O'Clock Blues," which stayed at number one on the R&B chart for 15 weeks. This was the first of many hits. King created a unique style that was new but rooted in blues history. He often praised musicians like T-Bone Walker, Blind Lemon Jefferson, Lonnie Johnson, Charlie Christian, and Django Reinhardt who influenced him.

King said his guitar style came from his inability to play in the bottleneck style. He mixed the styles of ballad singers like Nat King Cole and blues shouters like Joe Turner and Dr. Clayton. He especially liked Louis Jordan, whose music he honored in the 1999 album "Let the Good Times Roll."

During the 1950s, King was the top blues performer, playing hundreds of shows each year. In 1956, he played 342 gigs. In 1962, he signed with a major label, ABC, but his first records there were not successful.

In 1965, his album "Live at the Regal" became very famous and inspired many young musicians. He had more R&B hits with songs like "How Blue Can You Get" and "Paying the Cost to Be the Boss." In 1969, his song "The Thrill Is Gone" reached the top of the pop charts, something no blues artist had done in years.

King gained popularity among rock fans thanks to musicians like Mike Bloomfield and Eric Clapton. With his manager Sidney Seidenberg, he toured internationally, visiting places like Japan, Australia, China, and Russia. He also performed for prisoners and worked on rehabilitation programs.

In 1990, King was diagnosed with diabetes and reduced his tours. He still performed outside the U.S. every few years. He mostly sat during his shows but his singing and guitar playing remained strong. For his 80th birthday in 2005, he released a Grammy-winning album with Clapton, Mark Knopfler, Roger Daltrey, Gloria Estefan, and others. Musicians like Bono, Amadou Bagayoko, and Elton John paid tribute to him.

In 2009, King won a Grammy for his album "One Kind Favor." In 2012, he performed at the White House with President Barack Obama singing "Sweet Home Chicago." King was married twice and divorced twice. He is survived by 11 children from different relationships; four others passed away before him.

BB King was famous for blues music but liked other kinds of music too. It's hard to think of another blues artist who will be as influential as BB King. He influenced many musicians and fans over 65 years.

Riley B King was born in Mississippi to African-American farm workers. He learned guitar from a friend and sang with gospel singers. In his early 20s, he moved to Memphis.

He played at a bar in West Memphis and was a disc jockey on a local radio station. People called him "The Beale Street Blues Boy," which became "Blues Boy King" and then "BB." In 1950, he started recording for Modern Records.

His first hit was "Three O'Clock Blues" in 1952. It was number one for 15 weeks. King made a new style of blues music. He said his guitar technique came from not being able to play in the bottleneck style.

During the 1950s, King was a top blues artist. In 1956, he played 342 concerts. In 1962, he signed with ABC but his first records there did not do well.

His 1965 album, "Live at the Regal," became famous. In 1969, his song "The Thrill Is Gone" was near the top of the pop charts. Rock musicians like Mike Bloomfield and Eric Clapton helped make him popular with rock fans.

King toured internationally and played for prisoners. In 1990, he got diabetes and had to play sitting down. For his 80th birthday in 2005, he made an album with famous musicians. In 2009, he won a Grammy. In 2012, he played at the White House with President Obama.

BB King was married twice and had 11 children. Four of his children died before him.

Kenton Cool's voice is very weak because of the hard work at high altitude. He is now in Kathmandu, the capital city of Nepal. He flew there from Everest base camp that morning. Cool talks about climbing three big mountains in one weekend. On Saturday, he climbed Nuptse, the first and smallest of the three mountains. Later that day, he climbed Mount Everest and reached the top in the dark early Sunday morning. Then, on Monday, he climbed Lhotse, the third mountain.

Cool says he used a special chance. For the first time since the late 1990s, there were ropes on all three mountains. This doesn't make his climb any less difficult. He thinks someone else will climb these mountains without ropes or extra oxygen soon.

Sixty years ago, Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay climbed Everest. Now, many people climb it, and it causes problems for the environment. Cool thinks about what climbers might do 60 years from now. He talks about a Swiss climber named Ueli Steck, who planned to climb Everest and Lhotse without ropes. Steck trained very hard and was a great climber.

Helicopters are now used more often to help climbers. A helicopter rescued a climber at 7,800 meters, which is the highest rescue ever on Everest. In the future, there might be a place for helicopters on the South Col to help more tourists.

Alton Byers, a mountain expert, says the Everest area cannot handle so many tourists. Climate change and tourism are causing problems. Glaciers are melting, and there is less water for farming and new hotels. In Namche Bazaar, a new pipe brings water to meet the needs of tourists. Garbage is put in pits near villages. Human waste at base camp is collected in barrels but later dumped in a big hole that could pollute the water.

Byers says these problems can be fixed if people try harder. For example, $85,000 can be spent on climbing Everest, but $500,000 could fix many of these issues.

Climate change is also a problem. Glacial lakes are forming quickly and could flood the Sherpa homes. Changing weather makes it harder to fly into the area. A new road is being built to bring more tourists, but Byers worries it will cause soil erosion and landslides.

Everest shows us how to solve problems like climate change and tourism.

On Saturday, he climbed Nuptse, then Everest early Sunday morning in the dark. On Monday, he climbed Lhotse. Cool used fixed ropes on all three mountains, something not seen since the late 1990s. He says doing it again will be harder without ropes or extra oxygen.

Everest was first climbed 60 years ago. Cool thinks future climbers might try new routes like Ueli Steck planned. Steck left Everest after an argument with Sherpas.

In Namche Bazaar, a Sherpa town, they build pipelines for water because the local stream is dirty. Garbage pits are everywhere, and human waste is dumped in a valley, which could pollute streams.

Byers says solving these issues costs money. One climber spends $85,000 to climb Everest. Solving problems could cost half a million dollars a year.

Weather changes affect tourism too. Cloudy days close Lukla Airport more often. A new road for 4x4 cars is being built to reach Everest, but Byers worries it may cause soil erosion and landslides. Everest is a good place to study climate change and tourism effects.

A new survey in 33 countries shows that people around the world have wrong ideas about important facts.

In Britain, people think the richest 1% own 59% of the wealth, but they actually own only 23%. Americans believe 33% of their population are immigrants, but it's really only 14%.

Brazilians think the average age in their country is 56, but it’s actually 31. Russians think 31% of their politicians are women, but it’s only 14%.

In Britain, people think 43% of young adults aged 25-34 still live with their parents, but it’s actually 14%. In India, people think 60% of the population has internet access, but only 19% do.

Why are people often wrong about these facts?

One reason is that people find math hard and sometimes misunderstand the questions. For example, people think 37% of people are not religious, but it’s actually only 18%. They think about how many people go to church instead of how many say they have a religion.

People also use quick guesses based on what they know, which can be wrong. For example, they overestimate rural populations because they think of how big rural areas look, not how many people live there.

People see things from their own point of view and don’t understand how different others might be. In India, people overestimated internet access because the survey was done online and mostly reached richer, connected people.

People worry about certain things and overestimate them because of those worries. In Britain, people overestimate how much the richest own, how many young people live with their parents, and how many immigrants there are.

However, people often underestimate other important facts. Most countries think fewer people are overweight or obese than they really are. In Saudi Arabia, people think only 28% are overweight or obese, but it’s actually 71%. In Britain, people think 44% are overweight or obese, but it’s actually 62%.

The real facts are often surprising and different between countries. In Russia, the richest 1% own 70% of the wealth, while in New Zealand, they own only 18%. In Italy, half of young adults aged 25-34 live with their parents, but in Norway, it’s only 4%. The average age in India is 27, but in Japan, it’s 47. In Brazil, Hungary, and Japan, only 10% of politicians are women, but in Sweden, it’s 44%.

When the real facts are so different, it’s no surprise that people get them wrong.

In Brazil, Hungary, and Japan, only 10% of politicians are women, but in Sweden, 44% are.

When the truth is so different, it's not surprising that people get it wrong.

We know about wildlife emergencies like the tiger in India, the orangutan in Indonesia, and the panda. These animals are loved and nobody wants to see them go extinct. However, scientists are now worried that the loss of wildlife close to where we live, like ladybugs, could be a bigger problem for biodiversity.

Scientists think we are in the Anthropocene age, a time when humans are changing ecosystems and causing many species to go extinct. A report by the World Wildlife Fund (WWF) shows that the number of animals with backbones has dropped by 52% over forty years. Freshwater animals have decreased by 76%. Bees and other pollinators help grow three-quarters of the world's food. Worms turn waste into nutrients, and bats eat mosquitoes, helping control malaria.

Dr. Nick Isaac, a scientist, says that it’s not just the number of species disappearing, but also how many are left in each group. This is very important. About 23 to 36% of birds, mammals, and amphibians used for food or medicine are now in danger of extinction. In many places, wild animals are a key part of people's diets, especially for poorer communities.

The main reason for this is that humans are using too many resources, which damages ecosystems, causes climate change, and destroys habitats faster than before. It’s not just large animals we need to worry about, but also small creatures like insects and worms. Even though these animals might not face extinction soon, fewer of them will affect everyone.

In the UK, the situation is similar for both animals with and without backbones. It’s not as simple as fish dying and people starving; it’s more complicated. Sir David Attenborough said in 2013 that humans are harming the Earth. The WWF believes there is still time to stop the decline. David Nussbaum, the UK Chief Executive of WWF, said that the report should make everyone realize the importance of protecting nature and ensuring a healthy future for people and animals.

Humans are cutting down trees faster than they can grow back, catching more fish than the oceans can replace, taking water from rivers and underground sources faster than rain can refill them, and putting more carbon into the air than oceans and forests can absorb.

Everyone knows about animals like tigers, orangutans, and pandas that might go away forever. People love these animals and don't want them to disappear. But now, scientists are worried that small animals like ladybugs are in bigger danger. This could hurt all the different kinds of life on Earth.

Scientists think we are in a new time called the Anthropocene age, which means many animals are disappearing. A report from the World Wildlife Fund shows that the number of animals with backbones has gone down by 52% in the last 40 years. Freshwater animals have gone down by 76%. Bees and other insects help grow much of our food. Losing them would be very bad.

Dr. Nick Isaac, who studies the environment, says that losing common animals will hurt people more than losing rare ones. In Britain, insects and other small animals are disappearing just as fast as bigger animals. This will cause big problems for humans.

Between 23% and 36% of birds, mammals, and frogs that we eat or use for medicine might go away forever. Many people, especially poor people, eat wild animals.

People are causing this problem. We are hurting the places where animals live, making the weather change, and destroying homes for animals. We need the little animals like insects and worms. Even if they don’t go away completely, having fewer of them will hurt everyone.

TV animal expert Sir David Attenborough said humans are a "plague on Earth." But the WWF says we can still stop animals from disappearing. David Nussbaum, the head of WWF in the UK, said we must change how we act. We need to protect nature and animals for a healthy future.

Nussbaum said humans are cutting down too many trees, catching too many fish, using too much river water, and making too much pollution.

Women have often had small roles in professional football, but this might be changing. France has just chosen its first female professional team manager. It doesn't matter that it's a second-division club. Some people think it's just for publicity, but what matters is that Helena Costa got the top job. This makes her the first female manager in the top two divisions of any professional European league. Vronique Soulier, president of the club’s supporters' group, said she was happy about this. At first, she was surprised, but then everyone agreed it was good news.

Helena Costa, the new manager of Clermont Foot 63, was born in Portugal and has a master's degree in sports science. She is also a UEFA-licensed coach. Before this, she coached male youth teams at Benfica, the Qatar women's team, and the Iranian women's national team until September 2013.

Costa, aged 36, was hired for two years by the club president, Claude Michy. Michy likes to get attention for his club. In 2013, he said they signed Messi, but not the famous Lionel Messi. The French women's minister, Najat Vallaud-Belkacem, praised the decision, saying it shows the future of professional football includes women.

Carolina Morace, an Italian who coached a men's team before, hopes this becomes normal. Raymond Domenech, a former French national team manager, thinks women can manage men's teams well. He said he would hire a woman as his assistant if he managed a club again.

On the club's website, they said Costa's appointment could bring a new era. Some fans are skeptical, thinking it's just for publicity. Others wonder if she can earn the players' respect. However, Soulier hopes the new manager can motivate the team.

Costa, known for her strong leadership, was called "Mourinho in a skirt" after her time at Chelsea. She accepts the comparison when it comes to wanting to win.

Loneliness is now a big issue. The Office for National Statistics says Britain is the loneliest country in Europe. British people have fewer strong friendships and know fewer neighbors compared to other European countries. A study by the University of Chicago shows that loneliness is twice as harmful to older people's health as being overweight and nearly as dangerous as living in poverty.

However, this study does not look at younger adults. In 2010, the Mental Health Foundation found that young people aged 18 to 34 feel lonelier than older people. These young people worry more about being alone and feel more depressed because of loneliness than those over 55.

There are many programs to help older people who feel lonely, but young people over 21 often don't get the same help. Loneliness can cause stress, depression, paranoia, anxiety, addiction, and even suicide.

Social media can help connect people far away, but it can also cause problems when it replaces face-to-face interactions. People often show only the best parts of their lives online, which can make others feel worse about their own lives.

Apps like Headspace are popular for mental health issues, but they might not help with loneliness. It’s better to find out why you feel lonely and try to fix that.

A study from the University of Michigan in 2013 showed that using technology to meet new people can be good. Websites like Mumsnet can help parents feel less alone.

Helplines can also help. Samaritans and Get Connected offer support for loneliness and related mental health issues. Websites like Mind provide support services to remind people they are not alone.

At work, talking to your boss about how you feel can help. John Binns, who works on mental health in businesses, says that being open with your employer and coworkers can make returning to work easier after a break due to stress or depression.

Nicky Forsythe, a psychotherapist, says having a regular time and place to talk about your life with someone who listens can be very helpful.

Recent research shows that loneliness can be deadly for older people. With an aging population, it’s important to reduce loneliness before it becomes a bigger problem. Building good relationships early in life can help prevent loneliness as you get older.

People are talking a lot about feeling alone. In Britain, people have fewer close friends and know their neighbors less than in other parts of Europe. Studies show that feeling alone is very bad for older people's health. It can hurt them even more than being overweight. Feeling alone can also cause as many deaths as being poor.

This is surprising. But these studies do not talk about young people feeling alone. In 2010, a survey found that young people aged 18 to 34 feel lonely more often than older people. They worry more about being alone and feel more sad because of it.

Sam Challis from a mental health group says that while there are places to help older people who feel alone, young people over 21 are too old for youth services. This is not good because feeling alone can cause mental health problems like stress, sadness, fear, worry, and even wanting to hurt yourself.

What can young people do to stop feeling alone? Using the internet and social media can help or hurt. They are good when they let you talk to friends far away, but not so good when they take the place of meeting people in person. Sometimes, seeing perfect lives online can make you want to stay home alone.

A study in 2013 found that using technology to meet new people can be good. If you cannot go out, the internet can help. For example, Mumsnet is a website for parents that can help you feel less alone when you are at home with kids.

Helplines can also help. One in four men who call Samaritans say they are lonely. Get Connected is a free helpline for young people to help with feelings of loneliness.

At work, telling your boss how you feel can help. Talking to coworkers can protect you from feeling too stressed.

Recent research shows that feeling alone can kill older people. With more older people, we need to try to stop feeling alone before it is too late. Ruth Sutherland from a counseling service says that getting older does not have to mean feeling more alone. It is important to make good relationships early in life.

A new computer-assisted autopsy system called Virtopsy is becoming popular in European hospitals. It was invented by scientists at the University of Zurich. Instead of using a knife to cut the body, doctors can now look at the body in 3-D on a computer screen.

Michael Thali, who directs the Institute for Forensic Medicine in Zurich and helped create Virtopsy, says this new method could change criminal investigations. He believes it will be harder for murderers to avoid detection because Virtopsy can find all pieces of evidence.

Virtopsies use MRI, CT scans, and surface scans to create detailed images of the body. This helps find injuries, air pockets, heart attacks, and cancer that might be missed in a traditional autopsy.

Richard Dirndorfer, who helped develop Virtopsy, thinks it could replace traditional autopsies over time, similar to how DNA analysis replaced blood group analysis.

Doctors can now see deep inside bodies using computer imaging. This has already found injuries that were missed before. For now, the goal is to use Virtopsy along with traditional autopsies.

Forensic scientists can plan autopsies better with Virtopsy. Many criminologists from around the world have visited Switzerland to learn about this new method.

The project started decades ago but got a boost from a donation by a wealthy eye doctor. New forensic scientists and pathologists see Virtopsy as a way to improve traditional methods, not replace them completely.

Lars Oesterhelweg, Deputy Director of the Institute of Forensic Medicine at Charit Hospital in Berlin, says that while Virtopsy is very useful, traditional cuts are still needed to check the color of blood, consistency of body fluids, and smells.

Oesterhelweg also notes that Virtopsy is especially helpful when the cause of death is unclear. It allows experts to review cases again and get different opinions.

Relatives of the deceased often prefer Virtopsy because it does not disfigure the body.

A new computer autopsy system is getting popular in European hospitals. The inventor says this system means there won't be any "perfect murder" anymore.

This method, called 'Virtopsy,' is used in some forensic medical places in Europe. Scientists at the University of Zurich made it. Instead of cutting the chest like in old autopsies, doctors can now look at the body in 3-D on computer screens.

Richard Dirndorfer, who first used DNA in crime work, thinks Virtopsies might replace old autopsies someday, just like DNA replaced older tests.

Doctors can see deep inside bodies with Virtopsies and find things they can't with old autopsies.

Many criminologists come to Switzerland to see this new way. Forensic scientists and doctors think it can be used with old autopsies.

Thali also says Virtopsy helps look at old cases where the cause of death was not clear. This means they can try again to find murderers.

Scientists say families like Virtopsy better because it doesn't cut or damage the body like old autopsies do.

In Iceland, girls can be named Aagot, Arney, or Sfrur, and boys can be named Baldey, Bebba, or Br. Other names like Dgg, Dimmbl, Etna, Eybjrt, Frigg, Glds, Hrn, Ingunn, Jrlaug, Obba, Sigurflj, rana, and Vagna are okay too. However, a girl cannot be named Harriet.

Tristan Cardew and his Icelandic wife, Kristin, are fighting a decision by the National Registry in Reykjavik. They won't renew their daughter Harriet's passport because they don't accept her name. The registry also doesn't recognize the name of their 12-year-old son, Duncan. Until now, the children traveled with passports using the names Stlka and Drengur Cardew, meaning Girl and Boy Cardew. This time, the authorities are enforcing the law strictly, which says no official documents can be issued to people with unapproved Icelandic names.

Because of this, the family from Kpavogur almost missed their holiday in France. They got an emergency UK passport from the British embassy to travel.

Names are very important in Iceland, where the phone book lists people by their first names. Most Icelandic last names show who your father or mother is. For example, Jn Einarssons children might be lafur Jnsson and Sigrur Jnsdttir.

Children born in Iceland must have names on a list of 1,853 female and 1,712 male names within six months of birth. If not, parents need approval from the Icelandic Naming Committee. Each year, the committee gets about 100 applications for new names and rejects about half. Names must follow Icelandic grammar rules, use only letters in the 32-letter Icelandic alphabet, and fit Icelandic language structure.

Harriet's name was rejected because it doesn't follow these rules. Some people think Iceland's naming laws are unfair and limit creativity. The Cardews could solve the issue by giving Harriet an Icelandic middle name, but Tristan thinks it's too late and the rule is silly. He wonders if the government doesn't want them in Iceland.

In Iceland, girls can have names like Aagot, Arney, or Ásfríður. Boys can be named Baldey, Bebba, or Brá. Other names like Dögg, Dimmblá, Etna, Eybjört, Frigg, Glódís, Hörn, Ingunn, Jórlaug, Obba, Sigurfljóð, Úranía, and Vagna are okay too. But a girl cannot be named Harriet.

Tristan Cardew, a British man who lives in Iceland, and his Icelandic wife, Kristin, want to use their daughter's name, Harriet, on her passport. The National Registry in Reykjavik said no. They also did not approve the name of their son, Duncan. So, the kids had to use the names Stúlka and Drengur on their passports, which mean Girl and Boy.

Now, the family needs new passports to go on vacation. They asked the British embassy for help and got emergency UK passports.

Iceland has rules about names. If a child is born there, the parents must tell the National Registry the name within six months. The name must be on a list of 1,853 names for girls and 1,712 for boys. If not, the parents need the Icelandic Naming Committee to say yes. Each year, about 5,000 babies are born, and the committee gets about 100 requests. They say no to about half of them to keep the Icelandic language safe.

Names must follow Icelandic grammar rules and spelling. Letters like "c" are not allowed because they are not part of Iceland's 32-letter alphabet. This is why Harriet was not accepted.

Some people think the naming laws are unfair. In 2013, a person named Blær won the right to use her name. The old mayor of Reykjavik said the law is not fair and stops creativity.

The Cardews could give Harriet an Icelandic middle name, but they think that would be silly.

Google has mapped many places like mountains, oceans, and forests, but it hasn't mapped the cold Arctic much before. Now, Google is working to map the Arctic to help people understand life there better. A small team went to Iqaluit, a big town in Nunavut, Canada. They brought warm clothes, laptops, and a heavy camera to put on their backpacks.

With help from a local expert, the team collected pictures and information for four days. This will let people see the town on Google's Street View in July 2013. Unlike other places, where cars are used to collect pictures, the team had to walk on snowy roads and unknown paths. Some paths are made of ice and melt in summer.

The team also walked on a long road called the "Road to Nowhere," even though they were warned about polar bears and other wild animals. John Graham, the mayor of Iqaluit, said the locals were excited to follow the team. He mentioned that explorers like Martin Frobisher and Captain Elliott Roosevelt helped start the town.

Google's map was good but missed a new road. Also, many businesses and homes get mail at the post office, so putting these addresses on the map would cause confusion. About 30 people, including elders, business owners, and students, helped fix this problem by showing where things should be on the map.

Arif Sayani, the town's Planning Director, said the maps could help promote the town to visitors and new residents. It might also help with planning decisions. The Google leader hopes to map other northern towns, but it will be expensive. They might ask volunteers to help in the future.

Google made maps of many places like mountains, oceans, and forests. They did not make maps of the Arctic before, but now they want to.

A small Google team went to Iqaluit, a big town in Nunavut, Canada. They brought warm clothes, computers, and a big camera. The team took pictures and collected information for four days. An expert who knows the land helped them, and some people in the town watched them work.

In July 2013, the town of 7,000 people will be on Google's Street View. Usually, Google uses cars to make maps, but in Iqaluit, they had to walk because some roads are made of ice and melt in summer. They even walked on a long road called the Road to Nowhere, even though there were warnings about polar bears.

Google already had a map of the town from satellites, but it was missing a new road. Many houses and businesses do not have street addresses, so Google asked 30 people, including elders, business owners, and students, to help put the right addresses on the map.

Arif Sayani, who plans things for the town, thinks the map will help people who want to visit or move there. It might also help with planning in the town.

The Google leader wants to make maps of other northern towns too. But it costs a lot to move people and things around the Arctic. So, Google might send cameras to the area and ask volunteers to finish the maps.

Governments in Europe hope to find a quick fix for rising unemployment. However, in the areas hit hardest by job losses in the EU, unemployment keeps going up, and talking about solutions doesn't help much.

In a part of Italy, one mayor thinks he has found a way to help his town's big problem with jobs. Valter Piscedda, the mayor of Elmas, a small town close to Sardinia’s capital, Cagliari, plans to pay some residents to move away. The town council will pay for ten unemployed people to take English classes, buy cheap flights, and look for jobs in other parts of Europe.

Mayor Piscedda came up with this idea because over the past year and a half, especially recently, he has seen young people who are very upset about not finding work. Some ask for help to find jobs locally, while others are so discouraged that they want to leave and find work experience abroad.

So, his plan is to help those who want to gain experience outside Italy. As Italy's economy struggles, Sardinia and much of southern and central Italy face high unemployment. In the second quarter of 2014, unemployment was 17.7%, and more than 54% of people under 25 were out of work.

For the "Adesso Parto" (Now I'm Leaving) program, Elmas' council will give €12,000 to the first ten applicants aged 18 to 50 who are unemployed, have lived in the town for three years, earn no more than €15,000 annually, and do not need to be university-educated.

Encouraging people to leave is a sensitive topic since many Italians, including young graduates, are already leaving the country. Mayor Piscedda believes that those who leave might return and contribute much more later. He hopes the program will help those most in need.

Some in Elmas think the program is good because there are few jobs locally. Others wonder why the money isn’t used to create jobs in the town instead. Online, some criticized the plan, calling it an admission of failure.

However, Piscedda defends his plan, saying he deals with people's problems daily and needs to do something to help. He argues that the jobs he can create as mayor are temporary and don't offer long-term benefits.

Governments in Europe want to solve the problem of more people being out of work. In the poorer areas of the EU, unemployment keeps getting worse.

Apart from volcanoes, hurricanes, and earthquakes, water and sand can also destroy cities.

A century ago, Venice flooded about ten times a year. Now, Piazza San Marco, which is only three feet above sea level, floods about 100 times a year.

Rising sea levels are not the only reason. In many places, the land is sinking. Between 1950 and 1970, industrial activities made Venice sink by 20 cm. Ho Chi Minh City in Vietnam is sinking by about 2 cm a year, but Jakarta is sinking faster, by 10 to 20 cm each year. In the last thirty years, Jakarta has sunk about four meters.

Jakarta has pumped out a lot of groundwater, causing the land to dry and sink, creating a bowl shape. Rivers that used to flow through the city to the sea now cannot drain properly.

Venice has plans to protect itself, and Ho Chi Minh City and Jakarta are taking action. However, in Miami, politicians deny there is a serious environmental issue. Miami is less than ten feet above sea level, often flooded by tropical storms, and built on porous rock that absorbs seawater. This water fills the city's foundations and comes up through drains and pipes, polluting fresh water. Miami might become uninhabitable.

In the Maldives, people are thinking about leaving their homes. Male, with a population of 153,379 and only four feet above sea level, built a ten-foot sea wall costing $63 million. But only stabilizing rising sea levels can save it and other islands.

In Africa, the Sahara Desert is spreading south at 30 miles per year, threatening northern Mauritania. Around Chinguetti, the desert has grown by more than 260 acres over twenty years. The population has dropped from 20,000 to a few thousand, and trading has almost stopped due to sand in the streets.

In California, Rancho Mirage near Palm Springs may need to be abandoned soon. With 38 million people and 32 million vehicles, the state uses too much water. Rancho Mirage uses more than 200 gallons per person daily, causing a man-made drought. A 25% cut in water use has been implemented, but it may not save the city.

Forest fires are a growing threat in America. From 1953 to 2014, there were 800 major fire disasters. A USDA Forest Service report shows more urban areas are becoming vulnerable to wildfires.

In Australia, some Victorian resorts and Melbourne suburbs are among the 52 most vulnerable to bushfires due to long-term droughts making trees highly flammable. While a single forest fire won't destroy a city, repeated fires could make it uninhabitable.

Many cities struggle against nature. Male's future looks especially bad because even if its sea wall works, the islands around it will disappear, taking away Male's reason to exist.

Volcanoes, hurricanes, and earthquakes can destroy a city. Water and sand can do it too.

Venice, a beautiful city, used to flood ten times a year. Now, it floods about 100 times a year. The lowest part of Venice, Piazza San Marco, is only three feet above sea level.

Venice sank 20 centimeters between 1950 and 1970. Ho Chi Minh City in Vietnam sinks 2 centimeters each year. Jakarta sinks even faster, 10 to 20 centimeters every year. In the last thirty years, Jakarta has sunk four meters.

Jakarta pumps out too much water, making the land sink like a bowl. Plans are being made to save Venice, Ho Chi Minh City, and Jakarta. But in Miami, leaders do not think the city has a big problem.

Miami is less than ten feet above sea level. More storms are flooding the city. Miami is built on rock that lets water pass through easily. This water fills the city's foundations and comes up through pipes, forcing sewage up and polluting fresh water. One day, it may be impossible to live in Miami.

In the Maldives, people may have to leave their homes. The capital, Malé, has 153,379 people and is only four feet above sea level. Malé built a ten-foot sea wall for $63 million. But if sea levels keep rising, Malé and the islands will not be safe.

In Africa, the Sahara Desert is growing and moving south at 30 miles per year. This affects people living in northern Mauritania.

In California, the city of Rancho Mirage may have to be abandoned in the next ten years. The problem is not global warming but too many people. In 1870, California had half a million people. Now, it has 38 million people and 32 million cars.

Each person in Rancho Mirage uses over 200 gallons of water daily. They have cut water use by 25%, but this may not help much. People may need to leave some desert cities in California.

Forest fires are a big problem in American towns and cities. Between 1953 and 2014, there were 800 major fire disasters. Many towns and cities are at risk from wildfires.

Many cities are having trouble with nature. Malé looks like it could be in big trouble. Even though the new sea wall might work, the islands around Malé will likely disappear soon. If the islands go, Malé will lose its reason to exist.

Some people call it the "hotel of mum and dad." One in five young adults live in their family home until they are at least 26, and the same number do not pay anything for living there. A recent survey found that the number of adults living at home varies across the country, from almost 9% in the East Midlands to more than double that in London, where house prices and rents are very high. The survey also found that 20% of young adults living at home do not pay anything.

Many young adults are struggling with low wages and high rents. Those who want to buy a home find it hard to save for a deposit because of high rental costs. Research shows that half of renters cannot save any money for a deposit, and a quarter can only save £100 or less each month. Even though mortgages are cheaper due to low interest rates, the best deals require large deposits.

Because of these challenges, young adults are moving back home to save money. Parents who cannot give their children a lot of money are often happy to help. The survey found that 28% of adults living at home are trying to save for a deposit, but 30% are not saving any money.

Michael Day, 30, lives with his parents in Bristol. He finds it hard to choose between paying high rents and saving for a mortgage deposit. Renting a one-bedroom home in the city costs between £500 and £800 a month, while buying a similar property costs about £130,000. He pays a small amount to cover bills and spends his extra money on golf and holidays. He says he needs to save for the foreseeable future.

Sue Green from Saga, a company that sells insurance to people over 50, says most parents did not plan to have their children living with them in their 20s or 30s. Most parents are happy to let their children live rent-free because it helps them save for a home. Children who do not pay rent often help by buying groceries, doing odd jobs, or cooking meals.

Angus Hanton from the Intergenerational Foundation says older generations caused the housing crisis, and young people should not be blamed for staying at home. Young people have seen a 20% drop in average income since 2008. Rents and car insurance are very high, and mortgage rules are stricter for young people but not for older buy-to-let investors. Many jobs are part-time or temporary, making it harder for young workers to build stable lives.

Jenna Gavin, 29, lives in her family home in Southport, Merseyside. She works as a medical receptionist nearby and wants to stay in the area. Renting a one-bedroom flat would cost more than £420 a month plus bills, using most of her earnings. She tries to save for a deposit but finds it difficult. Her parents do not charge her rent and want her to save money. Jenna contributes by buying food and helping around the house. She hopes to move out in a couple of years.

One in five young adults in the UK stay at home until they are 26, and one in five do not pay any rent. In the East Midlands, less than 9% of young adults live at home, but in London, more than double that number do. This is because houses and rentals are very expensive there.

Many young people give their parents some money to live at home, but 20% do not pay anything. Young people face low wages and high rents, making it hard to save for a house. Half of renters cannot save for a house deposit, and a quarter can only save £100 or less each month. Even though mortgages are cheap, people need large deposits to get good deals.

Because of this, more young adults are moving back home to save money. Parents are okay with this if they cannot help with a deposit. The survey shows that 28% of adults live at home to save for a deposit, but 30% are not saving any money.

Renting a one-bedroom home costs between £500 and £800 a month, while buying a similar flat costs about £130,000. He does not want to rent because it costs more than a mortgage, but he needs a big deposit to get a mortgage.

Angus Hanton from the Intergenerational Foundation says older people caused the housing crisis, so we should not blame younger people for staying at home. David Bowie, who died of cancer, surprised people until the end. His last album, Blackstar, came out on his 69th birthday, January 8, 2016. It showed he could still make exciting and challenging music.

In the 1970s, Bowie led musical and fashion trends. He was a singer-songwriter, a glam-rock pioneer, and made innovative electronic music. His ability to change sounds and images is unique in pop history.

Born David Robert Jones in south London, his family moved to Kent in 1953. There, he showed talent for singing and playing the recorder. Later, he studied art, music, and design.

At 15, David formed his first band, the Kon-rads. At 16, he changed his name to Bowie to avoid confusion with Davy Jones of the Monkees. His first album, David Bowie, came out in June 1967. In July 1969, he released "Space Oddity," a top-five UK hit timed with the Apollo 11 moon landing.

In March 1970, Bowie married art student Angela Barnett. His album The Man Who Sold the World, released in late 1970 in the US and 1971 in the UK, showed his writing and performing skills. Themes included immortality, insanity, murder, and mysticism.

Hunky Dory in 1972 was a good album but not very popular. That changed with The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars, featuring the hit "Starman."

Aladdin Sane in 1973 was Bowie's first UK number-one album. His interest in funk and soul music was heard in Young Americans (1975), which included the hit "Fame" with John Lennon.

Station to Station (1976) introduced the Thin White Duke persona. Bowie divorced Angela in 1980. Scary Monsters (and Super Creeps) in 1980 was a great album with the hit "Ashes to Ashes." He also played in Broadway's The Elephant Man.

In 1981, Bowie and Queen's "Under Pressure" was a number-one single. He appeared in movies like Christiane F (1981) and Cat People (1982).

In 1983, Bowie's album Let's Dance and its singles "Let's Dance," "China Girl," and "Modern Love" were big hits. His Serious Moonlight tour was very successful.

At the 1985 Live Aid concert, Bowie performed well. He and Mick Jagger recorded the hit "Dancing in the Street" for charity.

In 1992, Bowie married Somalian model Iman. Their daughter, Alexandria, was born in August 2000. His album Black Tie White Noise (1993) topped the UK charts.

In 1999, Bowie worked on the album Hours, based on music for a computer game. He performed at the Concert for New York City in 2001, helping raise money after the 9/11 attacks.

During his Reality tour in 2004, Bowie had chest pains and needed emergency surgery. He slowed down after this. In 2006, he received a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1996.

The Next Day (2013) was his first album in ten years. It included the hit "Where Are We Now?" and topped charts worldwide. In 2014, Bowie won the Brit Award for Best British Male, being the oldest person to receive the award.

Bowie is survived by Iman, their daughter Alexandria, his stepdaughter Zulekha, and his son Duncan from his first marriage.

David Bowie, who died of cancer, surprised us until the end. His last album, Blackstar, came out on his 69th birthday, January 8, 2016. It showed he kept making difficult and strange music.

In the 1970s, Bowie led musical and fashion trends. He made glam-rock and "plastic soul" music. Later, he moved to Berlin to make new electronic music. Born David Robert Jones in south London, he formed his first band, the Kon-rads, at 15. Soon, he went solo.

He changed his name to Bowie so people wouldn't mix him up with Davy Jones of the Monkees. His first album, David Bowie, came out in June 1967. In July 1969, he released Space Oddity, which became a big hit in the UK. The Man Who Sold the World came out in the US in late 1970 and in the UK the next year. It showed his talents with daring songs and a hard-rock sound. In 1972, he released Hunky Dory, a mix of complex songs. It wasn't very popular, but that changed with The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars. Bowie appeared as Ziggy Stardust, a sci-fi character, and the hit song Starman made the album a success.

Everything Bowie did became a hit. His first UK number 1 album was Aladdin Sane in 1973, with hit songs like The Jean Genie and Drive-in Saturday. His interest in funk and soul music was in Young Americans in 1975, which had the song Fame with John Lennon. For Station to Station in 1976, he became the Thin White Duke.

Bowie and his wife divorced in 1980. That year, he had another success with Scary Monsters (and Super Creeps) and its hit song Ashes to Ashes. He also acted in The Elephant Man on Broadway. In 1981, he had a number 1 single with Queen, Under Pressure. In 1983, he focused on the album Let's Dance and his shows. Let's Dance made Bowie a worldwide rock star. The album and its singles, Let's Dance, China Girl, and Modern Love, were big hits. The early 1980s was when MTV was popular. Bowie's skill in making eye-catching videos helped his popularity. The Serious Moonlight tour lasted six months and drew many fans. It was the most successful part of his career.

At the 1985 Live Aid concert, Bowie was one of the best performers. That year, he worked with Mick Jagger on the charity song Dancing in the Street, which went to number 1. A few days after performing at the Freddie Mercury tribute concert in April 1992, Bowie married the Somalian model Iman and bought a house in New York.

For Black Tie White Noise in 1993, he added soul and hip-hop. It topped the UK album chart and gave him a top 10 single, Jump They Say. In October 2001, Bowie performed at the Concert for New York City, joining Paul McCartney, Jon Bon Jovi, Billy Joel, the Who, and Elton John in a benefit show six weeks after the 9/11 attacks.

During his Reality tour in 2004, Bowie had chest pains while performing in Germany and needed emergency surgery in Hamburg. He saw this as a warning and slowed down. In February 2006, he got a Grammy lifetime achievement award. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1996.

The Next Day in 2013 was his first album of new songs in ten years. It included the single Where Are We Now? The album topped charts in Britain and worldwide. In 2014, Bowie won the Brit Award for Best British Male, becoming the oldest person to receive the award.

He is survived by his wife, Iman, their daughter, Alexandria, his stepdaughter, Zulekha, and his son, Duncan, from his first marriage.

At Addis Ababa airport, you see pictures of golden grains, tiny red seeds, and men around a big pancake. The sign says: "Teff: the ultimate gluten-free crop!"

Ethiopia is one of the world's poorest countries, often facing food problems. However, it is home to teff, a very healthy ancient grain now sold in health food stores and supermarkets in Europe and America.

Teff's tiny seeds, about the size of poppy seeds, are full of calcium, iron, protein, and amino acids. Since it is naturally gluten-free, teff can replace wheat flour in foods like bread, pasta, waffles, and pizza bases. Just like quinoa, teff's great nutritional value opens new and profitable markets in the West.

In Ethiopia, teff is very popular. About 6.3 million farmers grow it, covering over 20% of farmland. They grind it into flour to make injera, a flatbread essential in Ethiopian cooking. Teff is also key in many religious and cultural events. People in Ethiopia and Eritrea share large pieces of injera, using it as a utensil to scoop stews and feed each other, showing loyalty and friendship in a tradition called gursha.

As interest in traditional crops grows and the health and gluten-free markets expand, teff is gaining new importance, sometimes called Ethiopia’s second gift to the world after coffee.

Sophie Kebede, a London-based businesswoman who owns a UK company that specializes in teff, was surprised by its nutritional benefits. She said, "I didn't know it was so popular. I'm of Ethiopian origin; I've been eating injera all my life."

Increased demand for ancient grains hasn’t always helped poor communities. In Bolivia and Peru, while quinoa sales have raised incomes, they’ve also led to malnutrition and land disputes as farmers sell their entire crop to meet Western demand.

Ethiopia’s growing middle class is also driving up teff demand, making it too expensive for the poorest. Most small farmers now sell most of their teff to city dwellers.

While this has boosted some rural incomes, it has had nutritional impacts, according to the government, since teff is the most nutritious grain in the country. Urban residents consume up to 61 kg of teff per year, compared to 20 kg in rural areas. Richer people eat more expensive magna and white teff, while poorer people eat less valuable red and mixed teff, often mixing it with cheaper cereals like sorghum and maize.

The Ethiopian government aims to double teff production by 2015. They believe teff can improve school meals and emergency aid programs, helping to reduce malnutrition, especially among children and teenagers.

Despite Ethiopia's growing economy, it remains on the UN's list of least developed countries, with about 20% of under-fives suffering from malnutrition.

The government's Agricultural Transformation Agency plans to increase teff production by developing better varieties and introducing new farming methods and tools.

Currently, the government only allows the export of injera and other processed teff products, not raw teff. However, this might change if they produce enough teff for both domestic use and export.

Mama Fresh, a family business, has been selling injera to top restaurants and hotels in Addis Ababa for years. They also export injera to Finland, Germany, Sweden, and the US, mainly for Ethiopians living there. Mama Fresh plans to double its exports to America in 2014 and will soon produce teff-based pizzas, bread, and cookies.

Regassa Feyissa, an Ethiopian agricultural scientist and former head of the National Institute for Biodiversity, warns that without careful planning, increased teff production for export could lead farmers to neglect other important crops.

Since little Ethiopian teff is available internationally, farmers in the US, Europe, Israel, and Australia have started growing it.

George W. Bush, Benedict Cumberbatch, and Stephen Hawking did the Ice Bucket Challenge. David Cameron, Barack Obama, and Pamela Anderson did not do it. The challenge started in the U.S. in July and raised $100 million for the ALS Association, which helps people with motor neuron disease. It also raised 4.5 million pounds for a British charity and thousands more for charities in Hong Kong and Australia.

Some people do not like the Ice Bucket Challenge. They say it wastes water and some people do not give money to charity after doing it. The challenge works like this: someone talks about the charity on video, then pours ice water over their head or asks a friend to do it. Then, they ask three other people to do the same or give money.

During World Water Week in Stockholm, WaterAid asked people to use recycled water or sea water instead of fresh water. Douglas Graham, who works for the UK Motor Neurone Disease Association, said they are very happy with the donations. The charity helps people with a serious disease that has no cure and kills five people a day in the UK.

Pamela Anderson, an animal rights activist, did not support the challenge because of the charity's use of animals in experiments. Some people in California did not do the challenge because of the drought there. Matt Damon used water from his toilet, and Verne Troyer used milk for environmental reasons. The challenge caused a water shortage on the Scottish island of Colonsay.

Lincoln Humphries, a TV anchor, said he would rather donate to charities that help people in need. He thought the challenge was not real charity. Some people worry that small charities cannot handle the extra money, but the MND Association can. They use the money for research and to help 3,500 people with the disease. More than half of those diagnosed die within two years.

The challenge has made the disease more known. The MND Association’s website got 330,000 visits in one day, which is more than they usually get in a whole year. Graham says the awareness is very valuable. In 2013, British people gave 62 billion pounds to charity. The MND Association will use the money to help people with the disease.

The challenge works like this: You talk about the charity on video, then pour ice water on your head or ask a friend to do it. Then, you name three other people to do the same or give money to the charity.

Douglas Graham from the UK Motor Neurone Association said they got a lot of money unexpectedly and are thankful. The money helps a small charity that cares for people with a serious disease that kills five people a day in the UK.

Pamela Anderson wrote a letter saying she does not like the charity's use of animals in experiments. Some US stars did not do the challenge because of California's drought. Matt Damon used toilet water, and Verne Troyer used milk for environmental reasons. Some say the challenge caused a water shortage on the Scottish island of Colonsay.

Critics say small charities may not know what to do with extra money, but the MND Association says they will use it for research, care, and support for 3,500 people. More than half of the people with the disease die within two years.

The challenge made many people aware of the disease. The MND Association usually gets about 300,000 website visits a year, but they got 330,000 visits in just one day recently.

Graham said it is good to donate to any charity. British people gave £62 billion to charity in 2013. The MND Association will decide how to spend the money wisely.

Dan Sullivan, a 27-year-old venture capitalist, was late for a meeting because he got stopped on his motorcycle. He often works too much and forgets to do nice things for his girlfriend, like giving her presents.

So, Dan created a service called BetterBoyfriend.me. For about $70 a month, it sends a gift to a girlfriend or wife. Dan has tested this service with around 350 boyfriends, mostly his friends from Harvard and other tech workers. Each month, the members pick one of seven gifts, like chocolate or a tea set, which are sent without any labels.

Dan uses Facebook ads to test his ideas. His service became popular because people liked it.

There's another service called InvisibleBoyfriend. It lets users create a fake boyfriend who can text with them all day. The creator, Kyle Tabor, made it to stop unwanted attention, but many users now use it for companionship.

Both Dan and Kyle have formed real relationships with their customers. Dan helps boyfriends with their relationships and has learned from his mistakes. At first, he sent packages with his name on them, and some girlfriends found out. Now, about half of the women know about Dan’s involvement, especially if they've been married for a long time.

Dan also learned that it's better to give the gifts directly to the boyfriends, not their girlfriends, when he tried handing out flowers in a park.

Dan learned it's important to focus on the boyfriends, not the girlfriends, when giving gifts. Scientists have made a special mirror that sends heat into cold space. This mirror could replace air conditioners in buildings to keep them cool.

Researchers think the mirror could greatly reduce the energy used to cool businesses and shopping centers. In the U.S., about 15% of the energy used by buildings goes to air conditioning. The mirror might stop the need for extra cooling in some cases.

In a test in Stanford, California, a black roof got 60 degrees Celsius hotter than the air in the sun, and an aluminum roof got 40 degrees Celsius hotter. But the mirror was 5 degrees Celsius cooler than the air.

Shanhui Fan, a light expert at Stanford University, says covering part of a roof with the mirror can save a lot of power. It can cut the electricity used for air conditioning. In some cases, it can remove the need for air conditioning entirely.

Buildings get hot from many things like hot water, cooking, and sunlight. The mirror reflects 97% of the sunlight and sends heat as infrared light into space.

The mirror is made of thin layers, starting with a reflective silver layer. Other layers include silicon dioxide and hafnium oxide. When heated, silicon dioxide turns the heat into infrared light that goes directly into space.

The mirror is about two micrometers thick. Tests show it can cool at a rate of 40 watts per square meter. The cost is between $20 and $70 per square meter. Fan estimates it could save 100MWh of electricity each year on a three-story building.

Fan says the mirror won't solve global warming but can help reduce greenhouse gases by lowering electricity use. Marin Solja__i__, a physicist at MIT, is excited about the mirror's potential to lower air conditioning costs or eliminate the need for it.

The mirror can save a lot of energy used for cooling buildings like offices and shopping centers. In the U.S., about 15% of the energy used by buildings is for air conditioning. The mirror might mean we do not need air conditioners anymore.

The mirror costs between $20 and $70 per square meter. On a three-story building, it could save 100MWh of electricity each year.

Marin Soljačić, a scientist at MIT, thinks the mirror is exciting. He says you could use the mirrors on buildings to save money on air conditioning or maybe not use it at all. You could put them on top of shopping malls too.

The plan is to make a low-cost light that uses gravity to create free power. This could stop the use of unsafe kerosene lamps in Africa and India. British designer Patrick Hunt tried to get money from banks and investors but faced difficulties. He said, "Getting funding is slow, complicated, and risky, so no one wants to take a chance."

Instead, Hunt used crowdfunding on the website Indiegogo. In just five days, he reached his goal of raising £36,200. After 40 days, he collected £400,000.

The light works using a dynamo powered by a 10kg bag of rocks. When the bag is lifted to a height of about 2 meters and slowly falls, it generates enough power for 30 minutes of light.

Hunt is now preparing to make the lights in China. Before full production, he plans to send 1,000 lights to Africa to test the market.

Crowdfunding helps new businesses get money quickly. On Indiegogo, people can give money and receive rewards. For example, those who funded Hunt's light received their own light and felt good about helping others.

Danae Ringelmann, co-founder of Indiegogo, believes crowdfunding is fair and tests ideas well. She says it shows if customers like an idea without needing connections to banks or investors.

Even if a project doesn't get funded, it saves time and gives valuable feedback. Ringelmann started Indiegogo to help artists raise money. Now, the site raises about $2 million weekly for new businesses.

Indiegogo charges a 4% fee for successful projects. If a project fails, contributors can get refunds or the creator can keep the funds but pay a 9% fee.

In the UK, a woman raised £100,000 to open a cat café called Lady Dinah’s Cat Emporium. Crowdfunding lets entrepreneurs prove there is a market for their product, even if venture capitalists doubt it.

Ringelmann advises that having a good idea isn’t enough; it’s about executing it well. Confidence and speed are key. InvestingZone is a new platform that connects wealthy individuals with startups looking for investment.

His light works by hanging a 10kg bag of rocks. As the bag falls, it creates power for half an hour of light. This light can help people in Africa and India who use dangerous kerosene lamps.

Patrick is part of a group of new business owners who use crowdfunding to get money. Crowdfunding means asking many people to give small amounts of money. Another site like this is InvestingZone.

On Indiegogo, people who give money can get perks, like getting one of Patrick's lights. Danae Ringelmann, who started Indiegogo, thinks Patrick's light shows how crowdfunding can help test ideas.

Danae says having a good idea isn't enough. You need to believe in yourself and act quickly to make it happen. Big investors aren't interested in crowdfunding now, but that might change with InvestingZone.

JMW Turner, a great British painter, will be on the new 20 pound note. People voted for him in a national poll.

Mark Carney, the head of the Bank of England, asked the public to pick a dead cultural person for the note. Turner, known for his sea paintings, won against 590 other artists suggested by 30,000 people.

A group of experts chose five finalists: Barbara Hepworth, Charlie Chaplin, Josiah Wedgwood, William Hogarth, and Turner. These were picked because of their big impact on art and British culture.

The announcement happened at the Turner Contemporary gallery in Margate, with Carney and artist Tracey Emin there. Emin said this shows Britain values creativity.

The note will show Turner's 1799 self-portrait and his famous painting "The Fighting Temeraire." It will also have a quote from Turner: "light is therefore colour," and his signature from his will.

Historic figures started appearing on banknotes in 1970. Now, Turner joins Winston Churchill and Jane Austen on new plastic notes. Churchill is on the 5 pound note, Austen on the 10 pound note, and Turner on the 20 pound note by 2020.

Turner was born in 1775 in London and joined the Royal Academy at 14. He loved painting the Kent coast and made over 550 oil paintings and 2,000 watercolors. A movie about his life came out in 2014.

Victoria Pomery, the director of Turner Contemporary, said choosing Turner shows he is the nation’s favorite artist.

Victoria Pomery, the Turner Contemporary director, said the vote shows Turner is Britain's favorite artist.

For nearly 100 years, police and intelligence agencies worldwide have used lie detectors to catch criminals and spies. However, a new method developed by researchers in Britain and the Netherlands may replace the polygraph. Tests show this new method is successful over 70% of the time. It could be used in police stations globally within ten years. Unlike the polygraph, which checks for facial tics, rapid speech, or arm movements, the new method tracks full-body motion to detect guilt.

The polygraph is commonly used in the US for criminal cases and security checks for the FBI and CIA but is less popular in Europe. Many scientists and lawyers doubt its reliability. The new method has shown better results in tests.

Researchers think that liars move more, so they use a full-body motion suit, like those used in movies, to record these movements. The suit has 17 sensors that track movement up to 120 times per second in three dimensions for 23 joints.

Ross Anderson, a professor at Cambridge University, says that interviewers can only correctly guess if someone is telling the truth about 55% of the time. The new method is correct over 70% of the time, and in some tests, it has been over 80%.

Anderson explains that guilty people fidget more, and this can be measured. He adds that this new method is significant because it provides a better alternative to torture, which is morally wrong and unreliable.

The research team includes Dr. Sophie van der Zee from Cambridge University, Professor Ronald Poppe from Utrecht University, Professor Paul Taylor from Lancaster University, and Anderson.

The polygraph was invented in 1921 by policeman John Larson. It measures changes in pulse, blood pressure, sweating, and breathing to detect lies. However, the US Supreme Court ruled in 1998 that there was no agreement on the polygraph's reliability, a finding backed by the US National Academy of Sciences in 2003.

The study involved 180 students and staff at Lancaster University. Half were told to tell the truth, and half to lie. They were paid £7.50 for a 70-minute experiment with two tests. One test involved a computer game called Never End, where some participants played the game while others lied about playing it. The second test involved a lost wallet with £5; some participants returned it, while others hid it and lied about it.

The study found that overall, they correctly guessed whether 82.2% of the participants were telling the truth or lying based on their limb movements. Liars moved their arms more, but this was only 60% accurate. Tracking total body motion was more successful, over 70% of the time.

Anderson says that total body motion is similar across different cultures and anxiety levels, unlike other lie detection methods. Full-body suits are costly, around £30,000, and can be uncomfortable, so the team is looking into cheaper options like motion-sensing technology from video games, such as Microsoft’s Kinect.

Anderson acknowledges that intelligence agencies might train agents to stay still to trick the method, but staying still itself could be a sign of lying.

For almost 100 years, police and spy groups worldwide have used a machine called a polygraph to help catch bad guys. Now, scientists in Britain and the Netherlands made a new way to spot lies. This new way works right over 70% of the time. Police may use it in about ten years. It watches the whole body to see if someone feels guilty.

The polygraph checks for fast heartbeats, sweaty skin, and quick breaths to guess if someone is lying. It's used a lot in the U.S., but not as much in Europe. Many folks don't think it works well.

The new method looks at how much people move when they're nervous or lying. It uses a special suit like the ones used to make cartoon characters in movies. This new way works better than the polygraph. In some tests, it worked right over 80% of the time.

A scientist named Ross Anderson says that people who feel guilty move more, and now they can measure this.

To test the new method, scientists asked 180 people to either tell the truth or lie. Some people talked about a computer game they played, while others lied about playing it. Other people had to return a lost wallet or hide it and lie about it.

The new method worked right 82.2% of the time. It watched how much people moved their arms and legs to guess if they were lying.

The special suits cost about £30,000 and can be uncomfortable. So, the scientists are trying to find cheaper ways, like using the motion sensors from video games.

Rebecka Singerer was very upset when she was told that the beer she wanted was too dark and strong. She said, "I don't want a fruit beer. Women can drink whatever they want."

Singerer, who takes care of children, joined FemAle, a group in Gothenburg that makes and sells Sweden's first beer made by women. Their beer, called "We Can Do It," is now sold in stores. The label looks like Rosie the Riveter, a famous symbol of women's strength from World War II.

Elin Carlsson, a 25-year-old car painter at a Volvo factory, started the group. She says, "We Can Do It" is not just for women but for everyone. It's about showing that women can do anything.

Big beer companies like Carlsberg tried to make special beers for women, but these did not work well. FemAle does things differently. They have tasting events only for women to help them learn about different beer flavors.

Felicia Nordström, a bartender, got tired of men saying, "What do you know about beer, sweetie?" So, she worked with FemAle and a local brewery called Ocean. In one weekend, they created the recipe, and the next weekend, they brewed 1,600 liters of beer.

Thomas Bingebo, the head brewer at Ocean, says this is their hoppier beer and not aimed just at women. Big companies often fail when they try to make beer for women, but FemAle is doing something new.

"We Can Do It" sold out quickly, and other breweries want to work with FemAle. Carlsson believes many women choose wine because they don't know much about beer.

Sweden is becoming passionate about craft beers, and traditional strong lagers are disappearing in Gothenburg. Emma Henriksson, a 22-year-old garden equipment worker, says, "All the girls are different. There is no typical woman beer lover. Anyone can do it."

Singerer thinks FemAle has found a great way to attract women to beer. She feels very proud.

Trump told a crowd of 11,000 people he wants to set the election date for next Tuesday. He has strong support from many people, which he needs to keep until March 2016 to become the Republican candidate for the November general election.

He also laughed at a disabled journalist and wrongly accused Muslim Americans of supporting the 9/11 attackers.

Trump argues that the political media exaggerates these incidents, calling 70% of them "scum." However, he refuses to take back any of his comments. Some rivals believe Trump’s supporters may eventually tire of his attacks on minorities. A poll shows his support among Republicans has dropped by 12 points, but he still leads with 31%.

Former rival Bobby Jindal described Trump as an egomaniac and narcissist who does not fit into traditional political categories. Trump’s opposition to immigration reform, free trade deals, and President Obama’s national security policy aligns with key election issues. Polls this early in the election process can be wrong since most people haven't decided how to vote yet. Current polls show Trump has 25-30% of the Republican vote. Changing Trump’s supporters’ minds will be difficult. About 20-30% of voters say they definitely won’t support Trump.

Republican pollster Frank Luntz believes Trump appeals to voters who feel unheard and appreciate his outspokenness. Supporters like how Trump speaks his mind and isn’t afraid of anyone or anything.

A long time ago, in 1977, people went to see a movie in a galaxy far, far away. In 2015, the Star Wars movies are still very popular. There are plans for a seventh movie, and new films about Han Solo and Darth Vader are coming.

Paul Dergarabedian, a media expert, says fans eagerly wait for new posters, trailers, and information. He believes no other movie series can create such excitement.

Episode VIII is set for 2017, and another spin-off, "Rogue One," will be in theaters in 2016.

"Rogue One" will tell the story of a rebel mission to steal the Death Star plans. There's a rumor that Darth Vader might appear in "Rogue One," showing how much people love the original Star Wars.

Disney is using smart marketing to build excitement for the new films. They made all six original Star Wars movies available on streaming services. This helps remind fans why they love Star Wars.

Rosser thinks movie studios want to keep making good films and get people to go to the cinema instead of watching at home. Dergarabedian predicts "The Force Awakens" will open with record sales in December 2015 and make at least a billion dollars worldwide. Star Wars is a very strong movie brand.

James Hamblin, a senior editor at The Atlantic, tried an experiment where he stopped showering as often and didn't use shampoo or soap. He found out that cleaning too much can make your skin work harder to stay balanced, leading you to clean even more. When you shower, you remove oils and good bacteria from your skin. This can make your skin feel tight and dry. It also can lead to more bad bacteria growing, which might make you smell more.

At first, not showering can seem unpleasant, but eventually, your skin adjusts and becomes healthier. Using less soap can help with skin problems like eczema. Showering less also saves water and helps the environment. An average shower uses 65 liters of water, which is a lot of clean water going down the drain.

In places like California, where there isn't enough water, saving water is very important. Using fewer shower products also means less plastic waste.

If you're worried about smelling bad, you can still use deodorant if needed. Washing your hands with soap is still important to avoid spreading germs.

You don't have to stop showering completely, but you can skip a few showers and use less soap to help your skin and the environment.

You don't have to stop showering, but you can take shorter showers and use less soap. This helps your skin and the planet.

Moses King, 48, has been living with HIV in Liberia. He can handle the stigma and get medicine, but he and his six kids cannot afford enough food, especially meat and fish, which are costly but needed for protein.

Pate K Chon, a counselor for HIV patients, came up with an idea after seeing a fish farm in Thailand. She wanted to start a fish farm in Liberia to give HIV patients jobs and protein-rich food.

Chon started building a fish farm pool. In 2012, she met John Sheehy, who helped raise money and learn how to run a fish farm. Now, the Grow2Feed Liberia Fish Farm has 12 tanks, each holding 5,000 fish. This provides up to 200,000 fish a year for 1,200 HIV-positive people, including King's family.

The farm also uses fish waste to grow crops, giving food and income to the community. People living nearby work at the farm and get fish to eat and sell.

In Liberia, 1.5% of the population has HIV, mostly women and girls. Many face stigma and don't get treatment. Good nutrition is vital for HIV patients because they need more protein to stay healthy. Without food, the medicine can make them sick.

Paul White, who owns a fish farm in Ivory Coast, says fish farming is possible in Africa. Most fish sold in Africa is imported from China and is low quality. He believes more investment in local fish farming can change this.

Critics worry about inbreeding and toxins in farmed fish, but Sheehy says they use local fish and keep the water clean. He plans to open more fish farms in Liberia and other places.

For 85 years, Pluto was just a grey spot on classroom maps of the solar system. But on July 15, it was seen in high detail for the first time. The pictures show big mountains made of solid water ice, as big as the Alps or the Rockies.

These amazing pictures of Pluto and its large moon, Charon, came from the New Horizons spacecraft, 4 billion miles away. The mission took almost ten years.

Alan Stern, the main scientist for the mission, said New Horizons is giving amazing results. The data looks great, and Pluto and Charon are incredible.

A big surprise was finding mountains in the Kuiper Belt, where Pluto is. John Spencer, another scientist, said these mountains are about 3,000 meters high and spread over hundreds of miles.

One side of Pluto showed no craters, meaning there has been recent geological activity, possibly including geysers of ice or volcanoes that erupt ice.

Pluto used to be the ninth planet but is now called a dwarf planet. At a NASA meeting, Dwayne Brown, a NASA spokesperson, said they turned a blurry dot into clear images.

Stern said there will be more images and more to learn about Pluto in the coming year. The mountains seem to be made of water ice with a thin layer of methane and nitrogen.

Water ice is strong enough to form big mountains. The mountains on Pluto are likely less than 100 million years old, which is very young compared to the 4.56 billion-year-old solar system. This suggests the area might still be geologically active.

The images are so detailed that if the spacecraft flew over London, it could see the runways at Heathrow airport.

It takes hours for New Horizons to send back a picture because of the 5 billion kilometers distance. All the data will take 16 months to send back. The heart-shaped area on Pluto will now be called Tombaugh Regio, named after Clyde Tombaugh, who discovered Pluto in 1930.

Charon's new image shows cliffs stretching about 1,000 kilometers, suggesting cracks in its surface due to geological activity. There is also a canyon about 7 to 9 kilometers deep.

Cathy Olkin, a mission scientist, said seeing Charon was exciting. The team is very excited about the science in this one image.

Scientists think Pluto is mostly rock covered by ice, with surface temperatures around -230°C. The mission will continue into the Kuiper Belt, helping us understand the ancient solar system and planet formation.

In August 2015, scientists will pick which of two objects to visit next. NASA says the spacecraft can record and send data until the mid-2030s, when its power source will run out.

New Horizons also looked at Pluto’s other moons: Nix, Hydra, Styx, and Kerberos. John Grunsfeld, from NASA, said New Horizons shows how important basic scientific research is.

The images suggest Hydra’s surface is probably covered with water ice. Future images will give more clues about how these moons formed billions of years ago.
