Roger McKinlay, a former president of the Royal Institute of Navigation, thinks that using GPS too much might hurt our natural ability to find our way. He warns that if we don’t practice our navigation skills, they will get worse as we depend more on technology.

McKinlay says we need to invest a lot in navigation systems before self-driving cars can be trusted. Until then, he suggests doing more research on navigation methods and teaching kids how to navigate traditionally. He believes schools should teach navigation and map reading as important life skills.

In 2015, about 66% of adults in the UK owned smartphones, compared to 39% in 2012. McKinlay, who works with satellite communications, advises being careful not to rely solely on devices for navigation. He says if we don't use our navigation skills, we'll lose them.

A 2009 study by neuroscientist Dr. Hugo Spiers found that retired London taxi drivers did worse on navigation tests than working drivers. This shows that if you don’t use your navigation skills, you lose them.

Spiers agrees that relying on GPS can be risky. He mentions a case where a driver’s car fell into a lake because of incorrect GPS directions. Spiers says while the dangers of not using your brain for navigation are unknown, there is a real risk in depending on GPS.

Spiers adds that how we use navigational technology matters. Audio instructions from GPS can reduce the need to think about navigation, but using digital maps on smartphones requires more thought and interaction.

McKinlay believes that navigation technology must improve significantly before we can trust driverless cars and smart cities. He says GPS isn’t reliable enough for critical tasks like landing airplanes.

Spiers thinks artificial intelligence could bring new navigation tools, but McKinlay doubts this. He believes smarter machines will only be good at specific tasks until they can understand human thoughts and goals.

McKinlay stresses that it's crucial for humans to keep control over navigation. He asks if we really want people to be helpless when GPS fails or runs out of power. He reminds us that technology is just a tool, not magic.

We asked five people with unusual jobs about their pay, the bad parts, and what they like about their work.

1. Dog-food taster
The job: Tasting dog food to make sure it's good.
What it involves: Opening cans of dog food, smelling it, and eating it. This checks if the ingredients are balanced well.
Pay: Entry-level jobs pay about 20,000. Experienced workers can earn 50,000 or more.
Worst part: Meeting deadlines. Some pet foods smell bad.
Job satisfaction: Every day is different. Helping pets be happy and healthy feels good.

2. Hygiene technician
The job: Cleaning places that might be dangerous.
What it involves: Cleaning crime scenes, accidents, and very dirty houses.
Pay: Entry-level jobs pay around 14,500. Top salaries can be up to 22,000.
Worst part: Cleaning after suicides. It can be emotionally hard.
Job satisfaction: The job is varied and helps keep people safe.

3. Biogas engineer
The job: Setting up systems in poor countries to make gas from waste.
What it involves: Building systems that use waste to make gas for cooking and lighting.
Pay: Entry-level jobs pay around 10,000. Chief technical officers can earn 30,000.
Worst part: Seeing people struggle. The work can be dirty and smelly.
Job satisfaction: Helping people earn more money and improving community health.

4. Eel ecologist
The job: Protecting endangered eels.
What it involves: Catching eels in rivers to measure and weigh them.
Pay: Not mentioned.
Worst part: Eels are hard to catch. Learning about environmental damage is sad.
Job satisfaction: Working outside and seeing wildlife. Helping eels and the environment.

5. Shopping channel presenter
The job: Selling products on live TV.
What it involves: Talking about products and showing how they work.
Pay: Trainees start at 30,000. Experienced presenters can earn over 55,000.
Worst part: Working odd hours, including weekends and late nights.
Job satisfaction: Enjoying the excitement of live TV and getting viewers to buy products.

A car with a top speed of 25 mph, two seats, and no pedals or steering wheel may seem unusual. However, Google's new driverless car surprised the car and taxi industries. This electric car, being tested near Google's office in California, doesn't have any usual controls like foot pedals. Instead, it uses a smartphone app to pick up passengers and tell it where to go. There’s also a single STOP button between the two seats for emergencies.

The car handles all driving tasks such as navigating, steering, accelerating, and braking.

Google is making about 100 models for a two-year test. Sergey Brin, one of Google's founders, said the project aims to help people who don’t have easy access to transportation. He described riding in the car as relaxing and enjoyable.

Google states that the goal is to improve safety. The car is made with foam at the front and a plastic windshield to protect pedestrians better.

These cars were made by an unnamed company in Detroit. They will be used to figure out how to make driverless cars work well. Google plans to run a pilot program with these cars, which are not yet for sale.

One problem is that the cars need detailed maps of the roads before they can drive on them. Right now, only about 2,000 miles of California's roads have these maps, while the state has over 170,000 miles of public roads.

Google hopes to license this technology to car makers once it is improved. However, the idea of driverless cars replacing human-driven taxis worries some people. Dennis Conyon from the UK National Taxi Association fears that many taxi drivers could lose their jobs. In London alone, there are about 22,000 licensed black cabs, and Conyon estimates that around 100,000 people drive taxis for hire in the UK.

Other car companies like Volvo, Ford, and Mercedes are working on cars that assist drivers but still have controls. Chris Urmson, who leads Google's self-driving car project, explained that removing the steering wheel and brakes makes it easier for passengers to handle emergencies.

Urmson added that these cars will be simple but will take passengers where they want to go with just the push of a button. This is a big step toward safer roads and better transportation for many people.

Google's self-driving cars have driven 700,000 miles without causing any accidents. The company notes that thousands of people die on the roads each year, and about 80% of crashes are due to human mistakes.

Valdevaqueros is one of the last untouched beaches in southern Spain. Right now, the beach has a road full of camper vans from Germany, France, Italy, and Britain. These vans bring windsurfers and kitesurfers because of the strong winds in the area.

For years, it has been different from the concrete-lined beaches of Torremolinos and Marbella. However, in early 2012, the local council in Tarifa agreed to build a tourist complex near the beach. Environmental and conservation groups worry that the project will hurt the habitats of protected species. But for the council, the main issue is jobs. Tarifa has 18,000 people, and 2,600 are unemployed due to Spain's worst economic crisis in at least half a century.

Traditional jobs like fishing are disappearing, so tourism is seen as the only solution, but it must be sustainable. Sebastin Galindo, a councillor from the Socialist party, which opposes the project, says the complex meets environmental standards. There is a law to prevent ugly developments like those that ruined many Spanish beaches in the 1960s and 1970s. This law requires the complex to be at least 200 meters from the coast; it will actually be 800 meters away.

Opponents argue that more housing isn't needed since Spain already has a million empty homes. The Socialist opposition in Madrid criticized the idea, saying it discriminates against migrant workers who came to Spain during the boom years, many from Morocco, which is just 14 kilometers away and visible from Tarifa.

Surfers fear that new buildings will weaken the strong local winds and won't attract traditional package holidaymakers. "It’s not really a family spot," said Henning Mayer, who visits from Germany every year. "Just wait until they see what the wind is like." Ten years ago, they planned a new highway here, but it didn’t happen, so he thinks building new hotels will be impossible.

Tarifa is the southernmost point of Spain, where Africa and Europe meet, and where the Mediterranean Sea meets the Atlantic. Campaigners say it is important for migrating animals.

The campaign to save the beach started right after the Tarifa council approved the project. The campaign has a Facebook page and support from groups like Greenpeace, the World Wide Fund for Nature, and Birdlife Spain. The Andalusian College of Geographers also opposes the project, saying it will disturb two wildlife conservation areas and cross the border of a national park.

Ral Romeva, a member of the European Parliament, said money is more important than urban laws and European environmental rules. He also noted that the site lacks water, which is already scarce in Tarifa during hot summers.

Many locals wonder why a resort should be built 10 kilometers away instead of on unused land near Tarifa's historic center, known for its white walls and narrow streets, dominated by a 10th-century Moorish castle. Cristbal Lobato, who has worked at a beachside bar in Tarifa for 30 years, agrees with the complex if it creates jobs in the town, but opposes it if it only benefits a few. "If they put it in the center of Tarifa, where there is space, then clients could visit shops, tapas bars, and restaurants."

Biologist Aitor Galn, overlooking the green fields where the resort will be built, said, "Anywhere else in Europe, this place would have the utmost protection, but here they want to get rid of it all and cover it with buildings. They want to turn this into Benidorm, but what attracts people here is wildlife and the wind. By taking advantage of the current crisis and unemployment, builders and mayors can justify any amount of destruction."

Scientists made a map of the brain that shows where words and their meanings are found. The map uses colors like a rainbow to group words and their meanings in parts of the brain.

Jack Gallant, a scientist at the University of California, Berkeley, said their aim was to make a big map showing how the brain understands the meanings of words.

Words and ideas don't live in just one spot in the brain. One spot can be linked to many related words. Each word also lights up many spots in the brain. These spots work together to show the meaning of each word we use, like "life" and "love," "death" and "taxes."

One researcher not involved in the study called the map a big success. The map shows how new ways of looking inside the brain can help us understand how it works on important tasks. If scientists keep improving, this technology could greatly affect medicine and other fields.

Alexander Huth, the main writer of the study, said this method might be able to figure out which words a person is hearing, reading, or thinking. This could help people who can't talk due to illness communicate using a computer.

To make the map, scientists watched people's brain activity while they listened to stories. They then matched the words in the stories to the brain activity to see how groups of related words affected around 50,000 to 80,000 small spots all over the brain.

Huth used short, exciting stories to keep the listeners focused. Seven people listened to two hours of stories each, totaling about 25,000 words and more than 3,000 different words.

The map shows that related words light up the same brain areas. For example, the word "victim" and related words like "killed," "convicted," "murdered," and "confessed" light up a spot on the left side of the brain, above the ear. Words like "wife," "husband," "children," and "parents" light up a spot on the right side of the brain, near the top of the head.

Each word has more than one spot because words often have multiple meanings. The word "top" lights up spots that respond to clothing, numbers, measurements, buildings, and places.

The scientists made a website where people can look at the brain map. The maps were similar for all seven people in the experiment, suggesting that their brains organize word meanings in the same way. However, the study only included five men and two women who all speak English natively. People from different backgrounds and cultures may have different brain maps.

With this map, researchers can now understand how the brain handles different ideas, from numbers to murder and religion. Murder is represented a lot in the brain, according to Gallant.

Uri Hasson, a scientist at Princeton University, said the work was excellent. He noted that many studies only look at brain activity for single words or sentences, but Gallant's team showed how the brain works in real-life situations. Hasson thinks the next step is to make a more detailed map. He believes it will be possible to guess the words a person is thinking based on their brain activity in the future, though this raises big ethical questions.

Lorraine Tyler, a scientist at Cambridge University, said the research was a big success. However, the current map doesn't show small differences in word meanings. There is still much to learn about how the brain understands words.

A Canadian man named Jordan Axani became famous because he offered a free trip around the world to a woman with the same name as his ex-girlfriend. He chose Elizabeth Quinn Gallagher, a 23-year-old student from Nova Scotia. They traveled together for three weeks but did not fall in love. Jordan is 28 years old and lives in Toronto. He runs a charity called A Ticket Forward.

Jordan had bought tickets for a trip with his girlfriend, but they broke up and he could not change the name on the tickets. So, he decided to give the trip to someone else with the same name. Elizabeth Gallagher, who goes by Quinn, answered his online post and was picked to go on the trip. Before leaving, Quinn mentioned she already had a serious boyfriend.

When they came back to Canada, Jordan said, "This was never meant to be romantic. Quinn is like my little sister." He added that it took about a week for them to get used to each other and become close friends. They visited places like Milan, Venice, Vienna, Prague, Khao Lak in Thailand, and Hong Kong. Their favorite place was Prague, where they met many people.

Jordan said the trip was fun and they learned a lot about themselves. People followed them on social media and even recognized them in Hong Kong. After returning at 3 am, Jordan went straight to a meeting at his charity. His goal is to help survivors of abuse, cancer, and war by giving them free trips around the world.

Jordan is also talking to some production companies about turning his story into a TV show or movie. For now, he is not looking for a new girlfriend but says life will take its course.

American researchers found that a nasal spray with oxytocin, known as the love hormone, might help children with autism act more normally in social situations. Oxytocin improved how the brains of autistic children responded to facial expressions, making social interactions feel more natural and rewarding.

Kevin Pelphrey from Yale University says oxytocin could make behavioral therapies more effective. These therapies help people with autism deal with social situations better. With oxytocin, children might show more interest in talking and looking at others.

Autism affects more than one in 100 people. It makes social interaction and communication hard. There is no current treatment for the social problems caused by autism.

Yale researchers studied oxytocin because it helps with bonding and trust. However, results have been mixed. One study found no big improvement when young people took oxytocin for several days. Pelphrey thinks oxytocin might help the brain learn from social interactions, especially when used with therapies that encourage social interaction.

In the study, 17 young people aged eight to 16 with autism had their brains scanned while looking at pictures of cars or people's eyes showing different emotions. They either got a placebo or oxytocin through a nasal spray. The scans showed that after taking oxytocin, the reward parts of their brains worked more normally when looking at faces and less when looking at cars.

Pelphrey warns it is too early to use oxytocin as a treatment and advises against buying it online. More research is needed before it can be considered a treatment.

Simon Baron-Cohen from Cambridge University says the study shows changes in brain activity in key areas. However, oxytocin did not improve performance in recognizing social cues. It is unclear if oxytocin has any side effects or if it only helps people with autism. Oxytocin's effects last only about 45 minutes, which could make it hard to use as a treatment.

Doctors need more research to understand the benefits and risks of oxytocin. Uta Frith from University College London notes that while oxytocin made faces more interesting in brain scans, it did not change behavior. Showing an effect on behavior is crucial for the treatment to be useful.

American scientists think a special nose spray with a chemical called oxytocin can help kids with autism act more normally around others. Oxytocin is sometimes called the "love hormone" because it helps people bond and trust each other. The scientists found that when autistic kids used the spray, their brains reacted better to seeing faces. This could make it easier for them to talk and play with others.

Kevin Pelphrey from Yale University says oxytocin might work well with other autism treatments. He thinks it could help autistic people want to talk more and look at others' faces.

Autism is a condition that makes it hard for people to talk and play with others. About one in every 100 people has autism. There is no good way to fix the social problems autism causes right now.

The scientists studied 17 kids with autism between ages 8 and 16. Some got oxytocin, and some got a fake spray. Then, the scientists looked at their brains while they looked at pictures of cars and people's eyes. The kids who got oxytocin had more normal brain activity when they saw faces.

Pelphrey says it's too early to use oxytocin as a treatment. People should not buy oxytocin online or try it at home. More research is needed to see if oxytocin really works and if it is safe.

Some experts are excited but say we need to know more. Uta Frith says we need to see if oxytocin changes how people with autism act, not just how their brains work.

Cathal Redmond was swimming near Greece and took photos of colorful fish with his new underwater camera. Later, he found the photos were brown and unclear. He thought he needed more time to take better pictures underwater.

So, he invented the Express Dive, a refillable air storage device that fits in the mouth. It lets people swim underwater for two minutes. This is between snorkeling, which has limits, and scuba diving, which needs heavy and costly equipment. His invention looks like a mix of a scuba mouthpiece and a water bottle.

Redmond, aged 27, wanted to help people stay underwater longer than the usual 30 seconds of holding breath. In 2006, he took a scuba diving course and enjoyed breathing underwater to see fish. However, he did not like carrying 50 kg of equipment.

Scuba diving requires planning because of the heavy gear. You cannot suddenly decide to dive while walking on the beach.

During his final year of product design studies, Redmond created the Express Dive. It has two parts. Above water, it sucks in air through a mouthpiece vent, compresses it, and stores it in a tank. A green flashing light shows when it's full. As you dive, air comes back through the mouthpiece. The light turns red when air runs low. It takes two minutes to fill and provides two minutes of air.

Redmond made the device small enough to fit in the mouth. It feels like using a snorkel and extends the body’s ability to store air. Parts of the prototype have been tested, but not fully submerged for two minutes. With more testing, he believes he can create a safe device. It might cost €280 and weigh between 1 kg and 3 kg.

For those who think two minutes is not much, Redmond says the average swimmer can only hold their breath for about 40 seconds underwater. Two minutes is a big improvement.

Some people might think two minutes is not much better than snorkeling. But Redmond says most people can only hold their breath for about 40 seconds. Two minutes is much longer than that.

On an average day, Starbucks stores host many activities like business meetings and reading groups. Many people visit for their morning coffee. However, Starbucks faces some problems.

UK Uncut, a group that takes direct action, plans to turn many Starbucks stores in the UK into temporary child care centers, shelters, and places for homeless people. This is to show that Starbucks does not pay enough taxes in the UK.

This happened while Starbucks was being questioned by the House of Commons Public Accounts Committee. The committee asked why Starbucks did not pay any corporation tax in the UK for the past three years, even though the company made a lot of money there.

Troy Alstead, Starbucks' Chief Financial Officer, will try to fix the company's image when he meets the committee.

Some Members of Parliament (MPs) say the UK's tax department, HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC), has close relationships with big businesses. Conservative MP Richard Bacon said this relationship "smells bad."

UK Uncut wants to connect government spending cuts, especially those affecting women, with big businesses not paying enough taxes. Sarah Greene, an activist, says that without proper tax payments, services like shelters and rape crisis centers will lose funding. HMRC estimates that £32 billion was lost due to tax avoidance in 2011.

Greene believes the government could collect billions more if they were stricter on tax avoidance. UK Uncut chose Starbucks because an investigation found that the company paid only £8.6 million in corporation tax since 1998, despite making £3 billion in sales.

Anna Walker, another UK Uncut campaigner, said they want to highlight how cuts affect women and transform Starbucks into services like shelters and child care centers that the government is cutting.

Starbucks is a good target because it is on almost every street in the UK, allowing people to protest locally.

Other international companies like Amazon, eBay, Facebook, Google, and IKEA also pay little or no corporation tax in the UK.

Starbucks claims it pays the right amount of taxes. Howard Schultz, the group CEO, stated that Starbucks has always paid taxes in the UK. Over the last three years, the company paid more than £160 million in various taxes, including National Insurance, VAT, and business rates.

Margaret Hodge, who leads the Public Accounts Committee, said that Apple, eBay, Facebook, Google, and Starbucks avoided nearly £900 million in taxes. Prime Minister David Cameron responded by saying he is unhappy with the current situation and that HMRC needs to look at it carefully.

A Starbucks spokesperson said the company follows tax laws and accounting rules in all 61 countries where it operates, including the UK. They posted information about their tax practices on their website.

Starbucks spends hundreds of millions of pounds with local suppliers on items like milk, cakes, and sandwiches, and on store design and renovations. The company's total economic impact in the UK is more than £80 million a year.

The group UK Uncut wants to turn Starbucks cafés into places for kids, safe homes, and shelters for people without homes. They want people to know that Starbucks does not pay enough taxes.

The House of Commons asked Starbucks why they did not pay any taxes in the UK for the last three years.

UK Uncut thinks there is a link between the government cutting money and big companies not paying enough taxes. This affects women a lot.

Sarah Greene from UK Uncut said that if companies paid more taxes, there would be more money for safe homes. In 2011, the government lost about £32 billion because some big companies did not pay enough taxes.

Greene also said the government could get billions of pounds if they made sure companies paid the right amount of taxes.

An investigation showed that Starbucks paid only £8.6 million in taxes since 1998 even though they sold things worth £3 billion in the UK.

Anna Walker from UK Uncut said they chose to focus on Starbucks because it is easy for people to find them on most streets. They want to change Starbucks into the services the government is cutting, like safe homes and places for kids.

Starbucks says they pay the right amount of taxes. Howard Schultz, the group's CEO, said Starbucks has always paid taxes in the UK. Over the last three years, they paid more than £160 million in different kinds of taxes.

Apple, eBay, Facebook, Google, and Starbucks together avoided nearly £900 million in taxes. David Cameron, the Prime Minister, said he was not happy with this. He thinks these businesses should pay fair taxes while still being encouraged to invest in the UK.

A person speaking for Starbucks said tax laws are very complicated, but Starbucks follows the tax laws. Starbucks spends lots of money on local food and store designs. They say their work helps the UK economy by more than £80 million each year.

The High Court in London decided that three old Kenyans who were held and hurt during the Mau Mau rebellion can sue the British government. This might lead to many other people suing, saying they were mistreated when Britain controlled Kenya.

The British government argued that too much time had passed since the 1950s rebellion to have a fair trial, but the court disagreed. In 2011, the same judge said the Kenyans should not sue the Kenyan government, even though Kenya took over Britain's legal duties in 1963.

Human rights groups in Kenya think more than 5,000 of the 70,000 people held by British authorities are still alive and might sue. This ruling could help others around the world who were hurt during British rule.

The Foreign Office said the ruling could cause big legal issues and planned to appeal. Normally, you must sue within three to six years, but here, the time limit was extended to over 50 years, even though key people are dead and cannot explain what happened.

Paulo Muoka Nzili, 85, Wambugu Wa Nyingi, 84, and Jane Muthoni Mara, 73, won after a three-year fight. Their lawyers said they faced terrible violence. In Nairobi, Nyingi and Mara learned the news by phone and celebrated with their supporters.

Nyingi, who was held for nine years and still has scars, said he wanted the truth known and for people to be paid so they can forgive. Mara said she was happy and would tell her children she won.

In 2011, the judge found enough proof of systematic torture. He said a fair trial was possible, noting that thousands of secret files from the colonial era were found in 2011.

British lawyers admitted the three Kenyans were tortured but tried to avoid legal responsibility. Lawyers think this ruling will encourage others from places like Malaya, Yemen, Cyprus, and Palestine to sue.

Veterans from the 1950s Cyprus rebellion are watching the case. They could use British documents and Red Cross files, which are open after 40 years. The Red Cross recorded many torture cases in Cyprus.

People in Malaysia and Aden may also sue. In Malaysia, relatives of 24 workers killed by British troops are seeking a public inquiry. Former prisoners in Aden, now part of Yemen, might also sue, but British lawyers may find it hard to reach them.

A British court said three old Kenyans can sue the British government. These Kenyans were put in jail and hurt during fights in Kenya in the 1950s. Many others might also try to sue.

The British government said it was too late to have a fair trial because the fight ended many years ago. The court did not agree. In 2011, the government told the Kenyans to sue the Kenyan government instead, but the judge did not agree with that either.

About 70,000 people were put in jail by the British in Kenya. More than 5,000 of them are still alive today. They might also sue the British government. This court decision might help other people around the world who want to sue.

The Foreign Office said they would appeal the decision. They think it is too late to sue because the people who made the decisions are dead.

Paulo Muoka Nzili, 85, Wambugu Wa Nyingi, 84, and Jane Muthoni Mara, 73, won their case after three years. Their lawyers said they were badly hurt. When Nyingi and Mara heard the news on their phones, they were very happy and danced.

The judge in 2011 said there was proof that prisoners were maybe tortured. He thought a fair trial was possible because secret documents from that time were found in 2011.

The British government said these three Kenyans were tortured but did not want to take legal responsibility. Lawyers think this case will interest people from other places like Malaya, Yemen, Cyprus, and Palestine who were also hurt.

People who fought in Cyprus in the 1950s are interested in this case. They might use British documents and Red Cross documents to prove they were tortured.

In Malaysia, many people were put in jail during a war that started in 1948. Twenty-four farm workers without weapons were killed by British troops. Their families want a public inquiry. Ex-prisoners from Aden might also sue, but it could be hard to find them because Aden is now part of Yemen.

Sleep used to be seen as something for lazy people. But now, Arianna Huffington's book "The Sleep Revolution" is very popular. It says that good sleep can change your life.

Businesses are making money by helping people sleep better. Hotels offer sleep retreats for over $1,000. You can buy devices like a sleep-monitoring mattress cover for $249 or a brainwave-tracking sleep mask for $299.

Companies are adding nap rooms, and Huffington thinks they will be as common as conference rooms soon. People now see good sleep as part of a healthy lifestyle, like buying expensive juices or fitness classes.

Huffington says sleep helps you perform better. She gets eight hours of sleep each night, thanks to her team of assistants who do all her tasks. However, her assistants often struggle with low pay and long hours, so they don't get enough sleep.

Poor people and those working odd hours often have trouble sleeping well. Studies show that African Americans sleep less and worse than white people, partly because of stress from racism. Rich white women tend to sleep the best.

While Huffington talks about a sleep revolution, the real issue is that many people can't afford to prioritize sleep. Some researchers are trying to find ways to reduce the need for sleep, especially in the military. If soldiers could perform well with just a few hours of sleep, it could greatly reduce casualties.

In the future, people might not need sleep at all. Only those who can't afford new technologies might still need to sleep, making it a luxury for the poor.

Not long ago, not sleeping much showed you were busy and important. Now, Arianna Huffington's book, "The Sleep Revolution," says we should sleep more and it's a best-seller.

Businesses see money in helping people sleep better. Hotels offer "sleep retreats" for over $1,000. You can buy a sensor for your mattress for $249 or a brainwave-monitoring sleep mask for $299.

Companies are adding nap rooms like conference rooms. People now pay for healthy food and exercise, and they want good sleep too.

Huffington says sleep makes you better, not just rested. For some, good sleep is a sign of being wealthy. But many people can't sleep well because they are poor, worried, or work odd hours. Studies show white people sleep longer and better than African Americans.

Rich white women sleep the best. Huffington's book is for them. She calls it a "revolution," but really it's just a new idea for rich people. Most people can't afford to sleep enough.

Sleep helps you do better, but it takes time. The U.S. military wants to find ways for soldiers to work with less sleep. They want soldiers to sleep like giraffes, only 1.9 hours a night.

One day, people might not need to sleep at all. Only poor people will sleep a lot. We may need a new kind of sleep revolution then.

They call him the Robin Hood of the banks. Enric Duran took out many loans worth almost half a million euros without planning to pay them back. Instead, he gave the money to projects that fought against capitalism.

For 14 months, Duran hid. In an interview by Skype from a secret place, he said he is not sorry. From 2006 to 2008, Duran got 68 loans from 39 banks in Spain. He gave the money to social activists who used it for speaking tours and TV cameras for a media network. He believed these social movements needed more money to build alternatives to capitalism.

Duran tricked the banks to show how the banking system creates money out of nothing. At first, he filled out loan applications with his real details, but they were denied. He then learned how to create a complex web of accounts, payments, and transfers. Using a fake television production company, he got 492,000 euros.

In 2009, Duran was arrested in Spain by six of the 39 banks. He spent two months in prison before being released on 50,000 bail. In February 2013, facing up to eight years in prison, he fled instead of going to trial because he does not recognize the court's authority.

Duran believes his actions helped start a worldwide debate about the economic crisis. Today, many Spaniards support the anti-capitalist movement and groups like the Indignados.

Now, Duran wants to change Spain’s justice system by promoting restorative justice. He thinks some people in Spain agree with him and believe he owes nothing. He suggests sharing his knowledge about bank loans to help both the public and bank workers.

They call him the Robin Hood of the banks. He is a man named Enric Duran who borrowed almost half a million euros and did not pay it back. Instead, he gave the money to help projects that fight against capitalism.

Duran hid for 14 months. He does not feel sorry for what he did, even if he may go to jail. "I'm proud of what I've done," he said in a Skype interview from a secret place.

From 2006 to 2008, Duran borrowed money 68 times from 39 banks in Spain. He gave the money to social activists. These activists used the money to talk about why they don't like capitalism and to buy TV cameras for a media group. Duran said that social activists needed more money, but banks kept making money without doing much work.

He borrowed the money in a dishonest way to show that this was unfair. At first, he tried borrowing money with his real name, but the banks said no. Then, he learned how to trick the banks. By summer 2007, he knew how to do it. He borrowed money using a fake TV company's name. He got exactly €492,000 this way.

In 2009, Duran was caught in Spain and put in jail for two months. Then, he was let out after paying €50,000. In February 2013, he ran away because he could go to jail for up to eight years.

Because of what Duran did from 2006 to 2008, many people noticed the anti-capitalist movement for the first time. Many Spanish people were looking for other ways to live because capitalism had caused them problems.

Today, thousands of people in Spain support the anti-capitalist movement and groups like the Indignados.

Duran says he won't give the money back to the banks, but he can teach them how to help people and bank workers better. He learned a lot while borrowing the money dishonestly.

A group of experts says fake allergy tests are making many people think they need treatments they don't need. This can lead to poor diets and malnutrition. Allergies and food intolerances are becoming more common, but confusion between them and wrong diagnoses are causing real problems. The charity Sense About Science made a guide with help from allergy doctors.

Tracey Brown, the director of Sense About Science, says there are myths, misunderstood studies, and bad medical practices. This leads to too many or too few diagnoses. The costs are big—unnecessary actions for some and not enough action for those who really need it.

Experts worry that restaurants and caterers might not take proper care when serving someone with a real allergy if they think the person just has a food intolerance. Moira Austin from a charity that helps people with severe allergic reactions says there have been deaths when restaurants serve meals with ingredients that guests are allergic to.

The guide says most online and store-bought allergy tests are not based on science. One test checks for specific antibodies in the blood, but these antibodies do not show an allergy. Another test mixes acupuncture and homeopathy and measures electrical resistance through the skin. Testing hair for allergies is also useless since hair does not react to allergies.

Paul Seddon, a doctor who treats children with allergies, sees kids on overly strict diets due to unscientific tests. Adam Fox, another doctor, deals with patients who avoid many foods based on these tests. This makes it hard for children to eat normally and enjoy activities like going to parties.

Believing that a child's tiredness, headaches, or skin problems are caused by allergies can take a lot of time and tests to confirm or deny. Alternative therapists often give quick but incorrect answers.

Allergies are growing in developed countries. In the past 30 years, the percentage of children with allergic rhinitis and eczema has tripled. Many people now think allergies cause their health issues. The guide lists myths about allergy causes, such as food colorings, toxins, and fast food.

Experts say many people take extra medicines and eat bad foods because of fake allergy tests. Allergies and food problems are growing fast, but people mix up allergies and food intolerances. This causes trouble, says a group called Sense About Science. They made a guide about allergies.

"It's very confusing," said Tracey Brown from Sense About Science. "People without allergies take too many actions, while those with allergies don't get enough help."

Many people tell waiters they have allergies, but some actually have food intolerances, which aren't dangerous. Some restaurants might not be careful enough when serving people with real allergies because they hear so many false claims.

Moira Austin from an allergy group said, "It's very serious. If a restaurant thinks someone just dislikes a food, they might not be careful. People have died after eating food they were allergic to in restaurants."

The guide says most online and store-bought allergy tests don't work. One test checks blood for antibodies, but high levels don't mean an allergy. Another test mixes acupuncture and homeopathy, which also doesn't work. Testing hair for allergies is useless.

Paul Seddon, a doctor for kids with allergies, sees children on very limited diets because of fake tests. He wants to stop these tests by proving they don't work.

Allergies can make kids tired, give them headaches, and cause skin rashes. Checking for allergies takes time and many tests. Quick tests usually give wrong answers.

Allergies are growing in rich countries. Now, there are three times as many kids with certain allergies compared to 30 years ago. The guide talks about myths, like fast food or food coloring causing allergies.

It is now against the law to smoke inside a bar in New Orleans, Louisiana. Many other cities do not allow smoking indoors either, but New Orleans is special because it is known for having a fun atmosphere that attracts many visitors. An indoor smoking ban here might have different effects.

Since Hurricane Katrina hit in 2005, the city government has tried to make things quieter. They have worked with neighborhood groups to enforce stricter rules on bars and nightclubs and to pass a new noise law.

Bar owner William Walker dislikes the new anti-smoking law. He thinks it will make things worse by forcing smokers outside, which could lead to more tension.

New Orleans has many famous bars and music venues in quiet neighborhoods. This mix of lively bars and peaceful homes is part of what makes the city unique and appealing. However, some people find this arrangement unacceptable, and the future of New Orleans' musical culture feels uncertain.

Martha Wood lives near a noisy bar with live music. She bought her house partly because of the bar and won't complain about the noise. Her bar was one of the first in New Orleans to be banned from selling drinks to go due to noise issues in 2013, including complaints about loud smokers outside.

The Maple Leaf club went smoke-free in 2014, as did another club where artists demanded smoke-free nights. Zalia BeVille, manager of the All Ways Lounge, wishes the city had let this happen naturally rather than enforcing a ban everywhere.

All Ways Lounge has an outdoor patio, but Lost Love Lounge does not. Its owner, Geoff Douville, supports the ban because he previously felt forced to allow smoking to keep his bar open. Without a city-wide ban, Douville believes he couldn't have banned smoking in his bar without losing customers to nearby bars that still allowed smoking.

Many small business owners fear losing money due to the ban. Neil Timms, who owns an English pub, remembers how pubs in England closed after a similar ban in 2007. To avoid closing, he is building an outdoor patio.

Douville sees the ban as a chance to attract more customers who don't want to smell like smoke. He doesn't worry about noise complaints, saying no court will consider a bar a nuisance when the city itself requires smoking outside.

Councilwoman LaToya Cantrell, who proposed the ban, believes bar owners should ensure their customers behave respectfully outside. She argues that clean air and reduced noise are possible with better communication and cooperation between communities and businesses.

Cantrell notes that New Orleans is unique because it is known for relaxation and fun. She emphasizes the importance of protecting workers in smoky conditions, who are key to the city's economy.

There were concerns that police would not have time to enforce the ban. Instead, the health department will issue warnings and fines. Customers are encouraged to report illegal smoking by filling out a form or calling 311, including photos. Timms says he will follow the ban to avoid trouble.

Douville is not worried about noise complaints and agrees with Cantrell's positive outlook. He acknowledges that people will complain but believes they won't succeed.

A Spanish degree helped me get my first job as a journalist with an international press agency in Mexico City. However, I still made mistakes as a young reporter.

I traveled from New York to Mexico City by bus and had a job interview that tested my language skills. My work involved covering political events during the day and coordinating news about conflicts in Central America at night. Sometimes, I reported on disasters like fires, floods, and explosions.

I struggled with numbers in Spanish, just as I did in English. One time, I called a Mexican grandmother instead of the police because I misread a number. Another time, I reported incorrect death tolls, which led to criticism from my boss in Washington. He said no one had told me that death counts cannot decrease.

Numbers in different languages can be confusing due to various counting systems. For example, in German, 2:30 PM is "half of three," and 21 is "one and twenty." Some experts think there's a connection between dyscalculia, which is trouble with math, and difficulties in learning foreign languages. However, some people who find grammar hard can do well in a natural language environment.

Many fluent speakers in a second language can order food but struggle with numbers, especially over the phone. This issue followed me from Mexico to other countries and from Spanish to German and Portuguese.

Despite my problems with numbers, I once gained fame as a reporter. When the American consul in Veracruz was held hostage, I tried calling the consulate but dialed the wrong number and spoke to the gunman for 15 minutes. Though I didn't resolve the situation, my reputation as a reporter improved.

I got a Spanish degree and got a job as a journalist in Mexico City with an international news company. But, I made mistakes.

I traveled by bus from New York to Mexico City. At work, I reported on political events during the day and coordinated news about fighting in Central America at night. I also wrote about fires, floods, and explosions.

I had trouble with numbers in Spanish. One time, I woke up a grandma at 2 am because I misdialed a phone number. Another time, I changed the number of people hurt or killed in accidents. An editor in Washington called me and yelled because I lowered the number of deaths in a fire.

Numbers in different languages can be confusing. For example, in German, 2:30 PM is "half of three" and 21 is "one and twenty."

Some experts think that dyscalculia, which is trouble with math, might make it harder to learn numbers in a new language. Some people learn languages better when they live in a foreign country.

My friends said they can speak other languages well except for numbers, especially on the phone. My problems with numbers followed me to other countries and languages like German and Portuguese.

Once, I got a wrong phone number and accidentally talked to a gunman who was holding someone hostage. Even though I didn't solve the situation, my reputation as a reporter improved.

Nobody knows if the economic crisis in Greece started before shisha became popular, but everyone knows shisha is dangerous. It only costs 2 euros or less per use.

Maria, a former heroin addict, says shisha is the worst drug. It damages your body, makes you aggressive, and can make you act crazy. It’s cheap and easy to get, so many people use it.

This drug crisis is making things harder for Athens’ health services, which already have less money due to budget cuts.

Shisha is the preferred drug for many homeless Greeks who are poor and hopeless. It’s similar to crystal meth and often mixed with harmful substances like battery acid, engine oil, and shampoo. Users can become violent and may not understand their actions. Many users have died.

Konstantinos, another drug addict, says shisha makes you want to kill and can spread quickly.

Charalampos Poulopoulos, the head of Kethea, Greece’s anti-drug center, calls shisha an “austerity drug.” Dealers make it for people who can’t afford expensive drugs like heroin or cocaine.

Shisha can be sniffed or injected and is easy to make at home. It’s very dangerous.

In Greece, six years of recession have caused depression, drug and alcohol abuse, and crime to rise. Austerity measures have cut Greek incomes by 40%, leading to more prostitution to pay for drugs.

Eleni Marini, a psychologist, says many women agree to unsafe sex to earn more money. Shisha increases sexual desire but impairs clear thinking, leading to more pregnancies among drug-addicted prostitutes. In 2012, two sex workers gave birth on the streets of Athens.

Suicides and HIV infections are increasing. Drug addicts, estimated at 25,000, are becoming more self-destructive. Young Greeks, with high unemployment rates, are leading this trend.

Poulopoulos says the crisis has created a sense of hopelessness. People who might have stopped using drugs now see no reason to quit. In Athens, where the crisis is worst, shisha is part of this problem.

Kethea, a state-funded organization, has had its budget cut by a third. Since 2009, Kethea has lost 70 out of 500 staff members. Studies show that for every euro spent on anti-drug programs, the Greek government saves about 6 euros in criminal justice and healthcare costs. Poulopoulos says these cuts are a big mistake.

On the streets of Athens, where shisha is becoming more popular, people fear that austerity measures are not just failing but causing deaths.

Nobody knows if the money problems in Greece started first or the drug called shisha. But everyone agrees shisha is very bad. It only costs €2 or less.

Maria, who used to take another drug, says shisha is the worst. It hurts inside, makes people angry, and crazy. But it is cheap and easy to find, so many people use it.

This drug problem is hard for doctors in Athens. They have less money too.

Many poor Greeks who live on the streets use shisha. This drug is like crystal meth. It is mixed with bad things like battery acid, oil, and shampoo. It can make people violent. It is easy to buy and make.

Konstantinos, a drug user, says shisha makes people want to hurt others. Some users have died.

Charalampos Poulopoulos, who works at a place that helps with drugs, says shisha is a "poverty drug." Dealers make it for people who cannot afford other drugs like heroin and cocaine anymore.

Shisha is very dangerous. You can sniff or inject it, and you can make it at home without knowing much.

There is a lot of sadness and drug use in Greece. Crime has gone up because people earn less money. More people are selling their bodies to get money for drugs.
